# Agent Memory â€” Phorma Agent Studio

Global repo memory for AI agents working on this codebase. **Read this at the start of every session** (after [agent.md](../agent.md)). **Append to it after completing a feature** if you learned something a future agent should know: gotchas, repeated tasks, verified practices, dead ends. Keep entries terse â€” dated bullets under a topic heading. Prune entries that become wrong or obsolete.

---

## Tauri / Desktop Shell

- 2026-08-17 â€” `bundle.resources` in `tauri.conf.json` MUST be the object (map) form for paths outside `src-tauri`: the array form rewrites `../..` into `_up_/_up_` folders and the destination layout is load-bearing. Map form supports a directory key (`"../../cloud/src/": "deploy/cloud/src/"`), which preserves nested structure. Verified WITHOUT a release build: `cargo check` runs `tauri_build`, which copies resources into `backend/src-tauri/target/debug/`, so inspect that tree for the real layout. 15 entries, ~3.3MB. `deploy/{engine,cloud,cloud-aws}` as siblings is required twice over: both packages declare `@phorma/engine` as `file:../engine`, and `cloud-aws`'s CDK app walks four segments up from `src/infra/stack.ts` for its Docker build context, landing on `deploy/`.
- 2026-08-17 â€” `cargo test` had NEVER run in CI even though `sql.rs`, `llm.rs` and `data.rs` carry unit tests. It does now, alongside `cargo check --locked`. `deploy_assets.rs`'s tests cover the copy: nested structure, `node_modules`/`cdk.out`/`dist` left alone, and replacing a read-only previous copy (resources in a signed app bundle can be read-only, so `fs::copy` over one fails - remove then copy).
- 2026-07-03 â€” `"dragDropEnabled": false` on the window in `backend/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` is REQUIRED for HTML5 drag-and-drop (palette â†’ canvas) to work in the desktop app. Tauri defaults it to `true`, which hands drops to the OS file-drop handler; `dragover`/`drop` never reach the DOM. Works in browser, silently broken in Tauri. Needs app restart to take effect.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Killing a spawned process on Windows: `child.kill()` only kills the `npm.cmd` wrapper, not the node child â†’ orphan keeps the port. Use `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` (kill whole tree). Also kill any prior run before starting a new one.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Spawn long-running dev processes with env `CI=true` so CLIs fail fast instead of prompting interactively (the console is output-only).
- 2026-07-03 â€” Strip ANSI escape codes BOTH in Rust (output reader threads) and in the frontend console service, or artifacts like `[33mâ¯[39m` leak into the console.
- 2026-07-03 â€” AS's own dev server runs on port **7322** (`tauri.conf.json` beforeDevCommand/devUrl). Phorma Code uses 7321; don't collide.
- 2026-07-07 â€” Updater + process plugins: `tauri-plugin-updater` and `tauri-plugin-process` added to Cargo.toml, registered in `lib.rs` via `.plugin(tauri_plugin_updater::Builder::new().build())` and `.plugin(tauri_plugin_process::init())`. Capabilities need `updater:default` + `process:allow-restart`. `tauri.conf.json` needs `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts: true` + `plugins.updater` block with `pubkey` + `endpoints`. Updater signing keypair generated via `tauri signer generate` - private key at `backend/src-tauri/.tauri/updater.key` (gitignored, NEVER commit), public key in `tauri.conf.json`. CI uses `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` + `_PASSWORD` secrets.
- 2026-07-07 â€” `@tauri-apps/plugin-updater` JS API (CORRECTED 2026-07-14 against installed 2.10.1 d.ts): `check()` returns an update object or null. `update.download(onEvent)` and `update.downloadAndInstall(onEvent)` BOTH take an optional progress callback with `{event:'Started',data:{contentLength}}` / `{event:'Progress',data:{chunkLength}}` / `{event:'Finished'}` payloads (accumulate chunkLength yourself). The earlier note claiming "no callback + listen('tauri://update-download-progress')" was WRONG. Then `relaunch()` from `@tauri-apps/plugin-process` (on Windows `install()` exits the app itself; relaunch is for macOS/Linux).
- 2026-07-07 â€” `reqwest` in `backend/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` needs the `json` feature for `.json()` on Response/RequestBuilder. Without it, `.json()` method doesn't exist and cascading type errors about `[u8]` not being `Sized` appear on `bytes_stream()` iteration (misleading - the real cause is the missing feature).
- 2026-07-07 â€” `Cargo.toml` has `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. Do NOT use `unsafe` blocks in Rust code - use safe crates like `sysinfo` for disk-space queries instead of FFI (`GetDiskFreeSpaceExW` / `statvfs`).
- 2026-07-07 â€” Streaming pattern for new Rust commands: copy `llm.rs`'s emit pattern - `tauri::Emitter` global event with `{requestId, kind, data?}` payload, cancellation via `tokio::sync::watch` channel stored in a `Mutex<Option<HashMap>>`. For `bytes_stream()` iteration, use flat `match` arms (`Some(Ok(bytes))` / `Some(Err(e))` / `None`) - nested `if let` + `while let` patterns cause type inference issues with the `Bytes` type.

## Build / Dependencies

- 2026-07-03 â€” All npm installs in `frontend/` must use `--legacy-peer-deps`.
- 2026-07-03 â€” `EACCES` on `spawn node_modules/.bin/tauri` (or any `.bin` entry) means the wrapper script lost its execute bit (mode 644 instead of 755). Happens when `node_modules` is restored from a zip/tar or copied via a sync tool that strips modes. Fix: `chmod +x node_modules/.bin/tauri` (or reinstall). The native `cli.darwin-arm64.node` is `require()`-loaded and doesn't need +x; only the sh wrapper does.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Build verify loop: `cd frontend && npx ng build` and `cd backend/src-tauri && cargo check`. Keep both green after every phase.
- 2026-07-03 â€” `@angular/cdk` must stay at v20 to match Angular core.
- 2026-07-03 â€” `engine/` is consumed via the `@phorma/engine` tsconfig path alias (frontend/tsconfig.json â†’ ../engine/src/index.ts). Angular compiles it as app source; no build step. Keep engine code framework-free.
- 2026-07-03 â€” `backend/` needs its OWN `npm install` (installs `@tauri-apps/cli` into backend/node_modules/.bin). Without it `npm run dev` fails with "The system cannot find the path specified".
- 2026-07-03 â€” `cloud/` must depend on the `ai` package: the `agents` SDK dynamically imports it, and wrangler bundling fails with "Could not resolve ai" otherwise. Verify cloud changes with `npm run check` (tsc + `wrangler deploy --dry-run`) â€” no Cloudflare account needed; `wrangler dev` gives a full local DO for E2E.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Wrangler/esbuild honors tsconfig `paths`, so `@phorma/engine` resolves in cloud/ the same way as in the frontend.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Rust `process.rs` runs ONLY allow-listed programs (npx/npm). Extend the allow-list deliberately; never accept arbitrary program names from the webview.
- 2026-07-03 â€” TS structural typing: interfaces WITHOUT index signatures are not assignable to `Record<string, unknown>`. Cross-package boundary types should use `object` + per-kind casts instead.
- 2026-07-03 â€” `tokio::select!` requires the tokio `macros` feature in Cargo.toml.
- 2026-07-12 â€” Circular DI (NG0200) hazard around the run/model/cloud services: `RunControllerService â†’ ModelTransportService â†’ PhormaCloudService â†’ CloudService â†’ RunControllerService`. `CloudService` legitimately injects `RunControllerService` (to `apply()` remote run events). So services on the transport path must NOT inject `CloudService`. To read the Phorma Cloud base URL, call `loadPhormaCloudUrl()` from `core/phorma-cloud-url.ts` (both `ModelTransportService` and `PhormaCloudService` do this) instead of `cloud.phormaCloudUrl()`. That leaf module - not `cloud.service.ts` - owns `PHORMA_CLOUD_DEFAULT_URL`.
- 2026-08-24 - New sixth package `admin/` (`@phorma/admin`, the telemetry dashboard). It needs `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` like `frontend`, serves on **7323** (7322 studio, 7321 Phorma Code), and builds to `dist/admin/browser` - the Angular application builder appends the `browser` subfolder itself, so `angular.json` says `outputPath: dist/admin` and `wrangler.jsonc` points its assets at `./dist/admin/browser`. It is deliberately ISOLATED: no `paths` in its tsconfig and no import from `frontend`, `engine`, `cloud` or `cloud-aws` (the admin response types are a structural twin). Do NOT copy `@primeng/themes` across from `frontend/package.json` when mirroring pins - it is deprecated and unused there; only `@primeuix/themes` is imported.
- 2026-08-25 - CI's `checks` job runs Node **24**, not 20, and must not be "tidied" back to match `release.yml`. `cloud/test/workflow-state.test.mjs` imports `node:sqlite` at module scope; that builtin does not exist on Node 20 and needs `--experimental-sqlite` on 22, so the suite died at import with `ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE` and took the whole `Cloud unit tests` step with it. It had been failing since that suite landed, invisibly, because two earlier steps in the same job were already red. `portal-cleanup.test.mjs` guards the same import lazily and degrades; `workflow-state.test.mjs` cannot, since the entire file is about real SQLite behaviour. Local dev is Node 24, so a Node-20 CI was testing something no one runs.
- 2026-08-25 - A guard that asserts a path EXISTS must only name paths git tracks. `check-deploy-bundle.mjs` required every `NOT_BUNDLED` key to exist so a stale entry gets pruned, but five of them (`cloud/.wrangler/`, `cloud/dist/`, `cloud-aws/cdk.context.json`, `cloud-aws/cdk.out/`, `cloud-aws/dist/`) are build output. It therefore passed on any machine that had built and failed on every fresh checkout, which is exactly backwards: the failure only ever appeared in CI. Those five now sit in a `GENERATED` set that the liveness loop skips, with a cross-check that `GENERATED` and `NOT_BUNDLED` agree. Before adding an existence assertion, run `git ls-files -- <path>` on every entry.
- 2026-08-25 - The `npm test -- --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless` flag-forwarding failure is worse than "it warns and runs watch mode", and it was live in CI. Measured against a scratch package: npm 11.11.1 warns `Unknown cli config "--watch"` and passes the script ZERO arguments; npm 10.8.2 (the npm node 20 ships, so the runner's) drops them SILENTLY, same empty argv. And `@angular/build`'s karma builder defaults `watch = true` in `builders/karma/options.js` with no `CI`/TTY detection anywhere in `@angular/build` or `@angular/cli` - so the bare `ng test` starts a karma server, `singleRun` false, and never exits. `ci.yml`'s `Frontend unit tests` step was therefore a job-timeout hang waiting to happen; both Angular test steps now use `npx ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless`. Any new Angular package gets the `npx ng test` form from day one.

## UI / Styling

- 2026-08-17 - BYO deploy runtimes now ship INSIDE the installer (`bundle.resources` -> `deploy_assets.rs` -> `core/deploy/deploy-workspace.service.ts`), so no user-facing copy may mention cloning, `git pull`, or `cd cloud`. The update path is "update the app, Set up runtime files again, Deploy". Mechanism, layout invariants and the CI guard are in the `desktop-rust` steering; the studio-side seam is in `structure`.
- 2026-08-17 - `.phorma-settings__cloud-setup` cards had `margin-bottom: 14px` INSIDE a page body that is already a flex column with `gap: 10px`, so the real gap was 24px between cards whose own padding is 10px. Margin removed; the parent gap alone now gives a uniform 10px. Measure a gap as `next.top - previous.bottom` rather than reading the declaration - the container's `gap` is invisible in the rule you are editing.
- 2026-08-17 - Note tones (`__note--info` / `--warn` / `--danger`) are driven by ONE custom property, `--phorma-note-accent`, consumed by a single shared `color-mix` rule block; a tone costs one line. Two things paid for: (1) `--info` pointed at bare `var(--p-primary-color)`, which does not exist under karma, and `color-mix` with an undefined property is invalid at computed-value time - `border-color` silently fell back to `currentColor` and the fill vanished, the same trap as the old `--p-border-color` bug. Always give a literal fallback. (2) Budget: the tones fit because `.phorma-settings__inline-warning` (which was `__note--warn` with different padding) was folded into the note plus a new `__note--indented`, its dead `-close` rule deleted, and five identical `code` blocks merged into one selector list. Net -97 bytes at 21850.
- 2026-08-16 - The `anyComponentStyle` budget in `frontend/angular.json` is **22kB warning / 26kB error**, not the 20/24 several docs claimed (the `tech` steering is corrected). `settings-dialog.scss` compiles to 21850 bytes - measure with `npx sass --no-source-map --style=compressed <file> <out>` rather than a full build - so it has ~580 bytes of headroom and ONE new mixin expansion or rule block trips the warning. That is why the aws-byo-deploy AWS body section adds zero classes and zero SCSS: it reuses `__cloud-setup`, `__cloud-setup-intro`, `__input`, `__input--mono`, `__input--invalid`, `__hint`, `__note`, `__row`, `__row-label`, `__row--actions`, `__suffix` and `__btn`. `npm run build` prints a budget line only when one is EXCEEDED, so "no anyComponentStyle line in the output" is the pass signal - there is no number to read.
- 2026-08-16 - `.phorma-settings__note` and `.phorma-settings__cloud-setup-intro` are both `display: flex`, so contiguous text becomes an anonymous flex item: inline `<code>` or `<strong>` inside one splits the sentence into a row of disconnected boxes (the same trap `.phorma-settings__row-note`'s comment documents). Notes carry an icon plus ONE plain text run; put inline `<code>` in `.phorma-settings__hint`, which is a normal `<p>`.
- 2026-08-16 - Do NOT add `pInputText` to an element carrying `.phorma-settings__input`. That class applies `_field.scss`'s `chrome()` mixin AND `font-size: 12px`, and overriding font-size on a PrimeNG control desynchronizes its height from its neighbours (the size token drives height). The settings dialog's text fields are bespoke `<input>` by design - `_field.scss`'s own header says so. A requirement demanding an "explicit PrimeNG small size" is satisfied by the PrimeNG controls the surface really does render (buttons, selects), each carrying `size="small"`.
- 2026-08-11 - `max-width: Nch` resolves against the element's OWN font-size, so putting it on a wrapper div (inherited 14/16px) and expecting it to constrain a large heading inside is wrong by a factor of 4. Bit us in `docs/pitch-deck.html`: a `max-width:30ch` wrapper squeezed a 62px `h1` into five lines and overflowed the frame by 103px. Constrain the heading itself (its own `ch` is correct) or use px on the wrapper. Same class of bug as the 14px-root rem hazard: never do unit arithmetic against an assumed font-size, measure it.
- 2026-08-11 - Verifying a standalone HTML artifact with no Playwright installed: `chrome.exe --headless --disable-gpu --window-size=1280,720 --virtual-time-budget=3000 --dump-dom <file-url>` runs the page's JS and prints the resulting DOM, so a temporary probe script that writes measurements into `document.title` gives you real layout numbers to grep. `--print-to-pdf` needs `--headless=new` (old `--headless` silently produces no file) and an ABSOLUTE output path. Reading the PDF back: `[Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(28591)`, not `::Latin1` (null on Windows PowerShell 5), and `[IO.File]` resolves paths against the process cwd, not the shell's.
- 2026-08-10 - FIELD DESIGN LANGUAGE (soft/Framer-style): every PrimeNG form colour now points at a `--phorma-field-*` / `--phorma-control-*` / `--phorma-segment-*` / `--phorma-overlay-*` var defined per theme block in `styles.scss`, wired up once in `core/theme-preset.ts` (`PHORMA_SEMANTIC` + `PHORMA_COMPONENTS`, merged by `definePreset` in `app.config.ts`). Recipe: translucent fill, `border-color: transparent` on dark themes / 6% hairline on light, `shadow: none`, 8px radius, and a 1px `--p-primary-color` border as the ONLY focus indicator. Adding a theme mode = one `--phorma-field-*` block, no PrimeNG token names. GOTCHAS PAID FOR: (1) these colours MUST live in `colorScheme.light`/`colorScheme.dark`, not at the `semantic` level - PrimeNG emits the semantic block BEFORE the colour-scheme blocks in the same layer, so a semantic value loses to Aura's own on source order; (2) keep the resting `border-width` at 1px (transparent) or every field reflows 2px on focus; (3) Aura has NO `hoverBackground` for the default outlined input - only `filledHoverBackground` - so the hover/focus fill lift is a small unlayered rule block in `styles.scss`; (4) inputs with a value carry `.p-filled`, so the `filled*` tokens must be set too or valued fields diverge from empty ones.
- 2026-08-10 - `--p-border-color` IS NOT A TOKEN AURA EMITS (its hairline is `--p-content-border-color`). ~40 rules used it; the ones without a fallback were invalid at computed-value time, so `border-color` fell back to `currentColor` and rendered hairlines in the TEXT colour - a large part of why the chrome read as hard-edged. Aliased once in `styles.scss` (`:root { --p-border-color: var(--phorma-overlay-border) }`) rather than editing every call site. Use a `--phorma-*` token in new code.
- 2026-08-10 - PrimeNG's surface ramp is NOT theme-mode aware: the six theme modes only override `--phorma-*`, so `content`/`overlay`/`list`/`text` stayed global zinc (dark) / slate (light) and a Nord panel hosted a `#09090b` input. `theme-preset.ts` now retints those semantic groups per theme too. When adding a theme mode, the `--phorma-overlay-bg` / `--phorma-text` / `--phorma-hover-bg` values are what make PrimeNG overlays follow it.
- 2026-08-10 - Checkbox, radiobutton, toggleswitch, togglebutton, slider, select, multiselect and datepicker all reference `{form.field.*}`, so they inherit the field recipe automatically - but two of them break if you let them: an unchecked `p-checkbox` with a transparent border and a 5% fill is invisible (selection controls need their own `--phorma-control-border`), and `p-slider`'s track/handle are `{content.border.color}`, which is now a faint hairline. Both are handled in `PHORMA_COMPONENTS`; don't "simplify" them away.
- 2026-08-10 - Bespoke (non-PrimeNG) inputs share one recipe via the `shared/_field.scss` `chrome($radius)` mixin - `@use` it, keep only sizing/typography local. A global rule in `styles.scss` CANNOT do this job: component sheets are injected after the global sheet, so at equal specificity the component wins. Each expansion costs ~330 bytes of compiled CSS, so group selectors into ONE include per sheet where `anyComponentStyle` is tight (settings-dialog sits at ~22kB and went over with two).
- 2026-08-10 - Measuring contrast on translucent fills: token values tell you nothing, because the fill composites over a glass panel over the canvas. Screenshot the element, feed the PNG back into the page as a data URL, draw to a canvas and read pixels. Doing this caught placeholders at 2.5-2.9:1 across five themes (alphas 0.34-0.50 were too low); they are now tuned per theme to land at 3.7-3.9:1. Solarized needs the highest alpha (0.75) because Base1 over a Base02 field is a narrow luminance gap.
- 2026-08-10 - `getComputedStyle` read in the same tick as `el.focus()` returns the PRE-focus value: a focus-border check reported `transparent` and looked like a bug. Drive focus with a real `page.mouse.click` (or await a tick) before reading.
- 2026-08-10 - PrimeNG emits component theme CSS LAZILY: `--p-slider-*` vars do not exist until a slider renders. To verify a component-level token override, put the component on screen first (the slider lives in Settings > Canvas > Navigation), otherwise the token reads as an empty string and looks unset.
- 2026-08-10 - Form fields must opt out of the global `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--p-primary-color) }` rule in `styles.scss`. Browsers match `:focus-visible` on a text input even when it was focused by mouse, so the ring painted a SECOND primary line 1px outside the primary focus border on every field the user clicked into.
- 2026-07-28 â€” EXPANDED SIDE PANELS: Prompt / Properties / Evals / Usage each expand into a full-size dialog via `PanelExpandService` (`core/panel-expand.service.ts`, one `expanded` signal so only one can be open) + the shared `app-expanded-panel-dialog` shell (`shared/expanded-panel-dialog/`). Adding another: add the id to `ExpandablePanelId`, add a `ti ti-arrows-maximize` `.phorma-panel-icon-btn` to the panel header calling `panelExpand.open(id)`, and host the dialog in `app.html` inside `@defer (on immediate)`. The shell's `height` input takes `auto` for content-driven bodies (Properties) and a fixed `min(...)` for workbench bodies (Prompt/Evals). CRITICAL: the expanded overlay sits at `z-index: 75`, deliberately BELOW real dialogs (80) â€” an expanded panel is a bigger panel, not a modal, so confirms/settings summoned from inside it must layer on top. At an equal z-index the confirm lost on DOM order and was visible but unclickable.
- 2026-07-28 â€” Escape was globally deselecting the canvas even while an overlay was open (toolbar `onKeydown`), so closing any dialog with Esc silently emptied the selection the dialog was editing â€” the reopened panel came back blank. Guarded by `anyOverlayOpen()`, one `document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]')` probe. Every dialog in the app carries `role="dialog"`, so new ones are covered automatically. Any future global key handler that mutates app state needs the same guard.
- 2026-07-28 â€” Sharing a panel body between the sidebar and its expanded dialog: extract the body into a component with a `scope = input<string>('panel')` and route EVERY `id`/`for`/`inputId` through an `id(suffix)` helper. Both instances are in the DOM at once, so static ids silently duplicate and break every `<label for>` association. Verify with `document.querySelectorAll('[id]')` â€” total must equal the unique count. `PropertiesForm` (57 rewritten ids) and `AgentConfig` are the reference implementations; the panel/dialog then differ only in layout via a `layout: 'stack' | 'grid'` input.
- 2026-07-28 â€” A direct child of a `display: flex; flex-direction: column` scroll container needs `flex-shrink: 0` or it collapses to its own header height while `overflow: auto` hides the rest. The usage dialog's run-ledger card rendered as a 26px strip with 720px of unreachable content. Symptom to check for: `getBoundingClientRect().height` far below `scrollHeight` on a card that looks empty.
- 2026-07-28 â€” Chart.js options objects must be a `computed()` (not a static class field) whenever any axis bound depends on loaded data â€” a static field is evaluated at construction when the signals are still empty, so the bound is permanently wrong. Also: a secondary-axis bar series will auto-scale to fill the plot and bury the primary line, so cap it (`max: maxValue * 4`). And never label a time series date-only when points can share a day â€” the Evals trend showed three identical "Jul 28" ticks; add the clock time when `new Set(days).size < days.length`.
- 2026-07-28 â€” `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` immediately after `link.click()` can invalidate the blob before the browser reads it (empty/failed download). Defer with `setTimeout(..., 0)`. To E2E-verify a download without relying on Playwright download events, stub `URL.createObjectURL` to capture the blob and `HTMLAnchorElement.prototype.click` to no-op, then `await blob.text()`.
- 2026-07-28 â€” When surfacing per-node data from the usage ledger, remember the ledger outlives the graph (366 days of rows vs. whatever is on the canvas now), so historic rows routinely reference deleted nodes. Resolve unknown ids to an explicit "Deleted node Â· <short id>" label and make those rows non-clickable â€” a raw `node-ms4bâ€¦` id in a table reads as a rendering bug.
- 2026-07-28 â€” All five side panes (Properties, Prompt, Portal, Usage, Evals) are 100% PrimeNG controls: `pInputText`+`pSize="small"` on inputs, `pTextarea`+`pSize="small"` on textareas, `pButton` on buttons, plus `p-checkbox [binary]`, `p-inputnumber`, `p-select`, `p-selectbutton`. Zero native inputs/buttons and zero `span role="button"` remain â€” keep new fields consistent. Gotchas: `[link]` is not a pButton input (use `[text]="true"`); scope SCSS overrides as `.phorma-x__foo.p-button` and DELETE the old border/background/cursor rules or you double up on chrome; reach internals via `::ng-deep .p-inputnumber-input` / `.p-selectbutton`.
- 2026-07-28 â€” Destructive icon buttons should be `severity="secondary" [outlined]/[text]` with a `--danger` modifier class that goes red only on `:hover:not(:disabled)`. `severity="danger"` on every trash icon makes a panel read as a wall of warnings.
- 2026-07-28 â€” Never nest a `<button>` inside a `<button>` (invalid HTML, breaks keyboard nav). The Evals suite/run/result rows put the row button and its delete/action button as SIBLINGS in a `__row` flex wrapper, with the action revealed on `:hover` of the wrapper. Replaced the old `span role="button"` hack.
- 2026-07-28 â€” EVERY PrimeNG control in a panel needs an explicit size: `size="small"` on `pButton`/`p-select`/`p-inputnumber`/`p-checkbox`/`p-selectbutton`, `pSize="small"` on `pInputText`/`pTextarea`. Omitting it silently yields the default (larger) size, so a select renders 37px next to a 32px input in the same row and Back/Run in a header differ in height. Audit with a regex for tags lacking `size=`. Also do NOT override `font-size` on these controls in panel SCSS - the size token drives the height, so a hard-coded `0.8rem` desynchronizes inputs from the selects beside them.
- 2026-07-28 â€” PrimeNG checkbox/radio/toggleswitch render a transparent native `<input>` over the styled box, and the UA `cursor: text` on that overlay beats the wrapper's `cursor: pointer` (I-beam when hovering the box). Fixed globally in `styles.scss` via `.p-checkbox-input, .p-radiobutton-input, .p-toggleswitch-input { cursor: pointer }` plus a `:disabled` variant. Don't re-patch per component.
- 2026-07-28 â€” Two shared icon-button classes live in `styles.scss` - use them instead of per-panel sizing: `.phorma-panel-icon-btn` (1.5rem square, 0.4rem radius, for ALL panel header actions â€” Refresh / New suite / Expand / AI / Preview etc., paired with `severity="secondary" [text] size="small"` and NO `[rounded]`) and `.phorma-input-icon-btn` (1.85rem wide, height from the row's `align-items: stretch`, for copy/open buttons flush beside a small input, paired with `[outlined]`). Spinner: `.phorma-icon-spin` on the inner `<i>`. NEVER use `[rounded]="true"` on panel header buttons â€” it renders a circular pill that is inconsistent with the square assistant-panel pattern. The canonical reference is `.phorma-assist__icon-btn` in the assistant panel.
- 2026-07-28 â€” Don't use `float: right` for a trailing action inside a section heading - the following hint text wraps under the heading and collides. Make the label a flex row and give the button `margin-left: auto` (the Usage/Evals pattern).
- 2026-07-28 â€” `flex: 1` on a scrolling panel's grow section expands to `1 1 0%`, so the panel can squeeze it below its own content and the trailing hint overflows onto the next heading. Use `flex: 1 0 auto` (grow, never shrink) and `flex-shrink: 0` on the sibling sections.
- 2026-07-26 â€” Canvas overlays (ThinkingOverlay, AskUserOverlay, MCP warnings) reposition via `transformTick` bumped in `engine.onAfterDraw`, gated on overlays existing. When adding a NEW overlay type, add its presence check to the gate in `graph-canvas.ts` (`nodeThinking().size > 0 || pendingQuestions().length > 0 || hasMcpWarnings()`) or the overlay won't track pan/zoom. Overlay bodies render sanitized markdown via `marked` + `DOMPurify` + `DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml` â€” same pattern as assistant-chat.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Icons are **Tabler-only** (`ti ti-*`). `primeicons` is removed; PrimeNG components that render built-in icons (select chevrons, toast close, submenu arrows, checkboxes) need icon templates/`pt` overrides â€” audit when adding a new PrimeNG component.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Specular shimmer (`::after` gradient) was originally on the LEFT panel only. Right panel, terminal, status bar were plain glass. The single hairline divider is drawn by the resize handle, not a panel border (avoid double lines). REMOVED 2026-07-22: the left sidebar and toolbar shimmer `::after` gradients were stripped so ALL chrome panels (toolbar, both sidebars, terminal, status bar) are now plain frosted glass for consistency.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Angular templates do not support arrow functions in event bindings â€” use a component method.
- 2026-08-10 - Forcing `display: block` on a `p-select` host (to make it full-width in a form field) breaks the component's own `inline-flex` layout: the label and dropdown chevron stack vertically instead of sitting side by side, clipping the label to one character's height. Fix: use `display: flex; width: 100%` instead of `display: block; width: 100%` on the wrapper class. Hit this in the connection editor's "Auth mode" select (`connection-editor-dialog.scss`).
- 2026-07-03 â€” Literal `{` / `}` inside template attribute values (e.g. JSON placeholders) break Angular @-block parsing. Avoid braces in placeholders or use HTML entities.
- 2026-07-03 â€” `ToastService` has `success/warning/error/show` â€” there is NO `.info()`.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Console entry `timestamp` is an ISO string; `bottom-terminal.formatTime()` re-parses it with `new Date()`. Never store pre-formatted locale strings there.
- 2026-07-03 â€” PrimeNG context-menu submenus open on HOVER; Playwright synthetic clicks can't reach nested items. The palette supports click-to-add (`NodeDragService.requestAdd`) partly for this reason â€” keep it working.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Tried an SVG rainbow chasing-glow border on the prompt editor's focus state (dashed rect + hue-rotate). User rejected it on sight ("looks like shit") and it was reverted same-session. Lesson: flashy animated borders on a plain multi-line text input read as gimmicky, not premium â€” keep focus indication to a simple border-color change (see `.phorma-prompt__editor:focus`). Don't re-propose SVG glow effects for form inputs without being asked.
- 2026-07-04 â€” `ConfirmDialogService` supports a `prompt()` mode with a single text input (added for workflow naming). Pass a `ConfirmDialogInput` (initialValue, placeholder, required, maxLength); resolves to the trimmed string on confirm or `null` on cancel. The dialog component auto-focuses the input and Enter submits when non-empty. Reuse this for any rename/name flow instead of building a bespoke dialog. GOTCHA: `close()` clears `activeState` to `null` BEFORE calling `resolve`, so the `.then()` callback must NOT read `this.activeState()` â€” the resolution object carries `inputValue` through the resolver closure instead. Reading the signal in `.then()` silently returns `''` (the original bug that made saves always store "Untitled Workflow").
- 2026-07-06 â€” PrimeNG v20 button CSS variables are severity-prefixed: `--p-button-primary-background`, `--p-button-primary-hover-background`, `--p-button-secondary-background`, etc. There is NO generic `--p-button-background` or `--p-button-hover-background`. To make a `::before` overlay track the button's background across all severities/states, use `background-color: inherit` (picks up the computed `background-color` which PrimeNG swaps per hover/active/severity). `color-mix(in oklch, inherit, white N%)` does NOT work â€” `inherit` is not resolved inside `color-mix`. Use `background-color: inherit` + `background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,N%), transparent)` instead.
- 2026-07-23 â€” PrimeNG v20 `pButton` (non-outlined, i.e. primary/solid) renders an opaque `::before` overlay at `position:absolute; z-index:0; inset:0` with the button's `background-color`. In-flow children (bare text nodes AND static `<i>` icons, both `z-index:auto`) paint BELOW this overlay, so the label text AND icon are invisible on solid buttons. Fix: wrap the label in `<span class="...label" style="position:relative;z-index:1">` and give the `<i>` icon `position:relative; z-index:1` too. Outlined/secondary buttons don't hit this (their `::before` background is transparent). This is a general PrimeNG v20 gotcha, not specific to the version-history dialog â€” any solid `pButton` with inline content (icon + bare text, no `.p-button-label` span) will have invisible content.
- 2026-07-28 â€” There is now a SHARED fix for the solid-`pButton` invisible-content gotcha: add `class="phorma-btn-content"` (styles.scss) to any solid `pButton` and wrap bare label text in a `<span>`. The class sets `isolation: isolate`, pushes `::before` to `z-index:-1` and lifts `> *` to `z-index:1`. Use it instead of hand-rolling per-button `position:relative; z-index:1` rules. Detect the bug WITHOUT eyeballing: screenshot the button element, draw it to a canvas and count pixels with all channels > 200 â€” a solid button whose label is buried reports **0** bright pixels. Audit regex for offenders: `<button[^>]*pButton[^>]*>` filtered to matches lacking `[text]`, `[outlined]` or `phorma-btn-content` (note `severity="secondary"` on its own is still SOLID and affected).
- 2026-07-24 â€” Same invisible-text gotcha applies to the hand-rolled `.phorma-btn-shimmer` utility class (styles.scss): its `::before` overlay sits at `z-index:0` and the `> * { z-index:1 }` lifter only catches ELEMENT children. Bare text nodes are NOT elements, so `> *` skips them and they paint under the overlay (icon visible, label invisible). Fix: wrap any bare label text in a `<span>` inside `.phorma-btn-shimmer` buttons. Icon-only shimmer buttons (chat send, cmdk submit) are fine without a span.
- 2026-07-06 â€” `updatePrimaryPalette()` called in `ThemeService` constructor does NOT take effect on first paint â€” PrimeNG's theme engine hasn't emitted CSS yet when the service is first injected. To seed the saved palette on first paint, read localStorage synchronously in `app.config.ts` and pass the ramp to `definePreset(Aura, { semantic: { primary: ramp } })`. The `ThemeService` constructor still calls `updatePrimaryPalette` for runtime swaps, but the preset seeding prevents the flash.
- 2026-07-06 â€” Theme palettes are: Iris (purple, default), Azure (blue), Emerald (green), Monochrome (neutral). Retired ids: 'indigo' â†’ 'azure', 'blue' â†’ 'azure', 'slate' â†’ 'iris'. Migrations live in both `app.config.ts` (`readInitialPaletteRamp`) and `theme.service.ts` (`readInitialPalette`) â€” keep them in sync. The Iris 500 is `#8578f6` (oklch(0.645 0.20 286), a vibrant version of #8878F2).
- 2026-07-22 â€” Root font-size is **14px** (`html`/`body` in styles.scss), NOT 16px. Any rem-based type floor must be computed against 14: `0.857rem`â‰ˆ12px, `0.928rem`â‰ˆ13px. A prior pass wrongly used `0.75rem`/`0.8125rem` (16px-root assumptions) which rendered 10.5/11.4px. Verify font floors by measuring `getComputedStyle(...).fontSize` in the live browser, never by rem arithmetic alone.
- 2026-07-22 â€” Panel-width persistence bug (fixed): `Sidebar.panelWidth` was `signal(270)` and `ngAfterContentInit` pushed it into the registry, clobbering the saved `leftWidth`/`rightWidth` on every startup. Hydration must read the registry per-side AFTER the `side` input is bound. The `side` input is NOT bound in the constructor (input signal reads its default 'left' there) â€” hydrate in `ngOnInit`, which runs before `ngAfterContentInit`'s write-back. Default width is now 320 (`DEFAULT_PANEL_WIDTH` in panel-registry.service.ts); MIN 220 / MAX 640.
- 2026-07-22 â€” Dark shell is "obsidian/violet", not blue-charcoal: `:root.app-dark` neutral surfaces use hue ~275 at very low chroma (canvas `#0c0a10`, card `#130f18`, node `#17131d`, glass `rgba(19,15,25,0.88)`). Keep `--phorma-accent-blue` selection accents and the azure palette option â€” only neutral surfaces were tinted. Matches phorma-labs.com.
- 2026-07-22 â€” PrimeNG `p-button` in this app: never use the `icon`/`iconPos` props (they render removed `pi pi-*` PrimeIcons). Put the Tabler icon as content: `<button pButton severity="secondary" [outlined]="true"><i class="ti ti-plus"></i> Label</button>`. Icon-only destructive â†’ `severity="danger" [text]="true" [rounded]="true"`. Keep hero/accent buttons (green Run, OAuth Connect, runs Approve) hand-rolled to preserve their custom accent/shimmer.
- 2026-08-11 - A destructive confirm must describe what it destroys NOW, not what it destroyed when the copy was written. The library delete and "Remove from cloud" both started tearing down cloud resources (cron, published portal, cloud run history and usage) while still promising "Run history is kept" / "removed from your library". Also: a deployed workflow now ALWAYS confirms on library delete even with `confirmWorkflowDelete()` off - that setting covers a local, recoverable delete, not taking a public portal offline.
- 2026-07-24 â€” Sidebar list row truncation pattern (skills panel = canonical): action buttons live in a `.phorma-__row-actions` container that collapses to `width:0; opacity:0; overflow:hidden` when not hovered and expands to `width:auto; opacity:1` on row `:hover`. This is the ONLY way to let the title/meta column get the full row width (so text truncates at the right edge) while still revealing actions on hover without overlap. The workflows panel previously used `opacity:0` alone on each button - they still occupied layout space (~66px for 3 Ã— 1.6rem buttons), forcing the name to truncate far back. Fixed to match the skills pattern: wrap buttons in a collapsing `.phorma-__row-actions` span, shrink buttons to 1.4rem with 0.1rem gap, use `<span role="button" tabindex="0">` (NOT nested `<button>` - invalid HTML inside a button) with `(click)` + `(keydown.enter)` + `event.stopPropagation()` in the handler. Same pattern should be reused for any future sidebar list row with hover-revealed actions.
- 2026-08-24 - Not every overlay wants `role="dialog"`. An advisory overlay the user did not summon belongs in the `z-index: 60` band (the AI review bar's band) with `role="status"`, NOT `role="dialog"` and no focus trap: the global Escape guard probes `[role="dialog"]` and would start treating the overlay as a modal that owns the key, swallowing the canvas shortcut. Keep it below the 80 band so a real dialog it deep-links into layers over it. (The original example, the telemetry First_Run_Notice at `workspace/settings/privacy/telemetry-notice.ts`, was deleted on 2026-09-07 - the rule outlived it.)

- 2026-08-25 - Two defects behind one property (`admin` Property 35, "a range change refetches every bound view"), both worth generalizing. (1) A signal that views key a `resource()` on must not be re-`set` with an equal-but-new object: `DateRangeService.applyPreset` always minted a fresh `trailingRange(...)`, so re-clicking the ACTIVE preset (the dashboard opens on 30 days, so the very first click) refetched all five views for identical data. Route every writer through the one guarded setter (`setRange`, which returns false only for a range the Admin_API would 400) instead of touching the backing signal. (2) `linkedSignal` is LAZY and compares against the source value recorded the last time it COMPUTED - a `.set()` does not refresh that record. So `linkedSignal(() => range.from())` as a date-input draft went stale: typing a day that the commit then made the shared `from`, then a preset moving `from` away and back to that same day between two reads, read as "unchanged" and the input kept a superseded day, which then committed as one end of the next typed range. It only looked fine in the app because the template re-reads it every CD cycle. For draft-vs-committed state where the reset must key on the PREVIOUS committed value, use plain signals synced eagerly at the write (per end), not a lazy link.

- 2026-08-25 - Schedule trigger editor: the stored `cron` is ALWAYS UTC (both runtimes evaluate it that way - Cloudflare's agents SDK `schedule()`, and EventBridge Scheduler pinned to `ScheduleExpressionTimezone: 'UTC'` in `cloud-aws/src/aws/scheduler.ts`), and `ScheduleTriggerData.timezone` is EDITOR state that the panel converts through. All the conversion lives in `core/schedule-cron.ts` (pure, 35 specs): `zoneOffsetMinutes` derives an offset by formatting an instant in the zone and reading it back as UTC, so DST comes for free without a tz database. Two traps it exists to handle: a local time can carry the DATE across UTC midnight, which must rotate the weekday set (08:00 Mon-Fri Sydney is `0 22 * * 0,1,2,3,4`), and half-hour zones need minute-level offsets. Remaining limitation, stated in the UI popover: the UTC cron is fixed, so a DST transition shifts the run by an hour until the schedule is re-saved. Fixing that needs the runtime to own the timezone.
- 2026-08-25 - A bespoke segmented control must read `--phorma-segment-bg` (track) and `--phorma-segment-selected` (active fill) - the same two tokens `core/theme-preset.ts` maps onto PrimeNG's `togglebutton`, so it paints identically to every `p-selectbutton` in all six themes (measured `rgba(255,255,255,0.13)` on both). Do NOT invent a token name: `--phorma-segment-active-bg` does not exist, so `var(--phorma-segment-active-bg, var(--phorma-card-bg))` silently fell back to the card colour, which is DARKER than the track and read as a heavy black slab. Also skip the border and box-shadow - the selectbutton has neither, and they are what makes a segment look chunky.
- 2026-08-25 - `type="number"` cannot render a leading zero, so a time field shows "9 : 0" instead of "09 : 00". Use `type="text"` + `inputmode="numeric"` + `maxlength` and pad the bound value, then restore Up/Down stepping with a `keydown` handler (minutes in 5s). Dropping the `appearance`/spin-button resets at the same time keeps the sheet smaller.
- 2026-08-25 - A frequency segmented control whose value is DERIVED from the stored expression cannot latch on "Custom": the parse of `0 * * * *` is `hourly`, so the segment sprang back. Needs explicit UI state keyed by node id (`customCronNodeId`), with the shown frequency = parsed value unless the user chose Custom for THAT node. Any "advanced/raw" escape hatch over a derived model has this shape.
- 2026-08-25 - Browser harness setup order for canvas work: a fresh CDP profile has NO open document, and `WorkflowService.newWorkflow()` finishes initialising asynchronously - calling `__phormaTest.addNode()` in the same tick silently loses the node (`graph()` reads empty and `addNode` throws "Unknown node ... Known: (none)"). Open the doc, wait a tick, then add. Also `addNode` returns the NODE, not an id, so `select(node.id)`.
- 2026-08-25 - A PrimeNG `styleClass` target needs `:host ::ng-deep` in a component sheet. The class lands on the `<button>` inside PrimeNG's own template, which never carries the host component's `_ngcontent` attribute, so an encapsulated `.phorma-x__btn.p-button { ... }` rule matches NOTHING and fails silently - the symptom is a measurement that does not budge when you change the value. `settings-dialog.scss` already had two such blocks; follow them. Cheaper still: for a small action inside a settings note, reuse the plain-`<button>` `.phorma-settings__link` (what "Add API key" uses) and write zero CSS.
- 2026-08-25 - A control for a capability the chosen model lacks is REMOVED, not explained. Settings > Models > Default temperature drops its whole row via `acceptsSamplingParams(settings.defaultModel())` - the same engine function `buildWireRequest` gates on, so the control and the wire body cannot disagree. An explanatory paragraph in place of the widget was tried first and rejected on sight: a settings row whose only content is a reason it does nothing is worse than silence. The stored value survives and applies again on a model that accepts one. Gate on the STORED model id, not `modelDisplayValue()`, which is blank while a key is missing.
- 2026-08-25 - `<label for>` on a `p-slider` is dead markup: the component renders no labelable element, so `for="default-temperature"` referenced an id nothing carried. Use a `<span>` for the visible label and let the slider's `ariaLabel` supply the accessible name. Worth probing for elsewhere: `!!label && !document.getElementById(label.getAttribute('for'))` over a page finds them all.
- 2026-08-25 - `/* */` SCSS comments survive into the emitted CSS and therefore count against the `anyComponentStyle` budget; `//` comments do not. `settings-dialog.scss` sits ~50 bytes under the 22kB warning, so a normal-sized commented rule block tips it. Converting the comment style is NOT enough on its own if the rules themselves are new - measure with `npm run build` after each attempt, and prefer deleting a rule (reuse an existing class) over shaving prose.
- 2026-09-03 - `anyComponentStyle` is measured PER STYLESHEET, so a new surface that cannot fit in `settings-dialog.scss` (21972 bytes, ~556 left of the 22528-byte warning) belongs in its OWN component rather than in a shaving exercise. The Settings > Cloud plan cards went that way: `workspace/cloud/plan-cards/` is 1881 bytes in its own sheet and the settings sheet did not move a byte, because every new markup element there reused `__row`, `__note`, `__link` and `__subscribe`. Confirm with `npx sass --no-source-map --style=compressed <in> <out>` per sheet; `npm run build` prints a budget line only when one is EXCEEDED, so no `anyComponentStyle` line in the output IS the pass.
- 2026-09-03 - Do NOT add `phorma-btn-content` to a button already carrying `phorma-btn-shimmer`. Both own `::before`: the shimmer paints the specular gradient there, and `phorma-btn-content` sets `isolation: isolate` plus `::before { z-index: -1 }`, which inside the new stacking context buries the sheen behind the button's own background. The shimmer class already handles its own layering - a `<span>`-wrapped label needs nothing else.
- 2026-09-03 - A component whose only content is conditional (an error, a recovery link) should be `:host { display: contents }` and dropped straight into the host's flex column - no box means the parent's `gap` contributes nothing while it is empty. Wrap it in a real `<div>` only where the parent is a BLOCK, and then gate the wrapper with `@if`, or its `margin-top` leaves permanent dead space (hit in `.phorma-cmdk__locked`).
- 2026-09-04 - A `p-button` reached through `styleClass` is TWO elements, and only one of them is the layout item: the class lands on the inner `<button>`, while the flex or grid item is the `<p-button>` HOST (`display: block`). So an auto margin or `align-self` written against `.phorma-x__btn.p-button` absorbs no free space at all. Measured on the Settings > Cloud plan cards: `margin-top: auto` on the inner button left the 18px misalignment exactly where it was and merely deleted the 4px gap under the blurb, while the same declaration on `.phorma-plans__card > p-button` took the spread to 0.00. Put positioning on the host, keep sizing (`width: 100%`, `min-width`) on the inner button. Probe before believing a `::ng-deep` positioning rule anywhere in the app - `.phorma-prompt__label-btn.p-button { margin-left: auto }` looks like the same mistake.
- 2026-09-04 - Cards in a `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(Npx, 1fr))` grid are stretched to the row height, so any variable-length text above a trailing action (a blurb that wraps to a third line) leaves free space that nothing absorbs and the action lands at a different y per card. The fix is an auto margin on the action's layout item, NOT `justify-content` on the card. Assert it per GRID ROW: at a narrow settings pane the same grid drops to two or one columns, where unequal tops across rows are correct.
- 2026-09-04 - `flex: 0 0 auto` on a GRID item is inert, however confident the comment above it sounds. `.phorma-plans__card` carried it with a note about being "a flex item in a column that scrolls" while its parent was `.phorma-plans__grid`. Cheap proof, no rebuild: set `flex: 1 1 0%` and then `flex: 5 5 400px` inline and diff `getBoundingClientRect()` - a real flex item moves, a grid item does not. Also check the sibling claim before deleting: the section this component renders measured `height` 334.23 against `scrollHeight` 334, so nothing needed the guard moved anywhere.

## Product Rules

- 2026-07-03 â€” Prompts are **markdown**. Render previews sanitized (`marked` + DOMPurify) â€” never raw `innerHTML`.
- 2026-07-03 â€” No Monaco, no code editors. This is not a coding tool.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Domain/engine code must not hard-depend on Tauri â€” the app must work in a plain browser (`TauriService.isDesktop` guards).
- 2026-07-03 â€” API keys: desktop keys live in the OS keychain via `llm.rs` (webview only sees a boolean); engine requests carry the `{{API_KEY}}` placeholder that Rust (desktop) or FetchModelClient (web) substitutes. Never log or persist raw keys elsewhere.
- 2026-07-03 â€” RunEvents are the single visualization contract: local engine AND (later) cloud WebSocket both feed `RunControllerService.apply()`. New run UI must consume RunEvents, not bespoke state.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Tool calling is native: agents get tool schemas from their tool-link edges via the engine's `ToolHost` (studio: `ToolHostService`; cloud: `CloudToolHost`). Tool loop max 8 rounds, results capped at 8KB.
- 2026-07-03 â€” MCP stdio transport is NEWLINE-DELIMITED JSON-RPC (not LSP Content-Length framing). Sessions live in Rust (`mcp.rs`), keyed by tool node id. Remote MCP uses the engine's `HttpMcpClient` (streamable HTTP; responses may be SSE or JSON â€” parse both).
- 2026-07-03 â€” Ollama's OpenAI-compat endpoint sends `finish_reason` without a `[DONE]` line â€” stream parsers must flush tool calls on BOTH signals.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Engine E2E testing: a throwaway `npx -y tsx script.mts` importing `./engine/src/index.js` against local Ollama is the fastest full-loop verification (no UI needed).
- 2026-07-03 â€” Web Search tool uses DuckDuckGo's free instant-answer API â€” topical coverage only. Swap in a keyed provider (Brave/Tavily) for production-grade search without touching the engine.
- 2026-07-03 â€” Web Search was returning "No results found" for ANY query because Wikipedia's API rejects requests with no `User-Agent` header (HTTP 403 "Please set a user-agent"). `reqwest` (Rust desktop path) and Cloudflare Workers `fetch` send NO default UA. The engine's `safeParse` silently swallowed the 403 body into `{}` â†’ 0 results. Fix: `performWebSearch` now passes `User-Agent: PhormaAgentStudio/0.1 (https://phorma.dev)` via the `TextFetcher` signature (now `(url, headers?) => ...`). Also added `origin=*` to Wikipedia URLs for browser-path CORS. Lesson: any outbound HTTP from the engine should set a UA â€” many APIs (Wikipedia, GitHub, etc.) reject UA-less requests, and the failure is silent because `safeParse` masks non-JSON bodies.
- 2026-09-07 - The first-run telemetry notice is GONE and must not come back in any form (popup, banner, toast, onboarding step). Deleted: `workspace/settings/privacy/telemetry-notice.ts` + its spec, its `app.html` host, `TelemetryService.noticePending` / `dismissNotice`, and `shouldShowNotice` in `telemetry-core.ts` (dead once the signal went, so its Property 1 assertions went too - the property is now "Consent bootstrap decision" over `readConsent` + `acknowledgeDisclosure`). Telemetry STAYS ON BY DEFAULT; the disclosure moved to an accept-privacy step on the download website, before the installer is downloaded. The owner accepted the tradeoff: anyone who gets the app off-website sees nothing until they open Settings > Privacy, which is now the ONLY in-app disclosure and must keep working (toggle, Install_Id, counter list, pending payload, policy link). An installer checkbox was rejected because `tauri.conf.json` builds `nsis`, `app`, `dmg`, `appimage` and `deb` - Windows-only UI would leave macOS and Linux with nothing. `CURRENT_DISCLOSURE_VERSION` and the persisted `{enabled, disclosureVersion, decidedAt}` record stay: the version is what the website step pairs with, not a gate. Decision record: `.kiro/specs/telemetry-phone-home/requirements.md` Requirement 1.

## Settings System

- 2026-07-07 - `SettingControl` supports a `button` type (`{ type: 'button', label, icon? }`): the dialog renders a small outlined `p-button` on the row's control side, clicking calls `setting.set(undefined)`. Use for action-style settings (e.g. "Run setup wizard") - a toggle is NEVER the medium for one-shot actions.
- 2026-07-07 - Setup wizard (`workspace/onboarding/`) is strictly modal: no close button, backdrop click and Escape are no-ops (Escape is swallowed while visible so it doesn't leak to other dialogs/canvas). Exits are finish or explicit "Skip setup" - BOTH call `OnboardingService.finish()` which sets `firstRunDone` so the wizard never auto-opens again. The API-keys path also finishes before deep-linking to Settings. There is no plain `close()` on the service by design.
- 2026-07-04 - Application settings are registry-driven: `core/settings-registry.ts` (`SettingsRegistryService`) declares pages/sections/`SettingDef` descriptors whose get/set delegate to service signals (SettingsService, ThemeService, CanvasStateService). The Settings dialog renders generically from it - adding/removing a setting is one descriptor entry, no template changes. Bespoke UIs (API keys, palette swatches, integration creds, default model) use `customTemplate` ids mapped to @switch cases in `settings-dialog.html`.
- 2026-07-04 - Settings dialog is a bespoke two-pane overlay (`.phorma-settings`, mirrors confirm/cloud dialog pattern) - the app now has ZERO `p-dialog` usage. Controls are PrimeNG (p-toggleswitch, p-select, p-slider) with `appendTo="body"`. Opened via App menu > Settings or Ctrl+, (`SettingsDialogService.open(pageId?)` supports deep-links, e.g. `open('integrations')` from the properties panel).
- 2026-07-04 - Agent default model is TRUE INHERITANCE: `AgentNodeData.provider/model` are optional (both `workflow.model.ts` AND `engine/src/types.ts` - keep twins in sync). Engine `RunOptions.defaultModel`/`maxToolRounds` carry app settings into local runs; `CloudService.materializeDefaults()` bakes them into the spec at push time (no cloud/ changes). New agents from `node-catalog.ts` carry NO provider/model. Canvas subtitle shows "Default" when inheriting.
- 2026-07-04 - MCP preset secrets have two keychain scopes: node `mcp:{nodeId}:{envKey}` (override) and preset `mcp:preset:{presetId}:{envKey}` (app default, set in Settings > Integrations). Both pass llm.rs's `mcp:` prefix validation unchanged. Rust `mcp_connect` takes optional `preset_id` and resolves node scope first, then preset scope. Properties panel shows a status pill + collapsible Advanced group for overrides.
- 2026-07-04 - GOTCHA: an Angular `effect()` that calls a method which synchronously READS and WRITES the same signal (e.g. `refreshMcpSecretFlags` reading+setting `mcpSecretsConfigured` in browser mode) loops forever and CRASHES the page (renderer OOM). Wrap such calls in `untracked(() => ...)`. Hit twice in this feature (settings dialog + properties panel effects).

- 2026-08-11 - GOTCHA (agents SDK `ctx.storage.deleteAll`): `this.ctx.storage` IS accessible on `Agent` subclasses (the SDK itself uses it: `this.ctx.storage.sql`, `deleteAlarm`, `deleteAll` in its own `destroy()`). But `deleteAll()` only clears the DO's KEY-VALUE storage, NOT the SQLite tables - the SDK's state lives in `cf_agents_state` (SQLite), so a purge must `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS cf_agents_state`/`cf_agents_schedules`/`cf_agents_queues`/`cf_agents_mcp_servers` separately or those rows leak. The SDK's own `destroy()` drops them but also calls `this.ctx.abort("destroyed")` (via setTimeout) which aborts the request context - do NOT call `destroy()` from an HTTP handler that needs to return a response; replicate its table drops + `deleteAll()` instead.

- 2026-08-07 - CREDENTIALS THAT REACH A DEPLOYED WORKER - the honest matrix, verified by reading every path. A deployed run can ONLY resolve a credential that exists as a worker secret: `CONN_<ID>_<KEY>` (connections) or `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` (remote MCP bearer, now a declared `MCP_${string}` index signature on `Env` instead of a `as keyof Env` cast). Consequences: (a) stdio MCP is impossible by design; (b) interactive-OAuth MCP is impossible in the cloud in BOTH modes - tokens live in the studio keychain via `mcp-oauth.service.ts` `mcp-oauth:{nodeId}` and `CloudToolHost.mcpFor` only ever reads `authKey`, never `authMode`. **UPDATED 2026-08-10: point (c) no longer holds for `CONN_*` - see the SecretVault entry below. It still holds for `MCP_*`, so a remote MCP node with an `authKey` in hosted mode still runs UNAUTHENTICATED and fails silently at the MCP server.**
- 2026-08-10 - CONNECTION SECRETS ON A DEPLOYED RUN, second ingestion path (`SecretVault`, spec `.kiro/specs/deployed-credential-vault/`). The reported bug: save a bearer secret in the connection editor, push to the cloud, get "Connection X is missing 1 of 1 secret values on Cloudflare Worker" and an aborted push. Correct behaviour, unactionable UX - the local value is in the OS keychain (`conn:{id}:{key}`) and the worker counts `CONN_*` env vars, and nothing in the app could set one. Now: `POST /api/connection-secrets {connectionId, secretKey, value}` encrypts with `KEY_ENC_SECRET` and stores in a `SecretVault` DO scoped `secrets:{userId}` (hosted) / `secrets:default` (BYO); `WorkerConnectionStore` reads env FIRST, vault second. Gotchas that bit or nearly bit: (a) the vault must be per OWNER not per workflow, or the operator re-enters the same key once per workflow; (b) `pushWorkflow` reads the inventory BEFORE `POST /workflow` stamps `ownerId`, so `connectionHost` needs an `ownerFallback` from `auth.userId` or a hosted tenant's FIRST deploy of a workflow reads the wrong vault and reports everything missing; (c) a new DO class needs migration `v3` in `wrangler.jsonc` top level AND `env.hosted` AND `DeployConfigService.DO_MIGRATIONS`/`DO_BINDINGS` - the generated `wrangler.byo.jsonc` REPLACES the committed config, so missing it silently drops the binding from every BYO deploy; (d) the route sits ABOVE the `store.enabled` gate in `api.ts` because BYO has no D1; (e) it refuses on a BYO worker with neither `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` nor `PHORMA_TOKEN` - an open worker treats every caller as owner, fine for `/trigger`, not for a credential store. `deploy-config.test.mjs` now derives the expected DO class list from `src/index.ts`'s export statement, so this class of drift fails a test instead of a deploy.
- 2026-08-11 - The vault shipped with a DEAD END in the connection editor, reported by a user on a `basic` (user + password) HTTP connection: both the local-save button and the cloud-upload button deleted the row's draft on success, and both were disabled without a draft. So whichever store you wrote first, the other one became unreachable for that value - and since NEITHER store can be read back, "sync the stored value" is not a thing that can exist. Symptom as reported: saved the secrets locally, cloud upload greyed out, push kept aborting with "missing 2 of 2 secret values". Fix: `saveSecret` fans out from the ONE draft to every store this install has (keychain when `secretsSupported`, deploy target when `cloudConfigured()`), and the draft survives until every one of them holds it (`secretMissingSomewhere`). Phorma Cloud consent is asked once per DIALOG session (`cloudConsent` signal, reset in `seedForm`) instead of once per secret, or a two-secret auth mode stacks two identical prompts; declining stores locally and keeps the draft so the explicit cloud button is still a way in. `putConnectionSecret` grew a `{silent}` option so the fan-out reports both stores in one toast - errors always toast. Lesson for any write-only store: never clear the only copy of a value while a second destination still needs it. Test: `connection-editor-dialog.spec.ts`.
- 2026-08-10 - The connection editor asked for the same secret name TWICE - once as `auth.secretKey` (a pointer) and once as a declared field in the Secrets list - with nothing linking them, so a typo resolved to nothing at run time with no visible cause. Fixed by `authSecretKeyNames(auth)` (engine) + `withAuthSecretKeys` (editor): saving a connection auto-declares every name the selected auth mode points at. ADD-ONLY on purpose - removing a name the operator stopped pointing at would orphan a stored value. Do not "clean up" `secretKeys` to match auth.
- 2026-08-10 - `ConnectionSummary.missingSecretKeys` (both stores populate it) + `HostCapabilities.connectionSecretScheme` (`os-keychain` | `cloudflare-worker-env` | `none`) are what make a missing-secret finding end in an action naming the exact entry. The scheme is DECLARED data, not an inferred host id, so a new host inherits no remedy text by accident. Keep the finding's `(secret keys: ...)` fragment: `capabilities-findings.spec.ts` asserts on it.
- 2026-08-07 - `smtp` is a DECLARED BUT UNIMPLEMENTED `ConnectionType`. It is in `ALL_CONNECTION_TYPES` and therefore in every host's `connectionTypes` (so push validation lets it through), and the connection editor offers it, but nothing anywhere speaks SMTP: no `lettre` in Cargo.toml, zero `smtp` matches in `cloud/src/` or `backend/src-tauri/src/`, and `engine.ts` says outright it "keeps an SMTP client out of the engine". The `notify` node's `email` channel is an HTTPS POST to a provider API (`notifyUrl`/`baseUrl`), rejecting any non-http(s) URL. Email from the cloud = transactional API (Resend/SendGrid/Postmark) over an `http` connection, never SMTP.

The canvas popover renders a "DEPLOY" tag for them.

Rendered in: palette sub-group headings + per-tile pip, properties "MCP server" label, Settings Integrations card title, and the canvas kind badge (`transportGlyph`/`transportFont` on `RendererNode`, painted inside the same pill left of the `mcp-tool` text, with `bw` widened by `transportW` or the text overflows the pill).
- 2026-08-07 - Settings -> Integrations filtered on `envSchema.length > 0`, which silently EXCLUDED every OAuth preset (an OAuth credential is an interactive session, so `envSchema` is empty). The canvas warning's "Configure in Settings - Integrations" deep-link (`#integration-{presetId}`) then landed on a page with no trace of the server it was complaining about - the reported "I don't see it in the list". - 2026-08-25 - Angular 20 `resource().value()` THROWS (`ResourceValueError`) while the resource is in its error state, so `viewStateOf({ loading: r.isLoading(), error: r.error(), value: r.value() })` throws during change detection on any failed request instead of resolving to `failed` - the object literal evaluates `value` eagerly, so the precedence inside `viewStateOf` never gets a chance. All five `admin/` views shipped with that bare read and their failed state plus retry control never rendered; the guard is `value: r.hasValue() ? r.value() : undefined` (`hasValue()` is false in the error state and stays false through a reload from it). Harness notes from that file: answering a request needs TWO rounds of `detectChanges()` + a macrotask (the first delivers the answer to the resource, the second renders the state), the trend mounts run with `DeferBlockBehavior.Manual` so a 100-iteration property does not load and tear down chart.js each time (the plot is asserted on `chartData()`, since `UIChart` paints into a canvas with nothing readable in the DOM), and generated group labels must be whitespace-free and distinct - `GroupTable` tracks `@for` by label, so a duplicate is an Angular error rather than a view defect.

- 2026-08-25 - A Clerk-authorized Worker route CAN be tested end to end under Miniflare with no Clerk account and no stub: generate an RSA keypair in the test, bind the public PEM as `CLERK_JWT_KEY` (plus any non-empty `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`, which only selects the branch), and sign RS256 JWTs with the private half. `@clerk/backend` then verifies OFFLINE - no JWKS fetch, real `verifyRequest`, real allowlist check. Constraints: the key must be **RSA 2048 with exponent 65537** because `loadClerkJwkFromPem` extracts the modulus by string-stripping the standard SPKI prefix/suffix; the payload needs `sub`, `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`; and `exp`/`iat` are checked against the in-isolate `Date.now`, so mint them around the harness's virtual clock, not the wall clock. This is what makes the 200/400/404/405/500 answers of `/api/admin/telemetry/*` reachable in `cloud/test/telemetry-admin.test.mjs` - an open BYO worker only ever reaches 401 and 403, because `verifyRequest` hands an anonymous context (null `userId`) to a worker with no secrets and a null id is never allowlisted. Two more traps there: an `OPTIONS` request never reaches the Admin_API (the generic CORS branch in `index.ts` sits above the `/api/*` chain), so it is out of scope for "every admin response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`"; and a FLAT cross product of routes x methods x tokens x ranges almost never produces a 200 or a 404, because 401 and 403 swallow any method and any tail - generate the ANSWER CLASS first, then an input that produces it, and assert the expected status alongside the header.
- 2026-08-26 - `cloud`'s `test:unit` chain now runs FOUR Miniflare suites back to back and `telemetry-ingest` flaked once at iteration 94 with `TypeError: fetch failed -> connect EADDRINUSE 127.0.0.1:<port>`. Cause is the harness, not the worker: `Miniflare#dispatchFetch` sets `reset: true` on every runtime request (`DispatchFetchDispatcher.dispatch`), so its internal undici `Pool` never keeps a connection alive - one request, one socket, 120s in TIME_WAIT on Windows. Measured 8.9k to 12.7k sockets in TIME_WAIT across consecutive chains against a ~16k ephemeral range. A keep-alive dispatcher is NOT reachable from the test: `dispatchFetch` overwrites `init.dispatcher` with its own before calling undici, so any agent you pass is discarded, and rebuilding the request by hand means reproducing miniflare's internal `MF-Original-URL` / CF-blob headers. The fix is `withLoopbackRetry` (`cloud/test/miniflare-loopback.mjs`), which patches `dispatchFetch` on the instance so every call site is covered by one edit at the worker factory, and retries ONLY an error whose cause chain carries `EADDRINUSE`/`EADDRNOTAVAIL` on a replayable (string or absent) body. Safe because a connect failure happens before any byte reaches workerd, so a retry cannot double-write; `ECONNRESET` is deliberately NOT retried (it can mean workerd died). Do not solve this by lowering `numRuns` - the floor is 100.
- 2026-08-25 - `corsHeaders` in `cloud/src/index.ts` answers an UNLISTED origin with the FIRST entry of `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (`list.includes(o) ? o : list[0]`), not with no header and not with `*`. So a new browser origin does not fail as "CORS header missing" - it fails as "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:7322 does not match", which reads like a misconfigured client. The admin dashboard's dev server (7323) needed adding to that list under `env.hosted` next to the studio's 7322; the list change only reaches production on a `wrangler deploy --env hosted`, but a local `wrangler dev --env hosted` picks it up immediately from the committed config.
- 2026-08-25 - Verify what the HOSTED worker is actually running before debugging an authorization or route problem against it. `GET /status.json` reports `build` (the package version) and its component list, and `OPTIONS /telemetry` reveals route order: an `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` of the `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` head instead of `*` means the request fell through to the generic OPTIONS branch, so the telemetry routes are not in that build. Caught the hosted worker sitting on `0.2.0-beta.9` with eight status components (no `telemetry` store) while the repo was on beta.10 - `/api/admin/telemetry/*` answered a bodiless 404 and D1 migration `0002_telemetry.sql` was still unapplied, so setting `TELEMETRY_ADMIN_USER_IDS` alone would have changed nothing.
- 2026-08-26 - "No telemetry in the admin console" was a CLIENT bug, and the way to find it was to read the installed app's real `localStorage` off disk rather than reason about the code. WebView2 keeps it at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\com.phorma.agentstudio\EBWebView\Default\Local Storage\leveldb`; read the `.ldb`/`.log` bytes as Latin-1 (`[System.Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(28591)`) and regex for `phorma\.telemetry\.` - keys and JSON survive snappy compression well enough to read. The decisive evidence was an ABSENT key: `phorma.telemetry.upload` is written only by `applyIngestOutcome`, so no `nextAttemptAt` anywhere on disk proves no upload was ever ATTEMPTED, which rules out network, CORS, ingest URL and rejection in one step. Root cause: `defaultUploadState` armed the gate at `now + 15min` on every cold start, and since the record is not persisted until an attempt happens, every restart re-armed it - an install used in sessions shorter than 15 minutes uploaded literally never. Fixed to `now`; the gate is still re-armed after every attempt, which is what 4.3/5.4 actually require.
- 2026-08-26 - Before blaming the client for a missing-data report, prove the server half in two commands: `Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post https://cloud.phorma-labs.com/telemetry` with a valid Rollup (expect `200 {}`), then `npx wrangler d1 execute phorma-cloud --env hosted --remote --command "SELECT ... FROM telemetry_rollups"`. Delete the probe row afterwards or it shows up in the dashboard as a real install.
- 2026-09-02 - `CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES` was NEVER set on the hosted worker (absent from `wrangler.jsonc` and from its secret header), so the `azp` check was silently skipped in production while `.dev.vars.example` implied it was configured. It is now a `var` under `env.hosted`, holding the SAME origin set as `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. Two facts worth keeping: `@clerk/backend`'s `assertAuthorizedPartiesClaim` returns early when `azp` is falsy OR the list is empty and otherwise matches by EXACT string, so an incomplete list is a hard 401 per origin, not a degradation - and the SDK already warns that a token with no `azp` will be rejected in a future version, so the skip is not a resting place. Second: Tauri v2's Windows and Android webview origin is `http://tauri.localhost`; the `https://` form is v1 behaviour and now needs `app.windows.useHttpsScheme`, which `tauri.conf.json` does not set. `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` carried only the `https://` form, so Windows desktop CORS was pointed at the wrong scheme; both forms are now listed in both vars. A `vars` change needs `wrangler deploy --env hosted` to take effect.
- 2026-09-02 - `CLERK_JWT_KEY`, not `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`, is what actually verifies session tokens on the hosted worker. `@clerk/backend` 3.10.0's `verifyToken` branches `if (options.jwtKey) loadClerkJwkFromPem(...) else if (options.secretKey) loadClerkJWKFromRemote(...)` - so with the PEM set the secret key is never used for verification and no JWKS is fetched. Worse, `loadClerkJwkFromPem` builds the JWK from the PEM's modulus and uses the token's real `kid` only as a cache label (`local-${kid}`), so it never notices that the token came from a different instance: the signature check just fails. Consequence for a dev-to-prod Clerk rotation - rotating `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` alone does NOT move the worker's instance, and a stale `CLERK_JWT_KEY` 401s every production token with a failure that reads exactly like a wrong secret key. Rotate both, in one step.
- 2026-09-07 - A Clerk PRODUCTION instance rejects the Tauri webview outright, and this broke sign-in in the shipped beta.14 desktop build. Clerk enforces origin validation on production instances: a `pk_live_` key only works from origins the instance allows, and `GET https://api.clerk.com/v1/instance` showed `allowed_origins: null` on ours, meaning nothing but the primary domain. The studio's webview origin is `http://tauri.localhost` (Windows, since `app.windows.useHttpsScheme` is unset), so Clerk.js never initialized and no sign-in UI appeared - with NO visible error, because `backend/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` has `tauri = { features = [] }` and Tauri v2 only compiles devtools into a release build when the `devtools` feature is on. It worked in every earlier beta only because those shipped the `pk_test_` DEV key, and dev instances do not enforce this; the `clerk.ts`/`clerk.prod.ts` split is what first pointed a release at production. Fix needs NO rebuild: `PATCH /v1/instance` with `allowed_origins` listing all three `tauri*` forms plus every web origin, because the PATCH REPLACES the array and a partial list silently locks out whatever you left off - the `phorma-admin` dashboard also ships `pk_live_` and belongs in it. Clerk documents this as the mechanism for non-web origins (its own examples are `chrome-extension://` and Electron's `http://localhost:3000`), so a non-HTTPS desktop origin is fine once allowlisted. Keep the list in step with the worker's `CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES`: same origin set, two different gates. Lesson beyond Clerk: task 1.7 of the stripe-billing spec was "confirm the rotation with `/api/me` and a production session token" and it sat BLOCKED for the whole spec because no production build existed to mint one - that unverifiable check was exactly the one that would have caught this, so a blocked verification step is a release risk, not a formality.
- 2026-09-02 - `/status.json` is doubly blind to a Clerk instance mismatch, which is why the spec forbids using it to confirm a rotation. `probeAuth` sends `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` to `GET api.clerk.com/v1/jwks`, branches only on the HTTP status, and `drain()`s the body - and `/v1/jwks` answers 200 with whichever instance's JWKS the key belongs to, so a `sk_test_` and a `sk_live_` key are indistinguishable there. It also never touches `CLERK_JWT_KEY`. Instance identity IS checkable with no secret at all: each instance publishes `/.well-known/jwks.json` (dev `flowing-seahorse-72.clerk.accounts.dev` -> kid `ins_3G423Qf7eueo3Nd2xNmkyN9hZUd`, prod `clerk.phorma-labs.com` -> kid `ins_3Ikjqi3cLDAikti4i88ZiNEgMIA`). Decode a session token's header `kid` to see which instance minted it; compare a PEM's base64 modulus against the JWKS `n` to see which instance a `CLERK_JWT_KEY` belongs to. `/api/me` with a real token stays the only end-to-end proof.

Caught two drifts this way: the hosted worker was running build `0.2.0-beta.13` (tag `c3e2eee`, NOT an ancestor of `main`, tree was on beta.12), and it carries a live `TELEMETRY_K_ANONYMITY_DISABLED=true` var. A rebase that resolved this hunk by taking the billing side would have silently dropped a deliberate setting. Read the incoming side of a `vars` conflict before assuming your own branch is the newer truth.)

- 2026-09-02 - `cloud/migrations/` convention is ONE file per concern, not per table (`0001_init` = whole tenancy schema, `0002_telemetry` = whole telemetry store). Consequence for a multi-task migration: wrangler records a migration as applied by FILENAME, so anything appended to a file AFTER a remote apply silently never runs. Finish the file, then apply. A SINGLE scalar `billing_event_at` cannot gate every subscription-state write, because the event families do not carry the same information: `invoice.*` and `customer.subscription.deleted` RESTATE the tier they read off the row, while `customer.subscription.created` / `.updated` / a checkout session SUPPLY it off a price. A restating event that arrived first advanced the watermark and censored the older, not-yet-delivered supplying event, losing the supplied tier for good - repro `subscription.updated`(pro) at t plus `invoice.payment_failed` at t+1 delivered BACKWARDS ended `starter`/`past_due`, breaking requirement 18, on a pairing Stripe emits a second apart and orders never. The fix is ONE CLOCK PER FIELD (`billing_tier_at`, `billing_status_at`, `billing_dunning_at` + `billing_dunning_status`), each a monotone MAX, so every field is a last-writer-wins register over the event SET rather than the delivery order; `billing_event_at` survives as AUDIT ONLY and nothing may gate on it. Three things that are easy to get wrong here. (1) `status` needs TWO clocks, not one: a cancellation must overrule an `invoice.paid` carrying a HIGHER timestamp (a paid invoice for a deleted subscription entitles nobody) while still losing to a genuine later resubscription, which is a two-dimensional comparison - so `status` is a FOLD of a lifecycle register and a dunning register, and the invoice register is recorded even when the fold ignores it, or the stored state depends on arrival order again. (2) The fold lives in `upsertTenant`'s `ON CONFLICT` CASE, not in TypeScript around a read, so concurrent deliveries converge without a transaction. (3) A stale event still PERFORMS its write - the clocks refuse the stale fields individually - because skipping it is what lost the write-once buyer email whenever a checkout arrived after a newer event. Rejected alternatives, both plausible and both wrong: "a restating write does not advance the watermark at all" leaves two racing invoices divergent (`inv-failed@t` then `inv-paid@t+1` delivered backwards ends `past_due`) since a restating event DOES supply a status; and "resolve the tier from Stripe at write time" costs a round trip plus a new 502 path on every dunning event, makes the write depend on wall-clock Stripe state rather than the event, and fixes neither the email nor the cancellation case.

What DOES dominate that harness's runtime is the number of D1 round trips: `stripe-webhook`'s property went from 83s to 25s purely by replacing a per-event `SELECT` with one `WHERE id IN (...)`.
