- 2026-09-03 - `wrangler d1 execute --file --remote` is NOT a way to run a query: it takes D1's IMPORT path, uploads the file, and answers with a summary row ("Total queries executed", "Rows read") instead of the query's rows - and `meta.changes` comes back 1 for a statement that changed nothing. A read reads as one row of undefined columns and a write reports success it did not have. Use `--command` (one argv entry through `spawnSync`, no shell, so no quoting problem) and refuse a semicolon in the rendered SQL, because `--command` splits on `;` before SQLite sees it. Separately, `--local --json` reports `meta: { duration }` with NO `changes`, while `--remote` carries the real count, so anything reading `meta.changes` (`TenantStore.setRuntimeKey`) cannot be rehearsed locally.
- 2026-09-09 - "No telemetry in the admin dashboard" after the dev-to-production Clerk switch was ONE stale secret, and the diagnosis is worth reusing because four layers produce nearly the same screen. `TELEMETRY_ADMIN_USER_IDS` still held the DEV instance's user id; Clerk user ids are per-instance, `isOperator` is an exact match, so every production session read 403. Then the fix was applied as a JSON ARRAY (`["user_a","user_b"]`), which ALSO fails closed - the secret is split on commas, so the entries keep their brackets and quotes and match nothing. Two cheap discriminators. (1) Clerk user ids carry the instance prefix: dev instance `ins_3G423...` mints `user_3G4...`, prod `ins_3Ikjqi...` mints `user_3Iz...`, so a `user_3G4...` id in a production allowlist is visibly the wrong instance. (2) Read the layer off the dashboard's network tab - NO request at all means Clerk never minted a session on that origin, 401 means the worker verifies a different instance or the origin is missing from `CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES`, 403 means verified-but-not-allowlisted, and a 200 full of zeros means the data layer. A secret change needs no redeploy.
- 2026-09-09 - Probing a Clerk PRODUCTION instance's origin policy needs NO secret key, which makes it the first check to run when a `pk_live_` surface behaves as though it is signed out. `POST https://<frontend-api-host>/v1/client/sign_ins?_clerk_js_version=5.0.0` with `Origin: <candidate>` and body `strategy=`. THREE verdicts, not two, and the third was a surprise worth the entry: **422 `form_param_nil`** = authorized (it got as far as validating the form); **`origin_invalid`** = an unrelated origin, refused; and **403 `subdomain_not_allowed`** ("The request origin subdomain is not in the allowed subdomains list") = a SUBDOMAIN OF THE PRIMARY CLERK DOMAIN that has not been allowlisted. So a production instance governs `phorma-labs.com` subdomains through a SEPARATE allowed-subdomains list rather than through `allowed_origins`, and a `PATCH /v1/instance` on `allowed_origins` does NOT cover them - `telemetry-admin.phorma-labs.com` answered `subdomain_not_allowed` while `phorma-admin.phorma-agent-studio.workers.dev` answered 422. Always include a junk origin as a CONTROL in the same run, or a uniform answer reads as a pass. Watch the rate limit: a 429 mid-probe looks exactly like a refusal, so space the calls a few seconds apart. On Windows PowerShell 5.1 use `curl.exe -w "HTTPSTATUS:%{http_code}"`; `Invoke-WebRequest -SkipHttpErrorCheck` does not exist there and the loop dies on the first non-2xx.

- 2026-09-09 - Two Windows gotchas that made a wrangler read look like an auth failure, both worth recognising before chasing a permissions problem. (1) This shell garbles wrangler's stdout to the point of printing nothing at all, including for commands that succeed; redirecting to a file did not help either. The reliable form is a tiny node helper that `spawnSync`s wrangler's own JS entry - `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('wrangler/bin/wrangler.js')` and `process.execPath` - which also passes `--command` as a single argv entry so there is no shell quoting at all. (2) Do NOT `spawnSync('npx.cmd', ...)`: Node 20+ refuses to spawn a `.cmd` without `shell: true` (CVE-2024-27980) and returns `status: null` with no error printed, which reads exactly like a killed process. Resolve the JS entry instead. Separately, a `d1 execute --remote` answered `7403 "The given account is not valid or is not authorized"` once and then worked on retry with the same token and the same account - so treat a lone 7403 as transient and retry before re-authenticating. And `$args` is a reserved PowerShell automatic variable: assigning to it fails `Start-Process -ArgumentList` validation with a null-element error.
- 2026-09-09 - `fc.assert` over an `fc.asyncProperty` returns a PROMISE, and not awaiting it is silent and total. A `property()` helper that called `fc.assert(build(), {...})` without `await` printed PASS immediately for all three properties and left them running in the background, past the end of the file and past `mf.dispose()`, surfacing only as an unhandled "Attempted to use poisoned stub" rejection while the suite reported green and exited 0. Any helper wrapping `fc.assert` for async properties must be `async` and must `await`. Second half of the same lesson: report the WHOLE fast-check message, not `message.split('\n')[0]` - the first line is only "Property failed after N tests" and throws away the counterexample and the thrown cause, which is the entire diagnostic.
- 2026-09-09 - A new D1-backed Miniflare suite is a SOCKET BUDGET decision, not just a test. `cloud/test/billing-admin.test.mjs` passed in isolation at 400 iterations and failed at iteration 12 inside the full `test:unit` chain, because it ran straight after `billing-routes` and inherited a drained Windows ephemeral range - the documented "the visible failure lands in the innocent suite" shape, and it cost a debugging cycle looking for an arithmetic bug that did not exist. Two fixes, both required: an `await-port-drain.mjs` barrier BEFORE the suite in `test:unit`, and `DB.batch([...])` instead of a loop of `run()` calls for per-iteration setup (`getD1Database` costs one socket PER STATEMENT, so five DELETEs plus eight INSERTs per iteration is ~975 sockets across 75 iterations that one batch each reduces to 150). `withLoopbackRetryD1` wraps `batch` and unwraps each statement's `__inner`, so batching keeps the retry protection.
- 2026-09-09 - Rendering and SCREENSHOTTING a worker-served HTML page found three defects that every markup assertion in two suites was blind to, and all three were invisible in code review. (1) A backtick inside a CSS comment inside a template literal terminated the string; esbuild reported "Expected ; but found box" ~40 lines away. (2) `document.querySelector('#title span')` matched the STATE DOT rather than the heading text, because the `<h1>` holds the dot as its first span - so the runtime state swap wrote a heading into an 8px circle, leaving the old heading visible and the new one overflowing beside it. Only a screenshot shows that; the markup was correct and only the selector was wrong. (3) "sign-in" broke across lines as "sign-" / "in." because browsers break at an ordinary hyphen - fixed with `&#8209;`. Technique: a throwaway `tsx` script that calls the page handlers and writes their HTML to disk, then `chrome.exe --headless --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --window-size=W,H --screenshot=out.png --virtual-time-budget=2500 file:///...`. `--virtual-time-budget` runs the page's own script, so the device page's bootstrap fails to find `window.Clerk` and lands on its error state - which exercises the state swap for free. Delete the scratch files afterwards.
- 2026-09-03 - A key-minting migration is made re-runnable by two independent levers, not by a ledger: the STORED HASH read back from the vendor (`workspace_id` on the key object says whether that tenant is done, and it cannot disagree with reality the way local bookkeeping can), plus the DETERMINISTIC KEY NAME (`phorma-tenant-{id}`, now `runtimeKeyName()`), which is the ONLY handle on a key that was minted and then not stored - the plaintext is returned exactly once, so such a key can never be adopted and is invisible otherwise. Sweep same-name keys that are not the stored hash and disable them BEFORE minting, and a crash between mint and store costs one dead key rather than a live one nobody can account for. `cloud/test/workspace-migration.test.mjs` fails on "2 live keys in the target workspace" the moment that sweep is removed.
- 2026-09-03 - A rotation must purge the KV tenant cache or the worker keeps handing runs a key that was just disabled for up to the 60s TTL. `TenantStore.setRuntimeKey` deletes `tenant:{id}` when a `TENANTS` binding is present; an operator script has no bindings, so it needs `wrangler kv key delete tenant:<id> --binding TENANTS --env hosted --remote` after each mint. Same hazard exists on `/api/provision --rotateKey` today.
- 2026-09-03 - `getD1Database` costs one loopback socket PER STATEMENT, exactly like `dispatchFetch` - measured: 300 proxied `run()` calls leave 306 sockets in TIME_WAIT, and a keep-alive global undici dispatcher changes nothing because the magic proxy builds its own pool. So "this suite never dispatches a fetch" exempts nothing, and the in-process billing suites are the BIGGEST consumers in the chain (~12,800 sockets, `entitlement` ~4,700 and `stripe-webhook` ~7,100, since every statement the worker code issues crosses the proxy too) against a Windows ephemeral range of 16,384 held for 2 minutes. That drained the range and failed `telemetry-ingest`'s property on `connect EADDRINUSE` two suites later - the visible failure lands in the innocent suite, so read a port-exhaustion failure as a whole-chain budget problem, not a bug in the suite that reported it. Fix is `withLoopbackRetryD1` on every `getD1Database` handle plus `test:unit` order that runs the D1-heavy billing suites LAST; never lower iteration counts to buy it back.
- 2026-09-03 - Those two measures are NOT enough once the whole billing block is in the chain, and `cloud`'s `test:unit` could not complete on a stock Windows range at all: `stripe-webhook` failed at iteration 60 of 120 on `connect EADDRINUSE`, reproducibly, with nothing else running. The retry wrappers cannot cover it because their ladder tops out at ~22s while TIME_WAIT is 120s - they survive a transient shortage, not an empty range. Measured with `(netstat -ano -p tcp | Select-String 'TIME_WAIT').Count`: `stripe-webhook` needs ~7,050 sockets and passes ALONE, but inherits only ~2,500 free ports from `tenant-billing` + `entitlement` + `billing-routes`. So prevent the wall instead of retrying through it - `cloud/test/await-port-drain.mjs` polls until 10,000 ports are free (capped at 180s, then proceeds), and `test:unit` calls it before `stripe-webhook` and before `provisioning`. It is a NO-OP off Windows, which is exactly why CI was always green while local was unrunnable: `ubuntu-22.04` has 28,232 ports on a 60s recycle, ~4x the budget. Corollary for a verification sweep: do NOT run the cloud chain next to a karma run or anything else socket-hungry, and never diagnose one of these by trusting a single green CI run.
- 2026-09-07 - Two traps when writing an operator script in this repo, both found the hard way in `cloud/scripts/setup-local-dev.mjs`. (1) End with `process.exitCode = code`, NEVER `process.exit(code)`. On Windows `process.exit()` raced libuv's teardown of the console handles the script had touched and died with `Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c` and exit code `0xC0000409` (`-1073740791`) - AFTER every side effect had landed and the whole summary had printed. So the run genuinely succeeded and only the exit status was wrong, which is precisely what a wrapper or a CI step reads. Setting the code and returning also guarantees buffered stdout flushes. (2) The `npm test -- --watch=false` flag-forwarding failure is NOT specific to the Angular scripts: npm 10 and 11 swallow ANY unrecognised `--flag` after `npm run <script>` as their own config, warn `Unknown cli config`, and hand the script only the bare positionals - so `npm run dev:setup -- --tenant user_x --tier team` invoked the script with `user_x team` and it aborted on "Unknown argument". Any script that takes flags must be invoked as `node scripts/<name>.mjs --flag`, and its `--help` must say so rather than repeating the `--` folklore.

- 2026-09-07 - `wrangler d1 migrations apply` records a migration by FILENAME, and the LOCAL database is where that bites hardest, because a migration file is edited repeatedly while it is being written. Symptom: `d1_migrations` listed all four migrations, `tenants` carried every column from `0003_billing.sql`'s `ALTER`s AND `0004`'s, and yet `credit_grants` and `stripe_events` did not exist - an early apply ran the `ALTER`s that existed at the time, stamped `0003_billing.sql` as done, and the `CREATE TABLE`s appended later never ran. Nothing complains until a webhook inserts a grant and hits `no such table`, long after the setup looked successful. So do not trust `d1_migrations` as evidence: check `sqlite_master` for the tables the migration was supposed to create. On a local DB the fix is free - `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .wrangler/state/v3/d1` with the worker STOPPED (it holds the file open), then re-apply, and 0003 reports its real 9 commands. `wrangler dev` and `wrangler d1 execute --local` share one file under `.wrangler/state/v3/d1/miniflare-D1DatabaseObject`, so there is no split-brain to chase. Fastest way to inspect it when the shell swallows wrangler's output: `node:sqlite`'s `DatabaseSync` in `readOnly` mode against that file directly.
- 2026-09-04 - Any test that applies `cloud/migrations/*.sql` by hand must split on `/\r?\n/`, never `'\n'`. `core.autocrlf=true` (no `.gitattributes` in this repo) rewrites every migration with CRLF on checkout, and against a line still carrying its `\r` the comment stripper `/--.*$/` matches NOTHING - `.` will not cross `\r` and `$` sits after it - so every `--` comment survives the split, and the comment-only tail after the last `;` reaches D1 as `D1_ERROR: SQL code did not contain a statement`. Six suites carried the same `statementsOf` copy (`tenant-billing`, `entitlement`, `billing-routes`, `stripe-webhook`, `provisioning`, `workspace-migration`) and all six are fixed. It stayed hidden until a rebase: the files had LF while they were being written in-session, and only a real `git checkout` normalized them - so "it was green an hour ago" is not evidence here.
- 2026-09-07 - A Clerk PRODUCTION instance CANNOT sign anyone in from the Tauri webview, and no Clerk Dashboard setting fixes it. Measured in Chromium at the real origin (`http://tauri.localhost:80`, real prod bundle, CDP-instrumented): a production instance identifies the client with `__client=<jwt>; Domain=clerk.phorma-labs.com; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`, `tauri.localhost` is a different registrable domain, so Chromium (a) REFUSES TO STORE it (`blockedReasons: ["SchemefulSameSiteLax"]`) and (b) refuses to SEND it even when planted with `Network.setCookie` - clerk-js then gets a fresh anonymous client on every FAPI call. Google therefore returns to `/v1/oauth_callback` with no client, which 301s to `?err_code=authorization_invalid` and serves 403 `{"code":"authorization_invalid"}` as a dead-end page IN the app window. The decisive control was already in the capture: Cloudflare's `SameSite=None` cookies were stored from the SAME response that had Clerk's `Lax` ones rejected, so the discriminator is cross-site-ness, NOT the scheme. Two dead ends, do not re-propose: `Clerk.load({standardBrowser:false})` (clerk-js 5.127.2 hardcodes `credentials:'include'` in BOTH load paths - the browser bundle has no token transport; that lives in `/headless` + a `tokenCache`), and `app.windows.useHttpsScheme` (changes the scheme, not the site). A DEVELOPMENT instance is exempt and that is why this shipped: `auth_config.cookieless_dev` is true and the client rides the URL as `__clerk_db_jwt`, so `ng serve` and a dev desktop shell both work. This bug is UNREACHABLE from any dev-instance build - a dev-instance pass proves nothing about it. Interim fix shipped: desktop `signIn()` opens the Account Portal via `openExternal` and says the app will still read signed out. Real fix specced at `.kiro/specs/desktop-signin-handoff/` - and it is tractable only because `PHORMA_CLOUD_DEFAULT_URL` is `https://cloud.phorma-labs.com`, i.e. the worker is already SAME-SITE with `clerk.phorma-labs.com`, so a worker-served page runs clerk-js first-party with no new DNS.

Cloudflare documents the opt-out: `Cache-Control: no-transform` stops the proxy modifying the payload (same mechanism their own FAQ cites for "automatic setup is not working" when a site sets `public, no-transform`). - 2026-09-08 - MINOR OPEN DEFECT on the release routes, found by working the beta.19 playbook: `handleReleaseRequest` (`cloud/src/releases.ts`) gates on `if (request.method !== 'GET') return null`, so a **HEAD** request to `/download/stable/<version>/<file>` falls through to the agent router and 404s while the identical GET answers 200 with the real 8.4MB installer. Harmless to the Tauri updater (it GETs) and to browsers, but it makes HEAD useless as a cheap liveness probe - which is exactly what a verification step reaches for first, so the 404 reads as a missing artifact and sends you to debug R2 for nothing. Probe a release asset with `-Method Get ... -MaximumRedirection 0` and read `RawContentLength`, or accept the full download. Worth fixing by admitting HEAD (Workers returns a bodiless response for HEAD automatically), not worth its own release. Also note the download slugs are NOT the updater's target strings: the website route takes `windows-x64` / `macos-arm64` / `macos-intel` / `linux-appimage` / `linux-deb` (`DOWNLOAD_PLATFORM_MAP`), while the updater path takes `windows/x86_64` style (`updaterPlatformKey`) - guessing `windows` or `linux` on the download route 404s and looks like a broken release.

(1) `vitest`'s `hookTimeout` is a SEPARATE setting from `testTimeout` and defaults to **10s**, so `cloud-aws/vitest.config.ts` raising `testTimeout` to 90s with a comment explaining that 30s "sat close enough to the edge to flake" did nothing for the three `src/infra` suites that synthesize CDK in a `beforeAll` - they each carried a hardcoded `}, 30_000)` instead, and `iam-assertions.spec.ts` timed out REPRODUCIBLY on Windows/Node 24 while all 25 of its assertions passed the moment the hook had room. A hook timeout failure reads exactly like a broken assertion (vitest points at the `beforeAll` line), so distinguish them by re-running with `--hookTimeout=180000` BEFORE debugging the test. Fixed by setting `hookTimeout: 90_000` once in the config and deleting all three literals. (2) `check-deploy-bundle.mjs` failed on `cloud/dist-hosted/`, which is what `wrangler deploy --env hosted --outdir=dist-hosted` leaves behind - gitignored by `cloud/dist*/`, so it exists only on a machine that has deployed the hosted worker and never in CI. That is the exact shape `GENERATED` exists for, and it needed an entry in BOTH `NOT_BUNDLED` (a reason) and `GENERATED` (skip the liveness check), or the guard fails on a developer machine and passes in CI. (3) Running `npm install` in `cloud-aws/` on Windows STRIPS the Linux-only `libc: ["glibc"|"musl"]` metadata from `package-lock.json` (33 deletions) - platform churn that must be reverted with `git checkout --`, never committed, or a Linux CI runner loses the optional-dependency discrimination.

Harmless TODAY only because every workflow uses `npm install` and `check-versions.mjs` reads `package.json` only - it becomes a hard break the moment any workflow switches to `npm ci`, which fails outright on a lock/manifest version mismatch. Do not fix it inside a release; it is its own change. Also worth knowing for local verification: `nvm install` on this machine silently NO-OPS without elevation (prints nothing, `nvm list` unchanged), so the way to run the Node-24-only `cloud` suites locally is a portable unzip - `Invoke-WebRequest https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.8.0/node-v24.8.0-win-x64.zip`, `Expand-Archive`, then prepend it to `$env:PATH` for that one command. The prod instance has **Enable allowed subdomains** ON, so the default "any subdomain of the root domain is accepted" that the handoff design explicitly relied on ("no new Clerk `allowed_origins` entry", requirements.md) did not hold. Probe it per-origin with the existing `POST /v1/client/sign_ins` + empty `strategy=` trick: `phorma-labs.com`, `www.`, `accounts.` and `http://tauri.localhost` all answered 422 (authorized) while `cloud.` answered 403. Second, real defect found in the same console output: clerk-js 5.127.2 builds a `Worker` from a `blob:` URL, and `worker-src` FALLS BACK to `script-src` when absent, which does not admit `blob:` - so `/auth/device` logged a CSP violation on every load. Fixed with a separate `worker-src blob:` directive, never by adding `blob:` to `script-src` (that would also let a blob run as a top-level script on the page that handles sign-in). The third console line, `cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js` blocked, is Cloudflare Web Analytics auto-injecting into a worker HTML response; the block is correct and harmless. Lesson beyond Clerk: this shipped because the design recorded "no new allowed_origins entry needed" as a FACT about Clerk's defaults without probing the specific origin the new code would use - an assumption about a third-party default is only evidence once measured against the actual instance.

- 2026-09-09 - Operator cost visibility shipped: `/api/admin/billing/{costs,revenue}` plus a Spend view in `admin/`. The durable rules are in the `cloud-worker` steering; what belongs here is WHY it exists and the three findings behind it. (1) Nothing in this repo has ever funded the OpenRouter account - every vendor write is a `limit` on a key, which is permission to draw down a PREPAID balance, and OpenRouter has no card-based credits-purchase API (the Coinbase Commerce charge endpoint their docs once carried is deprecated). So a $20 subscription raising a key's cap to starter's $4 is an entitlement, not a transfer, and topping up is a manual dashboard action permanently. (2) A dry account was completely undetectable: `status.ts`'s `probeInference` fetches `/api/v1/credits` and then `drain()`s the body unread, so it only branches on the HTTP status and a zero balance answers 200 and reads green - the first symptom being `/api/infer` forwarding a 402 to a paying tenant whose own quota says they are fine. Its docstring claimed it read the balance; corrected. (3) The documented 75-80 percent margin was measured against the CAP, never against invoiced vendor cost or collected revenue, so it was an intent rather than a figure - and it ignored Stripe's processing fee entirely. The revenue route now measures gross, tax, fee, net, our metered model cost and the resulting margin from real Stripe reads. Deliberately NOT surfaced on `/status.json`: that badge is on a public footer, and a low balance is a business fact rather than an outage.
- 2026-09-09 - Two D1 states that look like bugs and are not, both now surfaced by the Spend view's attention lists rather than being invisible. A `canceled` or `past_due` tenant KEEPS both `openrouter_key_*` columns - `disableTenantRuntimeKey` patches the vendor and deliberately does not null them - so a populated hash after a cancellation is the expected steady state, and since there is no `GET /keys/{hash}` call anywhere in the worker, that list is the one to spot-check against the OpenRouter dashboard rather than a leak report. Separately, an `active` tenant with no `openrouter_key_enc` is the `no_runtime_key` population: entitled by their row and refused on every run.
- 2026-09-14 - Deployment reconciliation + cloud backup shipped (`.kiro/specs/cloud-workflow-backup/`); the durable rules live in the `cloud-worker` and `structure` steering. What belongs here is the failure that caused it and the three things that surprised us. The trigger: a user reinstalled, the IndexedDB holding their library went with it, and a workflow deployed to Phorma Cloud stayed live - cron firing, portal answering, credits spending - with NOBODY able to name it, because a Durable Object namespace cannot be enumerated and the only copy of its `workflowId` was in the wiped database. (1) `workflowKey()` reads `state.spec?.id` FIRST, so `DELETE /workflow` must resolve the workflow id BEFORE `setState({spec: null})` or the deregister aims at the literal string `default`. (2) The registry backfill has to run on ANY wake, not only a hosted one: a BYO install needs the same list for its `deployments.json` export, and the cost is one storage read on an instance that is already awake. (3) `GET /api/deployments` sits ABOVE the `store.enabled` gate while `/api/backups/*` sits below it, and the asymmetry is the whole design - the registry is in a DO that BYO binds too, so "I cannot tell you what it cost" (null spend) is acceptable where "I cannot tell you what is running" is not.
- 2026-09-14 - Backup encryption order is `gzip` THEN AES-GCM, never the reverse: ciphertext does not compress, so encrypting first stores every workflow at full size forever (measured - a 40-node spec came out under half its plaintext size the right way round). That needed `encryptBytes`/`decryptBytes` beside `encryptString` in `tenants.ts`, because pushing a gzip stream through the string pair means base64 in and base64 out, 1.78x the compressed size in R2. Same 12-byte-IV-prefix packing, so the two pairs stay one format. Also: `BACKUPS` is a SEPARATE R2 bucket from `RELEASES` on purpose - that one serves public installer downloads through unauthenticated routes, and private customer workflows in it would be one routing mistake away from being served.
- 2026-09-14 - `new URL()` normalizes a path segment before any route guard sees it: a literal `..` AND `%2e%2e` (it percent-decodes unreserved characters) are both RESOLVED AWAY, so `/api/backups/..` becomes `/api/` and 404s rather than reaching a workflow-id regex. `%2F` is NOT decoded and does survive into `pathname`, so that is the form a key-segment guard actually has to refuse. Asserting a 400 for `..` looks right and tests nothing.
- 2026-09-14 - The workflow-backup change left a STRAY top-level `r2_buckets` in `cloud/wrangler.jsonc` binding `phorma-backups` as `phorma_backups`. It bound nothing the code reads (`backup-store.ts` reads `env.BACKUPS`, correctly declared under `env.hosted`) while making every BYO deploy demand a bucket the user's account has never had - the exact thing the file's own "no `r2_buckets` here on purpose" note warns about. `cloud/test/deploy-config.test.mjs` caught it and CI on `main` was ALREADY RED for two commits before anyone tried to cut a release. Two lessons: a top-level binding in that file is a BYO regression by default, and a red `main` is a release blocker you should look at BEFORE bumping a version, since `gh run list` shows it in one line. `npm run check`'s dry-run binding list is the cheap confirmation - top level must show the three Durable Objects and nothing else.

A remote bearer token must reach the HTTP request in the webview, so `HttpMcpClient(endpoint, authHeaders)` takes headers and the CALLER resolves the token (keeps engine framework-free). Desktop: narrow Rust command `mcp::get_mcp_bearer(server_id, auth_key, preset_id)` returns ONLY that one secret (node-scoped then preset-scoped). Browser: `SettingsService.resolveMcpBearer` reads localStorage. Cloud: `CloudToolHost({resolveBearer})` maps authKey -> worker secret `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` (e.g. `GITHUB_TOKEN` -> `MCP_GITHUB_TOKEN`).

## Phorma Cloud Model Provider (Local-Run Inference Proxy)

- 2026-07-12 â€” `phorma-cloud` is a new `ModelProviderId` (added to BOTH `engine/src/types.ts` AND `frontend/src/app/core/workflow.model.ts` â€” keep the structural twins in sync). It routes local-run inference through the Phorma Cloud `/api/infer` proxy, billed against the tenant's subscription credits (OpenRouter runtime key). No BYO key needed. Curated models only (stored as full OpenRouter slugs): `openai/gpt-5.5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`, `google/gemini-3.5-flash`.
- 2026-07-12 â€” `ModelTransportService.create()` returns a `CompositeModelClient` that intercepts `request.provider === 'phorma-cloud'` â†’ `PhormaCloudModelClient` (POSTs the engine-built OpenRouter-shaped wire request to `${phormaCloudUrl}/api/infer` with the Clerk session JWT as Bearer; streams SSE back; parses with `createStreamParser({ ...request, provider: 'openrouter' })`). All other providers delegate to the existing Tauri/Fetch BYO path. The engine calls `stream()` per-node with `request.provider`, so the composite branches at runtime â€” no engine changes needed for the routing decision.
- 2026-07-12 â€” Cloud proxy `POST /api/infer` in `cloud/src/api.ts`: verifies Clerk JWT (`verifyRequest`), gates on subscription+quota via shared `resolveHostedInference()` (in `tenants.ts`), injects the tenant runtime key, forwards to OpenRouter, tees the response stream (one copy to the client, one parsed for the `usage` block), meters via `recordRun`. The tenant key NEVER leaves the worker. Security: authenticate every call + enforce quota exactly like `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` (402/429) â€” otherwise it exposes unauthenticated inference on the tenant's key.
- 2026-07-12 â€” CRITICAL GOTCHA (fixed): `/api/infer` metering (`meterInferenceStream`) reads the SECOND tee'd stream copy to extract usage AFTER the client's copy finishes. It MUST run via `ctx.waitUntil(...)`, NOT a bare `void promise.catch()`. Without waitUntil, Cloudflare tears the worker down as soon as the client finishes reading its copy â†’ the metering promise is killed before `recordRun` writes to D1 â†’ usage silently stays at 0 (symptom: Runs panel shows "N credits" for a run but Settings quota bar stays "0 / 1000"). Required threading `ExecutionContext` through `fetch(request, env, ctx)` â†’ `handleApiRequest(..., ctx)` â†’ `routeApiRequest(..., ctx)`. NEEDS WORKER REDEPLOY to take effect (`wrangler deploy --env hosted`).
- 2026-07-12 â€” Post-run quota refresh: `RunControllerService.finishRun()` calls `phormaCloud.refresh()` (after a 1.5s delay to let the waitUntil D1 write land) ONLY when `runUsage().phormaCloud` is true. Before this, the quota bar/account chip only refreshed on dialog-open/sign-in, so a just-completed Phorma Cloud run's spend never showed until you reopened Settings. `RunControllerService` injects `PhormaCloudService` directly â€” safe (no circular DI: PhormaCloudService only injects ClerkService, reads phormaCloudUrl from localStorage not CloudService).
- 2026-07-12 â€” CRITICAL GOTCHA (fixed): `recordRun` had a hardcoded `runs_used + 1` bump, called from BOTH `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` (correct: 1 per deployed workflow run) AND `meterInferenceStream` (the `/api/infer` local-run proxy â€” WRONG). Every local Phorma Cloud inference call (per agent node Ã— per tool-call round) was inflating the monthly run count, so a few local debug runs pushed users to e.g. 7/300. Fix: `recordRun` takes `countsAsRun?: boolean` (default true); the SQL now uses `VALUES(?,?,?,?)` + `runs_used + excluded.runs_used` with a bound `runIncrement` (0 when countsAsRun=false, 1 otherwise). `/api/infer` passes `countsAsRun: false` â€” local runs consume CREDITS (cost) only, never the run allowance. `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` is unchanged (defaults to true). NEEDS WORKER REDEPLOY. Existing inflated `runs_used` rows in D1 don't self-correct â€” reset manually if needed (`UPDATE quotas SET runs_used = 0 WHERE tenant_id=? AND month=?`).
- 2026-07-12 â€” `OPENROUTER_SLUG_PREFIX`, `toOpenRouterModel()`, and `resolveHostedInference()` were lifted from `workflow-agent.ts` into `tenants.ts` as shared exports (the DO + the `/api/infer` proxy both use them). `mapGraphToOpenRouter` in `workflow-agent.ts` handles `phorma-cloud` nodes (prefix `''`, providerâ†’openrouter) so deployed workflows with phorma-cloud nodes work in hosted mode. BYO own-Cloudflare deploy: phorma-cloud errors clearly (no tenant key).
- 2026-07-12 â€” `openAiBody` in `engine/src/model.ts` checks `request.provider === 'openrouter'` for usage accounting (`stream_options.include_usage` + `usage: { include: true }`). Added `phorma-cloud` to those checks so the proxy gets usage/cost data for metering. The `phorma-cloud` adapter in `ADAPTERS` reuses `openAiCompatible('https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions', false)` â€” `requiresKey: false` because the local client never holds a key (the proxy does).
- 2026-07-12 â€” `PhormaCloudService.sessionToken()` is the public method to resolve a fresh Clerk JWT for the proxy (added 2026-07-12). Don't access `clerk.session$` from outside the service â€” it's private. The method returns `null` when signed out.
- 2026-07-12 â€” BYO live model fetch: `ModelTransportService.listModels(provider)` mirrors `listBedrockModels` â€” desktop â†’ Rust `list_provider_models` cmd; browser â†’ direct fetch (CORS best-effort, falls back to free text). Rust `list_provider_models` in `llm.rs` supports anthropic/openai/gemini/openrouter. Gemini uses `?key=` query param; Anthropic uses `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version` header; OpenAI/OpenRouter use Bearer. Registered in `lib.rs` `generate_handler!`.
- 2026-07-12 â€” UI gating: Phorma Cloud provider only appears in the picker when `phormaCloud.subscribed()` is true. In both `prompt-panel.ts` and `settings-dialog.ts`, `providers` changed from a plain array to a `computed()` signal that filters `MODEL_PROVIDERS`. GOTCHA: templates MUST call it as `providers()` not `providers` â€” `ng build` catches this (TS2322: `Signal<...[]>>` not assignable to `any[]`). Phorma Cloud is excluded from `keyedProviders` in settings (no API key needed).
- 2026-08-25 - Every `ModelRequest` built OUTSIDE the run engine must spread `settings.providerEndpoints()` (`ollamaBaseUrl`, `lmstudioBaseUrl`, `bedrockRegion`). `RunControllerService` and `EvalRunnerService` passed all three; the four `ModelRequest` literals in `WorkflowBuilderService` (Ask, Plan turn, Plan palette, Agent loop) and the two in `FieldGenerationService` passed NONE, so the engine silently fell back to `us-east-1` / `localhost`. Symptom: an assistant chat on a Bedrock default model died with `bedrock request failed (400 Bad Request): "The provided model identifier is invalid."` while the identical model ran fine from the canvas - a geographic inference profile (`au.`/`eu.`/`apac.`/`us.`) only resolves in a region inside its own geography, and the URL region is what the adapter builds from `bedrockRegion`. A remote Ollama or LM Studio server was unreachable from the assistant for the same reason.
- 2026-08-25 - Claude Opus 4.7 onward REJECT sampling params: sending `temperature` (or `top_p`/`top_k`) to Sonnet 5, Opus 4.7/4.8/5 or Fable 5 is a hard 400 (`` `temperature` is deprecated for this model ``), and there is no accepted value - the field must be absent. `acceptsSamplingParams(model)` in `engine/src/model.ts` gates all three wire builders (`converseBody`, `anthropicBody`, `openAiBody`) through `wireTemperature`, which returns `undefined` so `JSON.stringify` drops the key. Matched on the MODEL ID, not the provider: the same model arrives as `claude-sonnet-5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `au.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` and `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-20260115-v1:0`. The pattern deliberately does not match `claude-sonnet-4-5`, which rejects only `temperature` AND `top_p` together (the engine never sends `top_p`). Covered by `engine/src/model-sampling.spec.ts`.
- 2026-08-25 - `ModelTransportService.testModel({provider, model})` is the reachability probe behind Settings > Models > Test. It goes through `create()` on purpose, so it exercises the real key resolution, proxy, region and wire format; a probe with its own HTTP path can pass while inference still fails. It sends no `temperature`. Listing a model catalog is NOT a substitute - `list_bedrock_models` / `list_bedrock_inference_profiles` answer per region and say nothing about whether an id is invocable from the configured one. On a Bedrock `ValidationException` the dialog appends the geo-prefix-vs-region hint, which is the actual cause almost every time.

## Usage Credits (abstraction over real USD inference cost)

- 2026-07-12 â€” Phorma Cloud NEVER shows dollars to the user. `TierLimits` now has `monthlyCredits` (round marketing number, the ONLY billing unit displayed) alongside `monthlyCostUsd` (real spend cap â†’ OpenRouter key limit, analytics-only). Base burn = 125 credits/$1 at the ORIGINAL (pre-margin-fix) ratio; higher tiers include a volume bonus (pro +5%, team +10%) baked into a LARGER USD budget so a credit buys more real inference â€” credit numbers stay round regardless of the USD side. Three gotchas found while writing it. (1) With `wrangler dev --env hosted`, wrangler loads `.dev.vars.hosted` INSTEAD of `.dev.vars` and does not merge them, so every var must be repeated in the env-specific file. (2) `cloud/.gitignore`'s bare `.dev.vars` pattern therefore left a REAL secret file (`.dev.vars.hosted`, and `.env.hosted` likewise) fully committable - now `.dev.vars*` / `.env*` with `!.dev.vars.example` as the only exception, verified with `git check-ignore -q` per name (`git check-ignore -v` prints the matching NEGATION pattern too, so "produced output" does not mean "ignored" - use the exit code). (3) `scripts/check-deploy-bundle.mjs` fails on ANY gitignored per-developer top-level file in `cloud/`, because it demands every entry be bundled or in NOT_BUNDLED while NOT_BUNDLED entries must also exist: a `wrangler.byo.jsonc` written by Settings > Cloud already broke that guard on the developer's machine and nowhere else. For a local hosted-mode worker the vars that actually matter are `PHORMA_MODE=hosted`, `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` (`sk_test_`), `KEY_ENC_SECRET`, `PHORMA_ADMIN_TOKEN` and `OPENROUTER_PROVISIONING_KEY`, plus `npx wrangler d1 migrations apply phorma-cloud --env hosted --local` - `/api/infer` spends the tenant's MINTED OpenRouter key, never `env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, so provisioning is a prerequisite for testing it.

- 2026-09-02 - `cloud/src/stripe.ts` is the ONLY place that talks to the Stripe REST API (task 3.1): `encodeStripeForm` (bracket form encoding), `requireStripeSecret` (the 501), `stripeRequest`. Four findings from building it. (1) Stripe QUOTES THE API KEY BACK in its error prose - a bad key answers `Expired API Key provided: sk_test_...` - so anything that logs a Stripe error body must redact the key first; Stripe masks the middle, but with `observability` enabled that log line is durable and the requirement-33 guarantee must not rest on a vendor's masking. A test asserts the redaction, and it CAUGHT the unredacted first version. (2) Never mirror Stripe's HTTP status onto ours - a Stripe 401 means OUR secret key is wrong, and forwarding it makes the studio treat an operator's misconfiguration as an expired user session. Every upstream failure is a 502 carrying only Stripe's snake_case `code`/`type` token (validated against `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/` before it crosses into our body), never the message. (3) `encodeURIComponent` escapes every character with meaning in a form body (`& = + %` and space) but leaves `!'()*` literal where the SDKs' encoder percent-encodes them; both decode identically, and it only shows in Stripe's customer search syntax (`query=metadata%5B'clerk_user_id'%5D%3A'user_1'`). (4) `Stripe-Version` is pinned to `2026-08-26.dahlia` in the module, so upgrading the account's default version in the Dashboard cannot change worker behaviour without a deploy. A blank secret (`wrangler secret put` with an empty line) counts as ABSENT, or `Authorization: Bearer ` reaches Stripe and a config mistake reads as a vendor failure.
- 2026-09-02 - Billing catalogue (task 3.4) is `BILLING_LOOKUP_KEYS` + `resolveCataloguePrice` in `cloud/src/stripe.ts`, with everything `TIERS`-derived (`isKnownTier`, `usdPerCredit()`, `grantCostUsd()`) in `tenants.ts` so the import edge stays one-way stripe -> tenants; `tenants.ts` importing `./stripe` would close a module cycle around two load-time consts. Five findings. (1) The allowlist is a `Map`, not an object literal, because the key arrives in a request body: `record['constructor']` is a truthy INHERITED value, so an object-backed allowlist hands back `[Function]` as the product kind. Same trap in `isKnownTier` - `TIERS['toString']` is truthy, so it uses `hasOwnProperty` or `tierLimits` would then serve starter's limits for a tier nobody declared. (2) Once a key is past the allowlist it is one of six literals, so later refusals can safely name it in the RESPONSE body - before it, the value is client-controlled and only the log gets it. (3) `GET /v1/prices` with `lookup_keys[0]=` + `active=true` + `limit=2`: the limit is 2 deliberately, so a lookup key on two active prices is DETECTED rather than resolved to whichever Stripe ordered first. `active=true` is requirement 6, not tidiness - an archived price is still checkout-able by id. (4) Status split that keeps the studio honest: 400 = caller (key off the allowlist), 501 = OUR catalogue is unconfigured (no such active price, missing/unknown `metadata.tier`, unusable `metadata.credits`), 502 = Stripe (inherited from `stripeRequest`). `metadata.tier` unknown must REFUSE - defaulting to starter would charge the Team price and grant Starter limits with no trace but a support ticket. (5) A top-up's `metadata.credits` decides money in a Dashboard field, so `grantCostUsd(credits) <= unit_amount/100` is checked (USD prices only, since 9.2b has not settled currency): the realistic failure is an extra digit, and 25,000 instead of 2,500 credits is $100 of inference sold for $40. `metadata.credits` is parsed with `/^[0-9]{1,9}$/`, never `Number()` alone - `'1e3'`, `'2,500'`, `'500.5'` and `'0x1f'` all coerce to something nobody typed. `tax_behavior !== 'inclusive'` WARNS but does not refuse: it is permanent per price, so the enforcement point is creation (9.1/9.5), and refusing would take the catalogue offline for something Stripe cannot fix.
- 2026-09-04 - The OpenRouter runtime key's `limit` is now `runtimeKeyLimitUsd` = tier allowance + `grantPool()`, the SAME number `effectiveCostUsdLimit` gives the gate, and the webhook's GRANT path reconciles too - closing the documented "KNOWN GAP" where a purchased pack raised OUR ceiling while the vendor still enforced the tier figure and refused the exact overage the pack was sold to cover. THE INVARIANT THAT MAKES THE NAIVE SUM SAFE, so nobody "improves" it: the cap is patched to `allowance + poolAtPatch`, and between patches the pool only SHRINKS (spending draws it down; a new grant IS a patch) while the allowance is constant (a tier change IS a patch) - therefore `ourCeiling(t) = allowance + poolNow(t) <= allowance + poolAtPatch = keyLimit` always, and the key can never refuse a run our own gate allows. Both halves are required and each is useless alone: the grant-aware sum never fires on a purchase, and patching on the grant path gets undone by the next tier change if the sum is tier-only. The residual is ACCEPTED, not a bug: after a month boundary the key cap can sit above our ceiling by whatever pool was unspent at the last patch until the next patch tightens it - the gate is the primary control and reads the live pool, so do NOT add a cron sweep or a "last patched month" column. Three consequences worth carrying: (1) `runtimeKeyLimitUsd` must never throw, because `reconcileRuntimeKey`'s no-throw contract is what keeps an OpenRouter outage from becoming an endless Stripe redelivery - and its D1 read genuinely fails on the LIVE hosted database, which has no `credit_grants` (0003 is still unapplied remotely) and is exactly what `scripts/migrate-openrouter-workspace.mjs` drives it against, so it degrades to the tier allowance; that shim now sends THREE statements, not two. (2) ORDERING CAVEAT - a key minted before `limit_reset: 'monthly'` existed reads `limit` as a LIFETIME ceiling and nothing records which kind a tenant holds, so this is only fully sound after the migration re-mints the fleet; there is no `GET /keys/{hash}` call anywhere and adding one to detect it is out of scope. (3) `provisioning.test.mjs`'s `openRouterStub` has a MODULE-GLOBAL `mintCounter` and later sections pin `hash_minted_N` literals, so a new block that MINTS must go at the END of that file or it renumbers six unrelated assertions red. And NEVER return `WebhookOutcome.retry` from the grant path: the grant is idempotent on the payment id, so a redelivery grants nothing and fails again forever, over money that already landed, until Stripe disables the endpoint for every tenant - log and discard, which is safe only because `reconcileRuntimeKey` never throws. (Event routing for the delayed-payment defect fixed alongside this is a durable rule and lives in the `cloud-worker` steering.)
- 2026-09-03 - Refusal CTAs (task 7.7) are one leaf module, `frontend/src/app/core/billing-refusal.ts`: `remedyForRefusalCode` maps the five append-only worker tokens to a `BillingRemedy`, `remedyForModelError` (builder and chat, reads the code off the thrown `ModelRequestError` via the engine's `failureCodeOf`) and `remedyForRunFailure` (run controller, code plus the terminal message) each fall back to their OWN historical regex, and `refusalNotice` holds the copy so the toast, Ctrl+P and the chat cannot drift. `BillingCtaService` (`shared/billing/`) performs the remedy and owns the `openBillingPortal()` + `BillingRefreshService.watch()` pair that `PastDueNotice` used to duplicate. Five things worth keeping. (1) An UNRECOGNISED code answers `'none'` and must NOT fall through to prose - a code present means a NEWER worker, `RunFailureCode` is `string` exactly so a future token is representable, and a future `card_expired` whose message says "subscription" would otherwise resolve to Buy credits. Only an ABSENT code asks the prose. (2) The two regexes are deliberately DIFFERENT and were not unified: the run controller's `/credits exhausted/i` must stay narrow because a `run-failed` message is arbitrary workflow text and a data node whose HTTP error body mentions a subscription must not raise a billing toast, while the builder's `/\(402\)|credits exhausted|subscription/i` is broad because that is how a `no_subscription` refusal used to reach a CTA at all. (3) `subscription_past_due` gets the portal, NEVER checkout - "subscribing" again buys a second Stripe subscription instead of fixing the card - and `runs_exhausted` (a 429, not a 402) gets a plan-cards DEEP LINK with copy that leads on the free remedy, next month, since it is not a purchase problem. `no_runtime_key` is our fault and gets a notice with NO button, saying there is nothing to buy. (4) The toast hangs off `run-failed` only: `node-failed` carries the same code but fires once per ancestor frame, so a nested run would stack a toast per frame for one wall. (5) `RunControllerService` injecting `BillingCtaService` adds no NG0200 edge - it reaches only signal-holder dialog services, the `BillingService` leaf, and `PhormaCloudService`, which the run controller already injects and which itself injects only `ClerkService` and `TelemetryService`. This SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-12 note that only the credits-exhausted case gets a toast, and the boolean `creditsExhausted` on `WorkflowBuilderService` / `AssistantChatService` is now `billingRemedy`.

## Robustness Primitives (EPIC 3, shipped 2026-07-19)

- 2026-07-19 â€” Retry/fallback/timeout/compression all live INSIDE one `executeNode` call (`runAgent`'s `streamRoundRobustly`), so the journal key (minted once per executeNode) stays stable â€” internal retries are replay-safe. Never move retries above executeNode.
- 2026-07-19 â€” Error classification: `ModelRequestError` (engine/src/model.ts) carries `status`; `isTransientModelError` treats 408/429/5xx/network as retryable, other 4xx as permanent. The Tauri Rust proxy throws plain strings â€” the classifier falls back to parsing `(\d{3})` out of the message, so keep the `"{provider} request failed ({status}): â€¦"` message format stable in all clients.
- 2026-07-19 â€” `RunGate.sleep(ms)` is the interruptible backoff/wait primitive: it registers a waiter so `stop()` wakes it immediately (throws RunStoppedError). Never use bare setTimeout for delays inside the engine.
- 2026-07-19 â€” Workflow timeout: local = pause-aware clock in `WorkflowRun` (banks running ms on pause via gate.onPauseChange, re-arms timer on resume, `unref()` the timer); timeout sets `timedOut` then `gate.stop()`, and `execute()` maps the resulting RunStoppedError to `run-failed` ("Workflow timed outâ€¦"). Cloud = engine deadline (remaining budget after resume) + `this.schedule(â€¦, 'workflowTimedOut', runId)` durable alarm whose ONLY job is waking an evicted DO; cancel alarms with callback === 'workflowTimedOut' at settle.
- 2026-07-19 â€” Error branch: `AgentNodeData.errorPortId` stores the port base id explicitly (NOT positional â€” agents have user-visible ports). `errorRoutePortId()` requires the port to exist AND have a connected handoff, else fail-fast. On success the agent restricts `viaPortIds` to non-error out-ports so success never leaks through "On error". The catch that routes errors wraps ONLY `runNodeBody` â€” downstream failures must not be captured by an ancestor's branch.
- 2026-07-19 â€” Error Handler node (`error-handler` kind): run `execute()` catch invokes it best-effort with a JSON `{error, at}` payload before emitting `run-failed`; a stopped gate is swapped for a fresh RunGate during handler execution (restore after). Handler failures never mask the original error; run still settles failed (heym semantics).
- 2026-07-19 â€” Context compression: `pricing.ts` `ModelPrice.contextTokens` synced from OpenRouter `context_length` (localStorage cache key bumped to `phorma.model-price-table.v2` â€” bump it whenever the row shape changes); engine gets `RunOptions.contextWindow` lookup fn. Compression keeps first user message + last 2 tool rounds, summary rides as a USER message (Anthropic rejects back-to-back assistant turns). Summarizer failure returns messages untouched â€” never fails the node.
- 2026-07-19 â€” GOTCHA: `Record<ModelProviderId, â€¦>` maps in cloud/ (PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS, OPENROUTER_SLUG_PREFIX) break silently/loudly when a provider is added to the union â€” lmstudio was missing from BOTH (one tsc error, one silent undefined-prefix bug). When adding a ModelProviderId, grep cloud/src for existing Record maps.
- 2026-07-19 â€” Playwright vs canvas: click-to-add palette buttons drop nodes at the canvas centre (they can stack); node drags need a real movement threshold (small first move, then the real drag). Port-to-port wiring works by mouse.down on the port dot â†’ move â†’ up on the target port circle, but coordinates come from screenshots â€” re-screenshot after every layout change. PREFER `window.__phormaTest` (below) over any of this.

## Test Suite Quality (audit 2026-08-14)

- 2026-08-14 - THERE IS NOW CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs engine vitest + `tsc` + the 11 scenario scripts, cloud `test:unit` + `check`, frontend karma + production build, and `cargo check --locked` on every push and PR. Before it, `release.yml` was the only workflow (tag-triggered, build-only) and ~1700 assertions ran only when a human remembered. If you add a suite, add it to `ci.yml` in the same change or it does not exist.
- 2026-09-14 - Three ways a test can lie about a feature, all paid for in one session. (1) An un-awaited `fc.assert(fc.asyncProperty(...))` in a karma spec ESCAPES its `it` and races the next `beforeEach`, which reassigns the request log under it - the failure reads as "the request was never made". Always `await` it and make the `it` async. (2) A service constructor `effect()` flushes on the FIRST `await` inside a spec, so it consumed a positionally-queued `fetch` response meant for the spec's own call and an assertion about the backup list failed while the code was correct. Drain it in an async `beforeEach` with `TestBed.tick()` then `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))`, before any spec queues anything. (`TestBed.tick()` is also how you flush an effect for a persistence assertion.) (3) A fast-check property that creates a NEW resource per iteration eventually trips a production cap - one creating a workflow per run hit the starter 25-backup ceiling at iteration 26 and reported a fake concurrency bug. Seed such a tenant on the highest tier AND clean up per iteration.
- 2026-09-14 - `cloud/test/billing-admin.test.mjs` had a TIME BOMB that had already gone off: `const RANGE = { from: '2026-09-01', to: '2026-09-08' }` was a fixed literal while `seedUsage` places rows relative to `Date.now()`. Once the real clock passed 2026-09-10 every seeded usage row fell outside the queried window, `vendorCostUsd` read 0, and four margin checks failed - having silently stopped covering the vendor-cost half of the subtraction some days before that. Now a rolling 30-day window derived from the UTC day. Look for this pattern anywhere a fixed date literal meets a relative fixture: the test passes for a while and then fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the code.
- 2026-09-03 - Jasmine allows `spyOn` on a given property ONCE per spec, so a fast-check property in a karma suite must NOT rebuild its harness per iteration - the second `spyOn(window, 'fetch')` throws "has already been spied upon" and the counterexample you get is noise. Hoist the harness out of `fc.asyncProperty` and re-arm it per iteration with `spy.and.resolveTo(...)` + `spy.calls.reset()`. Same reason not to call `TestBed.configureTestingModule` inside a property: it throws once the module is instantiated, and a `resetTestingModule()` at the END of the iteration is skipped by the failing `expect`. Also: a bare top-level `beforeEach` in a karma spec FILE joins Jasmine's root suite and runs for every spec in the app - put per-suite setup (localStorage cleanup especially) inside the `describe`.
- 2026-08-14 - `engine/npm run test:e2e` (`engine/test/run-all.mjs`) runs all 11 `*.e2e.mts` scripts. `vitest.config.ts` EXCLUDES `test/**`, so `npm test` never touched them. The runner sets `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=frontend/tsconfig.json`: `ias-template.e2e.mts` and `connectors-builtin.e2e.mts` import frontend modules that resolve `@phorma/engine` through the path alias, and tsx applies `paths` from ONE tsconfig picked relative to the entry file. Adding the alias to `engine/tsconfig.json` does NOT work - tsx only applies paths to importers inside that tsconfig's directory.
- 2026-08-14 - `ias-template.e2e.mts` had been silently dead: `connectors.model.ts` grew a VALUE import from `@phorma/engine`, so the script died at MODULE_NOT_FOUND with 0 of 11 checks run. A scenario script that crashes before its first assertion still prints nothing alarming. This is why the runner treats a non-zero exit as failure and why CI runs it.
- 2026-08-14 - Bullshit-test patterns found and removed here; recognise them: (1) `engine/src/events.spec.ts` used `import type` ONLY and compared two literals it declared itself, claiming the union was "checked at compile time" while `vitest.config.ts` sets no `typecheck` - renaming `notify-sent` in `engine.ts` left it green. (2) `capabilities.spec.ts` Property 32 asserted `isBlocked(f) === f.some(x => x.severity === 'error')` with `isBlocked` defined as exactly that call - `x === x`, true even for a validator returning nothing. (3) `plan-op.spec.ts` compared `planOpCall(op).id` to `LEGACY_OP_ACTIONS[op]`, the constant the implementation returns - passes for any mapping. (4) `egress.spec.ts` had six shape-only properties (deduped/ordered/capped/lower-cased) that ALL hold for an empty list, so no test said which hosts a firewall rule may reach. (5) `deploy-config.test.mjs` paired migration tags by two independent `includes()` calls, so swapping the classes on v1 and v3 passed. (6) `connections-panel.spec.ts` rebound a built-in connector (impossible), swallowed it with `.catch(() => {})`, and asserted a negative over an empty list.
- 2026-08-14 - Mirroring a production table into a test as an "oracle" is a shared-bug tautology, not a test. `egress.spec.ts` copied `PROVIDER_HOSTS`; changing `anthropic` to `api.anthropic.com.attacker.test` in BOTH passed. Where a count is needed, derive it by calling the function under test with a narrowed input instead.

It had zero tests, and reintroducing the exact shipped `beta.10 < beta.9` string-compare bug passed the whole suite plus `npm run check`. Test version comparison through the 204-vs-200 the updater sees, not by exporting the comparator.
- 2026-08-14 - `RunControllerService.apply()` (the app's only visualization contract, ~250 lines, 25+ event types) was untested. `run-controller.service.apply.spec.ts` now pins the credits/dollars split (`phormaCloudCostUsd` accumulates only when `provider === 'phorma-cloud'`) and the `scoped` suppression that keeps sub-workflow child events off the parent canvas while STILL counting their usage. `apply()` is synchronous signal-in/signal-out - feed event literals, read the signals, no run or transport needed.
- 2026-08-14 - `connection-store.service.desktop.spec.ts` checked secret NAMES only, so `freezeResolved` could have leaked real keychain values with the whole 27-file suite green. It now asserts each value equals `hostSecretSentinel(id, key)` and that `secrets`/`config` are frozen. Any spec covering the keychain path must assert the sentinel, not the key set.
- 2026-08-14 - Mutation testing is the only honest way to grade a test. Procedure that worked: read the file with `[IO.File]::ReadAllText($absolutePath)` (it resolves against the PROCESS cwd, not the shell's - use an absolute path), `.Replace()` one realistic bug, run the targeted suite, restore the exact original text. Do NOT `git checkout` to revert while in-flight feature work is uncommitted.
- 2026-08-14 - Live BYO cost estimation needs a loaded pricing table: a `node-usage` event with token counts and no `costUsd` yields cost 0 and `estimated: false` in a bare TestBed, because `PricingService.estimator()` has no entries. Assert the estimated flag by sending `costSource: 'estimated'`, not by omitting the cost.
- 2026-08-15 - Writing an "accepts exactly X" property against a regex-based validator: restate the shape as structural predicates (split the value at its separator, check each part's alphabet) instead of importing the production pattern. For `cloud-aws/src/core/config.ts`'s `IMAGE_URI_RE` the split is unambiguous because neither the tag nor the digest alphabet contains `@`, `:` or `/` - first `@` else last `:`. The independent oracle then makes both halves mutation-sensitive: relaxing the registry class to `[A-Za-z0-9.-]` fails on `DOCKER.IO/phorma:a`, and flipping `triggerApiUrl`'s trailing-slash flag fails on `https://.../`.
- 2026-08-15 - The WHATWG URL parser rewrites scheme-relative forms for its six special schemes, so `new URL('https:/host')` yields `https://host/` and `new URL('HTTPS://host').protocol` is `https:`. Any oracle that restates an endpoint shape by string prefix must therefore lower-case the scheme comparison and keep `:`-bearing junk out of its free-form generator, or it will disagree with a `new URL`-based validator on inputs nobody documented. `config.ts` also checks `?`, `#` and surrounding whitespace against the SUPPLIED string because the parser normalizes all three away.
- 2026-08-14 - Engine `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` covers `src/**` only, and `*.spec.ts` type errors sat in it unnoticed (a `WorkflowNode` literal missing `category`/`icon`/`position`, `WorkflowPort` literals using `type`/`label` instead of `name`/`role`). CI runs this step now. `test/**/*.mts` is still NOT type-checked - it needs `@types/node` for `process`, and 16 `startRun` calls omit the required `requestInput`.
- 2026-08-16 - "The URL equals what the registry says" is not a test that the registry produced it: a literal in the service that agrees with the registry today passes. The half that bites is patching the registry entry (`DEPLOY_TARGETS[target].instanceUrl` and `endpoints[op].path` are plain mutable properties) to emit a sentinel, then asserting the emitted URL carries it and that no fragment the registry owns survives. Restore in a `finally` - `phorma` and `cloudflare` SHARE one endpoint table, so patching through one target patches the other. Parenthesize the sentinel (`/@registry-path(status)`), or the op name re-forms `/status` and the fragment scan false-fails. Check fragments only AFTER the base: `https://trigger.example.test` contains `/trigger` inside the scheme's `//`.
- 2026-08-16 - `get_diagnostics` on a frontend spec came back clean on a `TS2352` (`CloudEndpointContext` cast to `Record<string, string>`) that `ng test`'s bundler then failed on. Treat a clean diagnostics read as necessary, never sufficient - run the suite.
- 2026-08-16 - PowerShell's `>` redirect writes UTF-16LE, so a karma log captured that way matches nothing when read as utf8. Read it back with `readFileSync(path, 'utf16le')` and strip the ANSI colour codes (`/\u001b\[[0-9;]*m/g`) before grepping for `FAILED`. Piping karma through `Select-String` in the same command line also truncates and reorders in this shell - redirect, then parse in Node.
- 2026-08-16 - A SECOND `TestBed.createComponent` does NOT put two panel-body instances in the DOM at once: Angular's `DOMTestComponentRenderer.insertRootElement` calls `removeAllRootElements()` first, so the earlier fixture's root is detached and every `getBoundingClientRect().width > 0` filter over it reports zero elements. To reproduce the duplicate-instance hazard (scoped ids, `<label for>` associations), keep `fixture.nativeElement` - which IS the `<div id="rootN">` host, so its `parentElement` is `<body>`, not the root - and re-append it to `document.body` after creating the second fixture, then `detectChanges()` both.
- 2026-08-16 - Asserting "the form shows a message naming THIS field", match the rendered `__hint` on `startsWith(<visible label>)`, not `includes`. In the AWS section an invalid Region also invalidates the App CMK ARN, whose own message reads "in the region above", so a case-insensitive `includes('Region')` matches two hints and the count assertion false-fails. Every hint in that section opens with its field's label, which makes the prefix match the stronger assertion anyway. Related: an EMPTY region does not invalidate `appCmkArn` at all - its region check is `!region || match[1] === region` - so "clear the region" costs one invalid field, not two.
- 2026-08-16 - Requirement 1.9's "explicit PrimeNG small size" is checkable in the DOM without reading the template: `size="small"` emits `p-button-sm`, `p-select-sm`, `p-inputtext-sm`, `p-textarea-sm`, `p-checkbox-sm` and nothing appears when the size is omitted. `p-inputnumber` and `p-selectbutton` carry NO size class of their own - they push it onto an inner `p-inputtext` / `p-button` - so checking the leaf classes covers the composites, and a `<p-*>` host tag outside the known table is the signal to extend it.

That is NOT scaffold breakage - `tsconfig.spec.json`, the `zone.js` + `zone.js/testing` polyfills and the Chrome launcher are all fine, provable by dropping one throwaway spec in and watching the same command exit 0. Pass a FACTORY, not the property - `fc.assert(fn)` where `fn` is the arrow that builds the property fails every case with "Invalid property encountered, please use a valid property", which reads like a fast-check version problem and is not one. Derive the base the same way the subject does (`environment.apiBaseUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '')`) and let the literal in the assertion be only the part the spec is actually claiming.
- 2026-08-26 - `admin/` has its own npm project and its own karma run (`npm --prefix admin exec -- ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless`, 39 specs), which `frontend`'s 1040-spec suite does not touch. Those steps sit at the END of `ci.yml`'s checks job, so watching an engine/cloud/frontend tail go green tells you nothing about them - and `check-telemetry-secrets.mjs` silently WARNs and skips its built-bundle half unless `admin npm run build` has run first.
- 2026-09-02 - Writing a property about BYTES (HMAC, hashing, framing, anything through `TextEncoder`): do NOT generate the input with `fc.string({ unit: 'binary' })`. It emits lone surrogates, and every lone surrogate encodes to the SAME U+FFFD bytes, so an injectivity property ("a signature over A never validates B", "distinct inputs hash differently") is genuinely FALSE for two distinct inputs and the counterexample tells you nothing about your code. `unit: 'grapheme'` is the right generator and is also the honest one wherever the value arrives from `request.text()`, which decodes bytes and therefore cannot produce a lone surrogate. Second half of the same lesson, from `cloud/test/stripe.test.mjs` (task 3.5): a positive crypto case signed with the same primitive the code verifies with is one library agreeing with itself - `node:crypto`'s `createHmac(...).update(payload, 'utf8')` is a different implementation reached through a different API, so one known-answer vector from it is what makes the payload-format claim real. Mutation grading on that suite: the fixture cases from task 3.2 did NOT discriminate two things the module documents, and the mutations that prove the new cases do are `STRIPE_SIGNATURE_HEX` `{64}` -> `{63,65}` (caught only by the 63/65 candidate cases, not by the pre-existing 4-char and 64-char-non-hex ones) and the signed payload's `parsed.timestamp` -> `parsed.timestampSeconds` (caught only by the leading-zero `t=01700000000` cases).
- 2026-09-03 - `engine/src/model-sampling.spec.ts` was importing `ModelRequest` from `./types.js`, which does not export it (it lives in `model.ts`), so `engine`'s `tsc --noEmit` was RED before task 6.6 touched anything while `npm test` stayed green - vitest sets no `typecheck`, so a spec's type errors cost nothing until someone runs tsc. Same class of miss as the 2026-08-14 entry above, which is the point: adding a spec means running the engine type-check too, not just the suite. Fixed in passing.
- 2026-09-03 - `fc.date()` GENERATES AN INVALID DATE by default in fast-check 4, and `new Date(NaN).toISOString()` THROWS `RangeError: Invalid time value`. `cloud/test/telemetry.test.mjs`'s Property 18 mapped `fc.date()` through `toISOString()`, so roughly one seed in ten failed with "Invalid time value" and NO counterexample - the generator died before the function under test was ever called. It passed standalone and failed inside `npm run test:unit`, which reads as suite interference and is not. Any `fc.date()` feeding a formatter needs `{ noInvalidDate: true }`. Fixed in passing during task 6.7.
- 2026-09-03 - Mutation-grading `grantDrawUsd` (task 6.7): the obvious mutation, dropping the `overageBefore` term, is BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING and every property still passes. The trailing `Math.min(cost, ...)` clamp already caps the result, so `min(cost, max(0, before+cost-allowance))` equals the difference of overages on every input. The mutation that actually discriminates the requirement-24 split is a WHOLESALE draw (`before + cost > allowance ? cost : 0`), which P2 catches in 24 iterations and shrinks to a three-run starter sequence. Grading a guard-heavy pure function means mutating the DECISION, not deleting a term the guards subsume.
- 2026-09-03 - `cloud/test/telemetry-ingest.test.mjs`'s failure injection was UNPROTECTED, and that turned the documented Windows `EADDRINUSE` into an unreadable failure. `failSql` is module state in the in-worker harness, the ingest handler CATCHES a rejected batch and answers `200 {}` exactly as a healthy no-op does, and `/__t/reset` did not clear it - so a `dispatchFetch` that rejected between arming and clearing left it armed for the rest of the process. Property 23 then failed at test 67 and SHRANK to the minimal input, because by then every input failed, and the counterexample ("0 stored rows", canonical uuid) described nothing. Now: `/__t/reset` clears `failSql`, and both injection sites use try/finally. The real cause surfaces again as `connect EADDRINUSE`. Two lessons - failure injection always gets a finally, and an "everything fails now" shrink result means look for LEAKED HARNESS STATE, not for a bug at the shrunk input. Also: `withLoopbackRetry`'s 4 attempts genuinely run out if you re-run a Miniflare suite back to back (four runs left 13,195 sockets in TIME_WAIT here). `netstat -ano | Select-String TIME_WAIT` counts them; they drain in about two minutes.
- 2026-09-03 - Property coverage counters must be gated on the property having PASSED. fast-check stops at the first counterexample, so a non-vacuity check like "straddling sequences were reached (0)" then fires as a SECOND failure for one cause and pushes the counterexample off the top of the log. `asyncProperty` in `cloud/test/entitlement.test.mjs` returns a boolean for exactly this.

## Sub-Workflows (EPIC 8, shipped 2026-07-23)

- 2026-07-23 - Portable nesting uses a FLAT cycle-safe `WorkflowSpec.subWorkflows` registry, not recursive inlining. Local runs/evals capture one immutable library-first transitive snapshot; cloud/export uses the embedded snapshot. This is what permits bounded self/mutual recursion without non-serializable specs.
- 2026-07-23 - Depth limits are Free/BYO 2, Starter 5, Pro 8, Team 10, with an engine hard ceiling of 25. Unknown hosted tiers currently fall back to Starter (5); custom enterprise needs an authoritative server tier definition before the UI may advertise more.
- 2026-07-23 - Nested execution is ONE run/RunRecord: child frames share gate, timeout, callbacks, journal, and the global node-execution budget. Interior events carry a root-to-leaf `scope`; trace groups them under Execute Workflow while parent canvas state ignores scoped child node/handoff events. Usage still rolls into the parent with scope-aware by-node keys.
- 2026-07-23 - Replay safety: the child journal namespace MUST derive from the Execute Workflow wrapper's deterministic journal key (payload hash + occurrence). Never use a separate child occurrence counter, because replayed wrapper nodes bypass it and can repeat side effects after DO eviction. Execute wrappers re-enter child frames on replay so journals suppress side effects while nested trace events reconstruct.
- 2026-07-23 - Approval identity is `requestId`, derived from frame/journal identity + node occurrence; `nodeId` is display metadata only. Repeated/parallel child frames can contain identical node ids, so maps and resolve APIs keyed by nodeId will collide and strand promises.
- 2026-07-23 - Historical run snapshots include optional `subWorkflows`. Cloud stores a versioned snapshot envelope in the existing graph column and parses legacy raw graph JSON for backward compatibility. Bring to Canvas must restore both root graph and embedded registry.
- 2026-07-23 - Extract-to-sub-workflow is pure in `core/subworkflow-extract.ts`: reject triggers/error handlers and ambiguous boundaries, move private tools, clone shared tools, prepend a Manual trigger, then rewire the parent around one Execute Workflow node. Save child FIRST; after the await verify active doc + graph reference are unchanged before one `replaceGraph` call, or abort to avoid overwriting another tab/concurrent edit.
- 2026-07-23 - `HistoryService.boundaryOnce()` forces the next graph mutation into a fresh undo step so atomic replacements such as extraction cannot coalesce with a preceding edit.

## AI Assistant Chat (EPIC 5, shipped 2026-07-21)

- 2026-08-25 - `[innerHTML]` content receives NO `_ngcontent` attribute, so every encapsulated DESCENDANT rule against rendered markdown is dead: `.phorma-chat__md p { ... }` compiles to `p[_ngcontent-x]` and matches nothing. The chat's entire markdown type scale had never applied - measured `marginBottom: 0px` on a rendered `<p>`. Fix is `:host ::ng-deep .phorma-chat__md { ... }` at top level (the container is in the template and keeps the host attribute; descendants go unscoped). The prompt panel and prompt dialog already did this via `::ng-deep { @include prompt.prompt-preview-typography; }` - copy that shape for any new markdown surface, and verify with a computed style, never by eye. Same root cause as the PrimeNG `styleClass` trap under UI / Styling.

It used to be an accent tint, which made the user's own words the loudest thing in the transcript. The ASSISTANT answer has NO bubble: bare markdown on the surface, full width, with a hover-revealed footer strip (copy, cost, model) instead of a copy button floating inside a bubble. Cost stays visible per the credits rule; the strip reserves `min-height` so hover cannot reflow the answer.

Applying is gated on `WorkflowBuilderService.canAutoApply` (= `phormaCloud.subscribed()`), proxied as `AssistantChatService.canAutoApply` to keep `PhormaCloudService` out of the chat service's dependency list, and re-checked inside `applyProposal` because the action registry can reach it too. - 2026-08-25 - The Apply button in the plan card was a full-width primary slab with an invisible label: the solid-`pButton` opaque `::before` overlay swallowing bare children, exactly the trap in the conventions, plus stretch from the card's `flex-direction: column`.
