Before this, a tool used by the first AND last agent landed in a trailing column, reading like a downstream step. Disconnected tools still stack in the trailing column.
- 2026-07-13 - After an AI build the canvas fits to screen TWICE: once right after ops finish placing (`canvasState.zoomCommand.set('fit')` via `WorkflowBuilderService.fitToScreen()`), again after `arrangeLayout()`. The fit command rail is `CanvasStateService.zoomCommand` - the canvas effect consumes and nulls it.

## Studio Action Registry (assistant control surface)

- 2026-07-31 - The assistant is no longer graph-only. `core/studio-actions/` holds ONE registry (`StudioActionRegistryService`) plus a per-surface provider service (`graph`, `prompts`, `evals`, `runs`, `workflows`/`versions`/`deploy`, `skills`, `connections`, `portal`, `usage`, `settings`/`navigation`). Adding a capability = one entry in the owning provider's `actions()` plus its executor. Do NOT touch the Agent-mode tool list, the Plan apply switch or the system prompts - all three derive from the registry (`toolDefinitions`, `planOpCall`, `summarizeActions`).
- 2026-07-31 - Root cause of "create an eval for me drops a node on the canvas": `agentToolDefinitions()` offered six graph tools only, `PlanOp` accepted five graph op forms only, and every system prompt cast the model as a graph architect. A request always funnelled to the nearest graph edit. Widening the ACTION surface is the fix; prompt wording alone was not.
- 2026-07-31 - `PlanOp` gained an `action` form (`{op:'action', action:<id>, args:{}}`). The five legacy forms (`add|connect|update|remove|disconnect`) MUST keep working: persisted `chat-threads` rows contain them. `studio-actions/plan-op.ts` is the pure mapping and `plan-op.spec.ts` pins it - if you change a graph action's parameter names, that spec is what catches the replay break.
- 2026-09-14 - There is no suite that enumerates every registered action, so a mis-tiered one is invisible: `silent` runs with no confirmation in Agent mode, which for a write means the model can destroy something on its own reading of a sentence. When adding actions, add a spec that asserts the tier AND that each executor delegates (`workflow-actions.recovery.spec.ts` is the shape: tier table, unique ids, `confirmSummary` present and naming the target, and a spy per owning service). The six recovery actions are `deployment_list`/`backup_list` (silent read) and `backup_restore`/`deployment_undeploy`/`backup_delete`/`backup_purge` (confirm write).
- 2026-07-31 - `summarizeGraph()` no longer emits `prompt-gist`. It was a 120-char fragment of the first prompt line, which is exactly why "modify that specific prompt" was unanswerable - the model saw a truncated hint with no way to get the rest. Nodes now report `prompt: N chars (read it with prompt_read)`. Never re-add state to the prompt that a Read_Action can fetch: prompt size must stay flat as the action surface grows.
- 2026-07-31 - `update_node`'s old `isAgentNode(node)` gate SILENTLY DISCARDED prompt patches aimed at other kinds. The test is now `hasPromptField(node.data)` (exported from `graph-actions.service.ts`), and a kind with no prompt field returns `ok:false` naming the kind instead of dropping the write.
- 2026-07-31 - Ask mode is a read-only TOOL LOOP now, not a single stream. It gets `toolDefinitions('read')`; tools are omitted when a caller passes its own `system` prompt, which is what keeps the analyzer and migration converter (`sendTask`) on their old single-round behaviour. Don't pass tools alongside a fixed task prompt.
- 2026-07-31 - Risk tiers: `confirm` for run start, eval suite runs, every delete, deploy, and settings/connection writes; `silent` for reads and local reversible document edits. Plan playback asks ONCE for the whole plan (`pendingConfirmations` + `execute(..., {confirmed:true})`) - per-op dialogs teach people to click through guardrails. Read the resolved boolean from `ConfirmDialogService.confirm`, never `activeState()`.
- 2026-07-31 - `graph_remove_node` is confirm-tier even though the Edit_Session could revert it (Requirement 6.1 names node deletion explicitly). `graph_remove_connection` is silent - the "connection" in that same requirement is the credential entity, which has its own `connection_delete`.
- 2026-07-31 - Panel reveal after a non-graph action is deduped per surface per turn (`revealedSurfaces`). Without the dedupe a multi-read turn flips the sidebar on every lookup.
- 2026-07-31 - `CloudService.pushWorkflow()` now returns boolean. Every failure path in it is a TOAST, so `await`ing it told the caller nothing - the deploy action reported success on a rejected push. Any new CloudService method an action calls needs the same treatment.
- 2026-07-31 - `revertable: false` on an Action_Result means the Revert bar cannot undo it. `AssistantChatService.withTurnNotes()` appends "Not covered by Revert" and "Did not work" sections to the persisted turn text - failures must reach the TRANSCRIPT, not just the transient activity feed which is cleared when the turn ends.
- 2026-07-31 - DI: the registry pulls in `CloudService` (deploy) and `RunControllerService` (runs), so it sits DOWNSTREAM of the NG0200 cycle, not inside it. Safe because nothing in the registry's closure injects `WorkflowBuilderService`. Keep it that way: an action service must never inject the builder or `AssistantChatService`.
- 2026-07-31 - ASSISTANT CONTEXT is visible and editable: `core/assistant-context.service.ts` owns it, the chat renders a chip strip above the input, and the document tab right-click menu adds/removes tabs. The active document is ALWAYS context (never make the user add what they are looking at). Context is keyed by open-tab `docId`, not `workflowId`, so it covers unsaved drafts and drops itself when the tab closes. Deliberately session state - a stale context item riding along invisibly in a later conversation is worse than re-adding it.
- 2026-07-31 - `AssistantContextService` injects ONLY `WorkflowService`. That is load-bearing: `DocumentTabs` uses it, and injecting `AssistantChatService` there instead would drag the whole builder/registry/cloud graph into the layout shell at startup.
- 2026-07-31 - Extra context workflows reach the model two ways: a capped identity-only block from `summarizeContextWorkflows()` (40 nodes per workflow, no prompt bodies) plus the `workflow_read` action for full detail. `workflow_read` resolves OPEN TABS before the saved library, because a tab carries unsaved edits the library copy does not.
- 2026-07-31 - The document tab context menu needed the same PrimeNG v20 workaround as the sidebar: an explicit `[target]` (the tab strip, via signal `viewChild`) or the contextmenu listener is never bound and the menu silently never opens. Keep it FLAT - PrimeNG opens submenus on hover and synthetic clicks cannot reach them.
- 2026-07-31 - WINDOWS GOTCHA that cost a clean diff: `Get-Content`/`Set-Content` in Windows PowerShell 5.1 read UTF-8 as cp1252 and write CRLF. Splicing a source file with them mangled every em dash to `Ã¢â‚¬â€` and flipped the whole file to CRLF, turning a 250-line change into a 584-line diff. Use Node (`readFileSync`/`writeFileSync`, utf8) for any scripted source edit in this repo - the tree is LF.

## Release Pipeline / Auto-Update

- 2026-07-14 - ROOT CAUSE of "app never sees new beta": the `publish-r2` job's "Download release assets" step lacked `VERSION` in its `env` (it was only set on the later "Sync to R2" step). `gh release download ""` silently falls back to the release marked **Latest** on GitHub - for prerelease chains that's an OLD version (betas are "Pre-release", so beta.1 stayed Latest). Old files got uploaded under the new version's R2 prefix and `stable/latest.json` was poisoned with the old version â†’ updater endpoint returned 204 to everyone. Fixed: `VERSION` env added to the download step, and `scripts/publish-r2.mjs` now aborts if (a) no downloaded filename contains the tag version or (b) the release's own latest.json version mismatches the tag.
- 2026-07-14 - To manually (re-)publish a release to R2 from a dev machine: `gh release download vX.Y.Z --dir release-assets-fix` then `node scripts/publish-r2.mjs vX.Y.Z release-assets-fix` with `cloud/node_modules/.bin` on PATH (wrangler isn't global locally; interactive account picker appears - choose "Phorma Agent Studio"). Verify with `curl https://phorma-agent-studio-cloud.phorma-agent-studio.workers.dev/update/stable/windows/x86_64/<older-version>` (expect 200 + JSON) and `/releases.json`.
- 2026-07-14 - `compareVersions` in `cloud/src/releases.ts` compared prerelease tags as PLAIN STRINGS â†’ `beta.10 < beta.9`, which would silently stop updates at the 10th beta. Fixed with SemVer-style dot-segment numeric comparison (`comparePrerelease`). NEEDS WORKER DEPLOY before shipping a `-beta.10`.
- 2026-07-14 - `release.mjs` lives in `scripts/` - the release command is `node scripts/release.mjs X.Y.Z` from repo root (running `node release.mjs` at root fails MODULE_NOT_FOUND).
- 2026-07-14 - GitHub marks the newest NON-prerelease as "Latest"; all `-beta.*` releases are Pre-release, so "Latest" can lag many versions behind. Never rely on gh's Latest fallback in CI.
- 2026-07-14 - UPDATE UX (VS Code-style, no visible installer): `tauri.conf.json` `plugins.updater.windows.installMode: "quiet"` makes the NSIS updater run `/S /R` (silent + relaunch) - without it the default `passive` mode shows a progress installer window and the user sees the app close/install/reopen at launch. `UpdateService` lifecycle: check â†’ background `download()` (download ONLY - never `downloadAndInstall()`, which on Windows runs the installer immediately) â†’ ConfirmDialog prompt "Restart now / On next launch" â†’ `install()`+`relaunch()` on confirm, or persist `phorma.layout.updateOnNextLaunch=<version>` on defer (next startup `check()` sees the flag and silently installs). Toolbar Update button (`.phorma-update-button`, left of the cloud button, desktop-gated) + status-bar badge both call `updates.updateNow()` (download-if-needed â†’ silent install â†’ restart).
- 2026-08-25 - `scripts/release.mjs` bumped `Cargo.toml` but NOT `Cargo.lock`, and the `rust` CI job runs `cargo check --locked`, so every release commit failed CI with "cannot update the lock file ... because --locked was passed". It went unnoticed because nothing else in the pipeline is `--locked`: `tauri-action` passes no such flag, so the installer build regenerates the lock and the release still ships. `release.mjs` now rewrites the workspace crate's own version in `Cargo.lock` too, reading the crate name from `Cargo.toml` so a rename cannot make it a silent no-op. Verified against a real bump: cargo's own regeneration touches exactly that one line.
- 2026-08-25 - A release tag builds installers ONLY. Anything a feature needs on the hosted Worker is a separate, manual, ordered chore, and the studio half of a feature can ship to users while the server half does not exist. Telemetry shipped in `0.2.0-beta.11` and needed, in this order: `wrangler secret put TELEMETRY_ADMIN_USER_IDS --env hosted`, `wrangler d1 migrations apply phorma-cloud --env hosted --remote`, then `wrangler deploy --env hosted`. Secret before deploy so no window exists where the routes are live and the allowlist is absent; migration before deploy so the first aggregate read cannot hit a missing table. `wrangler secret list --env hosted` and `wrangler d1 migrations list phorma-cloud --env hosted --remote` are the two cheap reads that tell you where a deployment actually stands.
- 2026-09-14 - A GitHub Actions job that fails in ~2s with ZERO steps and an EMPTY `runner_name` was never scheduled, and the reason is almost always account billing: "recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased". Cutting `1.0.0-beta.1` hit it on `publish-r2` - all four installer builds passed (macOS bills at 10x, Windows 2x, so the matrix drains the budget first) and the R2 sync then could not start. The message is NOT in `gh run view --job <id> --log` (that answers "log not found" because no log exists) and NOT in `gh run view --json jobs` (`steps` is `[]`). It is only in `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{jobId}/annotations`. Read a 0-step job that way before suspecting the runner image - the same `ubuntu-22.04` label succeeded in the same run.
- 2026-09-14 - `scripts/release.mjs` bumps **11** files, not 12. The playbook's Phase 4 gate said "expect exactly the 12 files" while its own enumeration listed 11 (3 under `backend/src-tauri/` + 6 `package.json` + 2 source constants). Corrected in the playbook; if you are counting a release diff, 11 is right.
- 2026-09-14 - ORDER THE TWO PRODUCTION STEPS: deploy the hosted worker BEFORE syncing R2, never after. R2's `latest.json` is what flips every installed client onto the new version, so publishing it first hands users a studio whose new routes (`/api/backups/*` in this release) 404 against the still-old worker. The playbook's Phase 7-before-8 ordering encodes this; it is a user-visible breakage window, not bookkeeping. It was REAL on `1.0.0-beta.1`, not hypothetical: re-running the stalled `publish-r2` job put R2 on the new version ~7 minutes before the worker was deployed, so for that window the updater offered a studio the server could not serve. If a retried R2 job ever lands first, deploy the worker immediately rather than finishing the checklist in order. `/api/backups` answering 401 (not 404) unauthenticated is the cheap proof the new surface is really live.
- 2026-09-14 - Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the default `powershell` shell here) breaks two of the playbook's Phase 8 probes. `Invoke-WebRequest` needs `-UseBasicParsing` or it blocks on an interactive "Script Execution Risk" prompt that just eats the whole tool timeout, and `-SkipHttpErrorCheck` does not exist before PowerShell 7 - use a `[System.Net.HttpWebRequest]` helper with `AllowAutoRedirect=$false` and read the status off the `WebException` response when you need to see a 204 or a 302.

## Flow Primitives (ForEach / Wait-for-Event / structured payloads)

- 2026-07-17 - New flow node kinds `for-each` + `wait-event` (added for the IAS/PAYGW accounting workflow). Touch points followed the registry pattern exactly: kind unions + data ifaces in BOTH `workflow.model.ts` and `engine/src/types.ts` (structural twins), catalog entries in `node-catalog.ts`, executors in `engine.ts` `runNodeBody` switch, properties-panel editors. Canvas needed ZERO changes (registry-driven), only a `waiting-event` node state mapped to the same amber breathing ring as `waiting-approval` in `canvas-graph-renderer.ts`.
- 2026-07-17 - ForEach semantics: port convention by POSITION (like approval-gate) - out[0] = loop body ("Each item"), out[1] = "Done". The loop node OWNS iteration (sequential default, opt-in bounded concurrency 1-8) instead of fanning out edges, because aggregators key collected inputs by port id (last-write-wins) - dynamic N-branch fan-in through the existing parallel/aggregator path would collide. Per-item terminal payloads are collected via a `sink?: string[]` threaded through `executeNode`/`followHandoffs`/`deliver`; the Done port receives `{results, exceptions}` JSON. Item failures are recorded as exceptions and the loop continues (`continueOnError` default true).
- 2026-07-17 - Wait-for-Event: engine contract is optional `RunOptions.waitForEvent(nodeId, correlationKey, message, payload)` (mirrors `requestApproval`). Correlation keys are templates interpolated per payload (`signed:{{jobId}}`). Studio host: `RunControllerService.pendingWaits` signal + runs-panel "Deliver event" cards; remote runs use `remoteEventSender` over the monitor WS (synthetic cards, same pattern as remoteApprovalSender). Cloud host: `POST /events {correlationKey, payload}` + `POST /approvals {nodeId, approved}` HTTP endpoints on the DO + WS `event` frame; `earlyEvents` map buffers webhook races (event arriving before the waiter registers). CAVEAT: waits are IN-MEMORY - DO eviction still kills a suspended run; durable checkpoint/resume is the next milestone.
- 2026-07-17 - Structured payloads: `engine/src/payload.ts` - `interpolatePayload` (`{{a.b.c}}` dotted paths into JSON payloads, `{{input}}` = whole payload, unknown tokens left verbatim), `extractItems` (bare array / itemsPath / single-array-property / first embedded JSON array in prose or fences), `mergePayloads` (JSON objects shallow-merge, event wins). `renderPrompt` now uses `interpolatePayload` so ALL agent prompts support dotted-path fields; plain `{{input}}` behavior unchanged.
- 2026-07-17 - Execution budget: `RunOptions.maxExecutions` (default 100). Both hosts pass 2000 when the graph contains a `for-each` node - real batches (150 items Ã— 2 nodes) blow the default anti-runaway budget.
- 2026-07-17 - Engine E2E harness: `engine/test/flow-primitives.e2e.mts` (24 checks, no model/UI needed - fake ModelClient, run `npx -y tsx engine/test/flow-primitives.e2e.mts`). Pattern: build graphs with tiny node/edge helper fns, drive `startRun` with stub `waitForEvent`/`requestApproval`, assert on the collected RunEvent list.
- 2026-07-17 - GOTCHA: class field initializers referencing constructor params don't work (`private readonly x = this.options.y` when `options` is a constructor param property) - TS injects field initializers BEFORE constructor-param assignment in this ordering. Assign in the constructor body instead.
- 2026-07-17 - DURABLE RUNS (checkpoint/resume): engine `RunOptions.journal?: RunJournal` (`lookup`/`record`) - `executeNode` computes deterministic keys `nodeId|fnv1a(payload)|occurrence` and REPLAYS journaled results (emits node-completed, follows handoffs, but skips the node body entirely - no model calls, no tool side effects, no duplicate approval/wait prompts). Recording happens BEFORE followHandoffs so a downstream crash never loses completed work. Restarting the SAME run (same graph+input+journal) resumes at the first un-journaled node.
- 2026-07-17 - Cloud DO run persistence: `run_journal` table in the Agents SDK's embedded SQLite (`this.sql` tagged template - available on the Agent base class), `activeRun {runId,input,startedAt}` in DO state, and partyserver's `onStart()` override (fires on every DO wake) re-triggers an interrupted run via `trigger(input, resumeRunId)`. Journal rows deleted when the run settles. Resumed hosted runs must pass `countsAsRun: false` to `recordRun` (increment ledger cost only, not the monthly run count).
- 2026-07-17 - GOTCHA: `stop` on a run suspended in `requestApproval`/`waitForEvent` does nothing by itself - the run is awaiting a HOST promise, not the gate. The host's stop path must resolve pending approval/wait resolvers (with false/'') so execution re-enters the gate and throws RunStoppedError. Studio does this in `RunControllerService.stop()`; cloud in the WS 'stop' frame handler.
- 2026-07-17 - tsx top-level-await gotcha: a test that awaits a run whose waitForEvent returns a never-resolving promise hangs the process ("unsettled top-level await"). To simulate DO eviction in tests, ABANDON the run (don't await handle.done) and synchronize on a side-channel promise instead.

## Learnings

- 2026-07-14 - Desktop shell keyboard hygiene: `frontend/src/index.html` now has a capture-phase keydown listener (guarded by `'__TAURI_INTERNALS__' in window`) that `preventDefault()`s WebView browser accelerators (Ctrl+P print, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+R/F5 reload, Ctrl+J/O/U/H/L/K/E/D/T/W, F3/F7). preventDefault does NOT stop propagation, so app handlers in `toolbar.ts` (Ctrl+P palette, F5 run controls) still fire. Browser preview (`ng serve`) keeps normal dev shortcuts (reload etc.) because the guard excludes non-Tauri. When adding a new app shortcut on a browser-reserved combo, the toolbar handler still needs its own preventDefault for web mode.

## Run History (EPIC 1)

- 2026-07-19 - RUN HISTORY shipped: shared `createRunRecorder` in `engine/src/run-record.ts` builds `RunRecord` (summary + graph snapshot + coalesced event log; token/thinking streams fold into per-node text entries, 64KB payload clip, 2000-event cap). Local runs â†’ `RunHistoryService` (fed from the emit tee in `RunControllerService.start()`, LOCAL runs only) â†’ IndexedDB v2 `runs` store. Cloud runs â†’ DO SQLite `runs`/`run_events` tables + `GET /runs` and `GET /runs/{id}` routes (works hosted AND BYO; D1 not involved). Retention 50/workflow both sides. E2E: `engine/test/run-record.e2e.mts`.
- 2026-07-19 - Trace rendering is centralized in `frontend/src/app/core/run-trace.ts` (`describeRunEvent`/`traceFromRunLog`): both the live `apply()` trace and the history detail view use it. To change a trace icon/label/tone, edit `describeRunEvent` - do NOT add `pushTrace` calls back into `apply()`.
- 2026-07-19 - IDB index gotcha: records with a null key value are silently EXCLUDED from IndexedDB indexes. Draft runs (workflowId null) are stored with a derived `workflowKey: 'draft'` field for the `by-workflow` index.
- 2026-07-19 - DO monitor WS now sends a `{type:'monitor-synced'}` sentinel after replaying its event buffer in `onConnect` - the studio's `CloudService.onmessage` filters it (and the Agents SDK's `cf_agent_state`/`cf_agent_mcp_servers` frames parse as unknown types and fall through `apply()` harmlessly). `CloudService.connect(workflowId?)` accepts a target workflow for live-attach from the history list.
- 2026-07-19 - `npx tsc` in a package without a local `typescript` dep prompts to install the SQUATTER package `tsc@2.0.4` - decline and use `../frontend/node_modules/.bin/tsc` (engine has no typescript dep by design).
- 2026-07-19 - Local `wrangler dev` for `cloud/` picks up the repo `.env` (Clerk keys) â†’ auth fails closed with 401. For open-instance local testing run `npx wrangler dev --local --env-file /tmp/empty/.env` (an empty env file).

## Connector Packaging (P1-14, shipped 2026-08-12)

- 2026-08-12 - A connector is ONE `*.connector.json`: connection template (type, auth mode, config field NAMES, secret key NAMES) + pre-configured `http-request`/`sql-query`/`transform`/`aggregate` steps + mapping tables + optional starter workflows. Format, validation, packaging and derivations all live in `engine/src/connectors.ts` (pure, `connectors.spec.ts` + `connectors-property.spec.ts`); the studio only adds storage/install (`core/connectors.service.ts`, IDB v10 `connectors` store). Plan and the five decisions: `docs/connector-packaging-plan.md`.
- 2026-08-12 - Installed steps are deliberately NOT in `NODE_CATALOG`. `registerConnectorStepResolver` (`core/node-catalog.ts`) is a one-function seam that `findCatalogEntry` consults for `connector-step:` ids, exactly like the `mcp-preset:` branch. WHY IT MATTERS: the obvious alternative (WorkflowService asks ConnectorsService) closes a DI cycle - `ConnectorsService -> ConnectionsService -> WorkflowService` - and NG0200 is already a hazard on the run path. The seam also means the canvas drop, click-to-add, the AI router and `window.__phormaTest` all support connector steps with zero changes.
- 2026-08-12 - A connector step instantiates as an ORDINARY data node with no back-reference to its bundle, so uninstalling a connector cannot break a workflow. Consequence worth remembering: the properties panel CANNOT show provenance, because it would have to be inferred by matching node data and would start lying the moment the user edits the node. That plan item was dropped on purpose - do not "fix" it by adding a connector id to node data.
- 2026-08-12 - `secretPositionsOf` originally used a global visited-Set for cycle safety, which silently treated the SECOND occurrence of a SHARED object as a cycle and skipped it - so a credential in a subtree two steps shared went unreported. Found by a property test whose `fc.constant` handed out one object instance to both steps. Fix: track ANCESTORS only (add on entry, delete on exit). Two lessons: (1) cycle guards must be ancestor sets, not visited sets, whenever the same subtree can legitimately appear twice; (2) never mutate a generated value in a fast-check property - `fc.constant` reuses the instance, so the mutation corrupts every later run and the shrunk counterexample is nonsense. Clone first.
- 2026-08-12 - Packaging (`packageConnectorBundle`) carries the connection's SHAPE, never its values: the author's own `baseUrl`/`host`/`database`/`tenantId` identify their install and a bundle is shared by definition, so config fields travel as names + labels marked required. It also strips `connectionId` and `errorPortId` (a port id belongs to one node instance), lifts a transform's inline `lookups` into bundle-level `tables`, and VALIDATES the result - so packaging a node with a hardcoded key fails loudly instead of publishing the key.
- 2026-08-12 - Built-in connectors (`core/connectors-builtin.ts`) are derived at read time and never persisted, so a fix to one reaches existing installs through an app update. They are validated by `npx -y tsx engine/test/connectors-builtin.e2e.mts`. That check lives in `engine/test/*.e2e.mts` rather than `engine/src/*.spec.ts` because it imports a FRONTEND module - engine must not depend on frontend, and the existing precedent is `ias-template.e2e.mts`.
- 2026-08-12 - `AggregateMetric` is `{name, fn, path?}` - NOT `{name, op, field}`. Guessing it cost a round trip on the built-in SQL connector.
- 2026-08-12 - THERE IS NO `input` IN EITHER SUBSTITUTION LANGUAGE, and both shipped built-in connectors were wrong about it. Expressions (`expr.ts`): `item` = the record being projected, `index`, `$` = whole payload, `$text` = raw text, and a bare `name` is shorthand for `$.name`. So `input.id` COMPILES and silently means `$.input.id`. Templates (`interpolatePayload`): `{{input}}` alone is the whole payload, but `{{a.b.c}}` is a dotted path, so `{{input.id}}` looks for a payload field literally called `input`. Both failure modes are silent nulls, and neither validation nor the capability walk catches them because the expression is syntactically fine. Guard added in `engine/test/connectors-builtin.e2e.mts` (no `\binput\.` anywhere in a step). Transform detail worth knowing: `projectOne` binds `item` per element, and when the source is NOT an array `item` is the whole payload - so `item.x` is correct in both record and array mode, which makes it the safest form to write.
- 2026-08-12 - Paginated `http-request` output shape: `selectResult(data, loop.result(), payload)` where `loop.result()` for a paginated request is the COLLECTED ITEMS ARRAY (not the last response body), so `resultKey: 'products'` yields `{products: [...all items...]}` merged into the incoming payload. Non-paginated, `loop.result()` is the parsed body, so `resultPath` + `resultKey` is how you pull a nested array out. Downstream `itemsPath` must match the `resultKey` you chose.
- 2026-08-12 - `docs/examples/dummyjson-products.connector.json` is a runnable manual-test connector: dummyjson.com, no auth, offset pagination (`skip`/`limit`, itemsPath `products`), a lookup table, a transform and an aggregate. Verified against the LIVE api (field names and `availabilityStatus` values) - worth re-checking if a manual test ever fails on mapping.
- 2026-08-12 - `.phorma-panel-icon-btn` is defined as `.phorma-panel-icon-btn.p-button`, so it does NOTHING on a non-pButton element. For a `<label>` wrapping a hidden file input, copy the skills panel's `__import-btn` rule instead (1.5rem square, 0.4rem radius, 6%/14% text-colour wash).
- 2026-08-12 - Adding a second family of `.phorma-palette__subheading` broke `agents-palette.spec.ts`, which asserted the exact list equalled the three MCP transport groups. Connector sub-headings now carry a `--connector` modifier and the spec scopes its query with `:not(...)`. When adding a new sub-group family to a shared container, give it a modifier class in the same change or an unrelated spec fails for the right reason and the wrong test.
- 2026-08-12 - Install verification worth repeating: `ConnectorsService` install is covered by a KARMA spec (`connectors.service.spec.ts`) hitting the REAL IndexedDB in headless Chrome, which is the only cheap way to prove a DB version bump plus a cross-service write actually works. Run the frontend suite with `npx ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless` (144 -> 152 tests with this feature).
- 2026-08-12 - Drive-by fix: `skills-panel.exportSkill` revoked its blob URL in the same tick as `click()`, the exact bug the `frontend-ui` steering warns about. Now deferred with `setTimeout(..., 0)` like every other download path.
- 2026-08-12 - BOTTOM-PINNED EXPANDER is now a three-panel pattern: runs History, workflows Templates, connections Connectors. Recipe: outer panel `display:flex; flex-direction:column; height:100%; overflow-y:auto`; the primary section `flex:1; min-height:0`; the expander `flex-shrink:0; margin-top:auto; max-height:50%; min-height:0` with a `--collapsed` modifier setting `max-height:none`, and its list `overflow-y:auto; min-height:0`. The 50% cap is what keeps the primary list visible however much is in the expander. GOTCHA: the Templates header is a single full-width `<button>`, which only works because it has no actions - an expander header that ALSO carries buttons (Connectors has install + package) must be a flex ROW with the collapse button and the actions as SIBLINGS, since a button inside a button is invalid HTML and breaks keyboard nav. Pinned by `connections-panel.spec.ts`, which also covers the two states that break stacked layouts: zero rows (empty state must not eat the expander) and many rows.
- 2026-08-12 - A connector row shows WHICH connection it is bound to, and resolves a since-deleted binding to "Connection removed" rather than rendering a raw `conn-...` id - same rule the usage ledger follows for deleted nodes. A spec asserts no badge ever matches `/^conn-/`.
- 2026-08-12 - BESPOKE DIALOG LAYOUT: the card must NOT be the scroller. Every dialog here was `card { max-height: calc(100vh - 48px); overflow-y: auto }` with a body carrying `min-height: 0`, which makes the body a shrinkable flex item - so on a short viewport the body was squeezed while its content, `overflow: visible`, spilled OUT of the box and painted over the footer buttons (reported as "buttons overlapping the body"). Correct shape: `card { overflow: hidden }`, `header/footer { flex-shrink: 0 }`, `body { flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto }`. Bonus: the confirm/save action stops scrolling out of reach. Fixed in the connector install, connector package and connection editor dialogs; check any new one against this. TESTING NOTE: geometry cannot tell "spilled and painted over" from "scrolled out of view" - both give the same `getBoundingClientRect`. The assertion that actually catches the regression is `getComputedStyle(card).overflowY === 'hidden'` plus `...(body).overflowY === 'auto'`, verified by reintroducing the old CSS.
- 2026-08-12 - Header glyphs to the left of a dialog heading were REMOVED from every modal by request (confirm, cloud, credits, skill editor, version history, onboarding, expanded panel, both connector dialogs). `ExpandedPanelDialog` lost its required `icon` input, so its four hosts (usage, properties, prompt, evals dialogs) dropped the attribute too. Do not reintroduce them. Note the confirm dialog no longer has a red alert triangle for `tone: 'danger'` - the danger cue is the red confirm button alone.
- 2026-08-12 - A card that opens something on click must not ALSO carry an action button for the same thing: the connector row's plug icon was replaced by making the whole `app-panel-card` clickable, which is what the connections list already did.
- 2026-08-12 - Reconfirmed the hard way: do NOT script source edits with PowerShell `Get-Content`/`-Raw` + `.Replace()`. A `` `n `` in a double-quoted PS string did not match the file's line endings, the replace silently no-op'd, and it looked like the edit had been applied. Use the editing tools (or Node) for anything that must actually change.

## Agent Skills (EPIC 6, shipped 2026-07-21)

- 2026-07-21 - Skills are markdown-only fragments embedded BY VALUE in `AgentNodeData.skills` (both type twins). The engine renders them in `renderPrompt` between the interpolated prompt and the capabilities/hand-off sections, VERBATIM (no `{{input}}` interpolation - deliberate; skills are static guidance). Zero cloud/Rust changes needed because skills ride inside the graph.
- 2026-07-21 - Library-vs-embed freshness: `SkillsService.syncAttachedSkills(graph)` MUTATES a graph clone, refreshing embedded copies by id (library wins; skills deleted from the library keep their snapshot). Hooked at exactly 3 places: `RunControllerService.start` (on the run's graphSnapshot), `CloudService.materializeDefaults` (push), `WorkflowService.exportActiveSpec`. The node data on canvas keeps the stale copy until one of those runs - that's by design, don't "fix" it.
- 2026-07-21 - IndexedDB is now v6: global `skills` store (keyPath id, NO workflowKey/index - the library is cross-workflow). `SkillsService` warms the library in its constructor so `syncAttachedSkills` can run synchronously at run start.
- 2026-07-21 - SKILL.md interop (`core/skills.model.ts`): minimal hand-rolled frontmatter parser (name/description scalars only, no YAML dep), first-markdown-heading fallback name, `serializeSkillMd` quotes values containing YAML-special chars via JSON.stringify. Compatible with Anthropic-style SKILL.md files (verified round-trip in browser E2E).
- 2026-07-21 - Canvas skill badge: `RendererNode.skillCount/skillGlyph/skillFont` set in `graph-to-scene.ts` (resolveIcon('ti ti-books')); drawn in `drawNode` as an accent pill LEFT of the kind badge, and the title clip rect must shrink to `titleClipEnd` (the skill pill's x) or long titles overdraw the pill.
- 2026-07-21 - New default panel tabs merge into EXISTING users' persisted layouts automatically (`loadTabs` maps over DEFAULT_TABS) - registering `{id:'skills', side:'left', order:2}` needed no migration.
- 2026-07-21 - `ConfirmDialogService.confirm` takes `tone: 'danger'`, NOT `destructive: true`.
- 2026-07-21 - Skill count pill deliberately reuses the kind-badge geometry (bh=13, radius 4, 8px Nunito) so the header reads as one badge family.

## Evals (EPIC 4)

- 2026-07-19 - EVALS shipped: `engine/src/evals.ts` owns suite/case/result types + pure `scoreOutput` (exact/contains/llm-judge; judge failures REJECT so callers record `error` status, never a silent pass/fail; `parseJudgeVerdict` walks balanced braces to survive prose/fences around JSON). `RunSource` now includes `'eval'`. E2E: `engine/test/evals.e2e.mts`.
- 2026-07-28 - EVAL STATS: all derived eval analytics live in the pure `engine/src/evals-stats.ts` (`modelAggregates`, `caseAggregates`, `suiteTrend`, `caseFlakiness`, `percentile`, `suiteDurationMs`, `suiteCostUsd`, `DEFAULT_PASS_LABEL` for the implicit no-override pass). Add new aggregations THERE, not in the component - they need zero Angular and are trivially testable (`engine/test/evals-stats.e2e.mts`, 68 checks). Semantics worth knowing: a case counts as passed for a run only when EVERY model pass passed it; `instability = 2 * min(p, 1-p)` so ranking by it surfaces genuinely flaky cases above consistently broken ones. `EvalService.runs` already holds the full 50-run history for the selected suite, so trends needed no service change.
- 2026-07-28 - PROMPT LIBRARY: global (cross-workflow) reusable agent prompts. `core/prompt-library.model.ts` + `core/prompt-library.service.ts` over a new IndexedDB `prompts` store (DB v8, keyPath `id`, no index - same shape as `skills`). Built-in entries are DERIVED from the `NODE_CATALOG` agent presets at read time and never persisted, so the catalog stays the single source of truth; editing one forks it into a user entry. Catalog `keywords` go on `PromptEntry.keywords` (searchable) NOT `tags` (user-facing chips) - putting them in `tags` flooded the filter with 22 chips nobody chose. Unlike skills, applying a prompt COPIES the markdown into `AgentNodeData.prompt` rather than embedding by reference, so later library edits never mutate a workflow behind the user's back. Interchange format is PROMPT.md (same minimal frontmatter parser as SKILL.md).
- 2026-07-28 - USAGE ANALYTICS widened: `UsagePeriod` gained `'1y' | 'all'` (`all` = since 0; the ledger prunes at 366d anyway) and `refresh()` now fetches `min(selectedPeriod, 90d)` from the cloud instead of a hard-pinned 90d. New facet filter signals `sources`/`statuses`/`environments` (empty set = no filter, `toggleFacet`/`clearFacets`) plus computeds `byNode`, `bySource`, `byStatus`, `byEnvironment`, `dailyByModel`, `durations`, `failedSpend`, `successRate`, `perRunAverage`, `creditsPerUsd`. `scopedEntries` (pre-facet) backs the filter chips so toggling one never hides the chip that would undo it. All of this was already recorded on every `UsageLedgerEntry` - nothing new is collected. The credits-vs-USD rule is unchanged: cloud share â†’ credits rounded ONCE in the final projection, BYO share â†’ USD with `*`/"(est.)" when estimated.
- 2026-07-19 - Eval runner architecture: `EvalRunnerService` bypasses the single-run `RunControllerService` and calls engine `startRun` directly per case (own `createRunRecorder`, pool of 3 locally). Case runs land in normal run history via `RunHistoryService.saveExternalRecord(record)` (added for recorders created outside the service). Unattended-run policy: `requestApproval: async () => true`, `waitForEvent` rejects immediately.
- 2026-07-19 - Cloud eval runs: DO `POST /trigger` accepts optional `source` (whitelisted to `'eval'`, else `'manual'`); new `CloudService.triggerHttp(workflowId, input, source?)` (the WS `triggerRemote` needs a connected monitor - HTTP path doesn't). No await-completion endpoint on the DO: poll `GET /runs` until the summary settles. Sequential only - DO 409s concurrent triggers.
- 2026-07-19 - Model comparison passes override `RunOptions.defaultModel` only (agents pinning provider/model unaffected). Deliberately local-only: cloud specs are materialized at push time (`materializeDefaults`), so defaultModel has no effect there.
- 2026-07-19 - IndexedDB is now v4: `eval-suites` (by-workflow) + `eval-runs` (by-suite, by-workflow) stores; same `workflowKey: id ?? 'draft'` null-key workaround. Deleting a suite deletes its eval runs.

## Published Endpoints / Portal (EPIC 9, shipped 2026-07-27)

- 2026-07-27 - Durable Object routes MUST drain the request body before responding. Returning a response while the request stream is unread throws `Can't read from request stream after response has been sent` and WEDGES the caller's NEXT request on that connection (symptom: an unrelated later GET hung for 354s). Any new DO route that ignores its body needs `await request.text().catch(() => "")`. In `portal.ts` the body is read ONCE at dispatch, before auth/rate-limit guards can return early.
- 2026-07-27 - `this.name` THROWS on a Durable Object reached by RPC. `partyserver` only assigns it for requests routed through `routePartykitRequest` (`dist/index.js` `get name()` throws a long "before it was set" error). Anything reachable via a stub method must carry its identity in state instead - portal sessions store `workflowId` + `ownerInstance`. The throw was swallowed by a best-effort catch, so the only symptom was silently-missing mirrored runs.
- 2026-07-27 - Table creation in `onStart()` is NOT enough: an RPC entry point can reach `trigger()` before `onStart` completes (`no such table: run_journal`). Extracted `ensureTables()` and call it from both.
- 2026-07-27 - `cloud/src/portal-page.ts` holds the whole portal page in TEMPLATE LITERALS (`STYLES`, `SCRIPT`). A single backtick in a CSS/JS comment ends the literal and breaks the worker build - and `wrangler dev` then HANGS on every request rather than reporting it clearly. Never write backticks inside those blocks. An inlined string was chosen over a wrangler `assets` binding because `wrangler.jsonc` is committed and shared by both deploy targets.
- 2026-07-27 - Public event redaction (`cloud/src/portal-events.ts`) is an ALLOW-LIST, not a filter: `toPortalEvent` maps 8 shapes and copies named fields only, so a new `RunEvent` variant fails CLOSED. Tokens stream ONLY from the resolved responder node; sub-workflow interiors are dropped wholesale (a nested frame can reuse the responder's node id, so the id check is untrustworthy inside a frame); every failure collapses to `PORTAL_GENERIC_ERROR`. A public WebSocket is NOT an option - the `agents` SDK sends the full `WorkflowSpec` + `ownerId` on connect and lets any client overwrite state.
- 2026-07-27 - Never assert redaction by asking a model to echo a marker: a 3B model will recite its own prompt, answer `FINAL-ANSWER-NOT-FOUND`, or refuse outright, and a model reciting its prompt is a prompt-engineering issue, NOT a transport leak. Two-layer approach: `cloud/test/portal-projection.test.mjs` drives every `RunEvent` variant through the pure projection (authoritative, deterministic), while the live E2E asserts only what the transport controls - absent metadata fields, whitelisted event types, and provenance by checking the streamed tokens reconstruct EXACTLY `run-completed.output`.
- 2026-07-27 - Per-visitor session instances (`{workflowId}#s{sessionId}`, `portalSessionInstance()`) are how the single-run 409 limit is dodged; `#s` never appears in studio-generated names. Consequences that MUST be handled: session DOs never arm cron (`rescheduleCron` returns early when `portalSession` is set), and settled runs are mirrored to the owner instance via `acceptPortalRun` or the Runs/Usage panels never see portal traffic.
- 2026-07-27 - `PortalIndex` is a PLAIN `DurableObject`, deliberately not an `Agent` (whose state broadcast would publish the slug table). It owns slug resolution in BOTH modes so a BYO user needs no KV/D1 binding - one `wrangler deploy` and publishing works.
- 2026-07-27 - Multi-turn chat needed ZERO engine changes: the transcript lives in the session DO and is serialized into the single `input: string` as a JSON envelope, which `interpolatePayload` already resolves as `{{message}}` / `{{history}}` / `{{fields.x}}` / `{{sessionId}}`. Prompts written against `{{input}}` will show the model raw JSON - document the tokens instead.
- 2026-07-27 - FIXED latent bug: `rescheduleCron` cancelled ALL schedules, including in-flight `waitTimedOut` / `workflowTimedOut` alarms, so a spec push during a suspended run silently dropped its timeouts. Now filters on `callback === 'scheduledRun'`.
- 2026-07-27 - Bundle budget technique: `cronstrue` (~48kB CommonJS, used only when a Schedule trigger is selected) was eagerly imported. Converting it to a lazy `import()` behind an `effect()` + a `cronDescriberReady` signal freed 22kB AND removed the CommonJS optimization-bailout warning (`allowedCommonJsDependencies: ["cronstrue"]` in angular.json silences the rest). That single change paid for the entire EPIC 9 frontend. When the `initial` budget is over, look for eager CommonJS deps behind rarely-selected UI before raising the budget.
- 2026-07-27 - Portal page alignment: ONE `--gutter` CSS variable drives the heading padding, log padding, composer margin and card margins. Hand-tuning them drifted by 2-4px at different breakpoints. Verify alignment by measuring the heading's TEXT range (a block `<h1>` box spans the full width and lies): `range.selectNodeContents(h1).getBoundingClientRect().left` vs the composer's border edge. Bottom-anchor a chat log with `.log::before{content:'';margin-top:auto}` - `justify-content:flex-end` clips the top of an overflowing log in Chromium.
- 2026-07-27 - Publish-flow UX trap: the worker legitimately reports "push this workflow first" before the first push, but surfacing that as a publish ERROR disables the very button that pushes. `PortalService.validation` keeps LOCAL graph validation authoritative and merges in only codes the studio cannot know (`REMOTE_ONLY_CODES` = `slug-taken`).

## BYO Deploy Config / Embed Widget (EPIC 9 follow-ups, shipped 2026-07-27)

- 2026-07-27 - PRODUCT RULE: **Phorma Cloud users get white-glove treatment, BYO users get the knobs.** Anything infrastructural (account IDs, worker names, wrangler, deploy config, "your worker is out of date") must be hidden when `cloudProvider() === 'phorma'` - we deploy their runtime, so it is both irrelevant and alarming. Verified by asserting the Phorma Cloud tab's text contains none of `wrangler`/`Account ID`/`Worker name`/`git pull`.
- 2026-07-27 - `cloud/wrangler.jsonc` is the file BYO users deploy, so its DEFAULT env must contain nothing Phorma-owned. It previously pinned our `account_id` AND bound our `phorma-releases` R2 bucket, so every BYO `wrangler deploy` targeted our account and failed. Phorma-specific bindings live in `env.hosted`. `cloud/test/deploy-config.test.mjs` fails if that regresses.
- 2026-07-27 - Corollary: a new Durable Object needs its migration added to BOTH `cloud/wrangler.jsonc` and `DeployConfigService.DO_MIGRATIONS`. Ours keeps working while BYO breaks, so the drift test compares the two lists directly.
- 2026-07-27 - BYO overrides are written to a GITIGNORED `cloud/wrangler.byo.jsonc` and passed via `--config`, never by editing the committed file (which would conflict on `git pull`). `run_streamed_command`'s `args: Vec<String>` is unvalidated, so adding `--config` needed no Rust change.
- 2026-07-27 - `scripts/release.mjs --dry-run` was WRITING every file and only skipping the git steps. It silently rewrote `cloud/package.json` to a test version during verification. Any `--dry-run` must `continue` BEFORE the write, not before the commit.
- 2026-07-27 - `frame-ancestors` does NOT fall back to `default-src`; when absent, browsers allow ANY site to frame the page. Portals were therefore clickjackable. It is now set explicitly on every portal response and defaults to `'none'`. Hardening change - non-embedded portals can no longer be framed at all.
- 2026-07-27 - Two CSP-injection bugs found by writing the tests: `.filter(Boolean)` passes a whitespace-only origin (`'  '`) straight into the directive - use `.map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)`; and `new URL('https://*')` SUCCEEDS with hostname `*`, so a bare `*` became the meaningless token `https://*`. `normalizeEmbedOrigin` now shape-checks the hostname.
- 2026-07-27 - An embedded widget must NOT use `theme: auto`. `auto` follows the VISITOR's OS, so a dark-mode visitor sees a dark panel on a light host site. The loader defaults to `light` and forwards `?theme=` to the page. Found ONLY by looking at a screenshot - the DOM and tests were all "correct".
- 2026-07-27 - Cache the embed loader for MINUTES, not hours. At `max-age=3600` a worker fix appears not to work at all in the browser while `curl` shows the new file. Confirm the served bytes with `curl` before debugging the code.
- 2026-07-27 - `cloud/src/portal-embed.ts` has the same no-backticks rule as `portal-page.ts` (it is a `String.raw` template). Both are asserted by `cloud/test/portal-embed.test.mjs`.
- 2026-07-27 - `cloud`'s `npm test` invoked `tsx` without it being a dependency; it only ever worked because agents ran `npx -y tsx`. Scripts must not depend on tools the package does not declare. Now `test` = `test:unit` (3 pure suites) + `test:portal` (114 live checks).

## UI Regressions Worth Remembering

- 2026-09-14 - `settings-dialog.scss` compiles to ~21.8kB against a 22kB `anyComponentStyle` warning, so a NEW section on a settings page must be its own component with its own stylesheet - which then gets Angular's scoping and cannot see the surrounding `.phorma-settings__*` recipes. Three such sections now share `workspace/settings/_section.scss`: `@use '../section' as settings-section; @include settings-section.base;` emits `.settings-section__{head,heading,desc,note,row,name,meta,badge,actions,btn,...}` once per sheet, which is safe precisely BECAUSE the scoping keeps the copies apart. Two other things any such component owes: a per-instance id scope from a static counter (`settings-dialog.aws.spec.ts` mounts TWO dialogs and asserts no id in the document repeats), and an entry in that spec's `SIBLING_SECTIONS` selector so its chrome counts do not start tracking your section.
- 2026-09-14 - Karma runs REAL Chrome with `src/styles.scss` loaded (`angular.json` test options), so layout probes in a component spec measure actual layout and are far cheaper than a browser session: `getBoundingClientRect().height` vs `scrollHeight` for a collapsed flex child, `actionsRect.right <= rowRect.right` for a row whose growing child needs `min-width: 0`, `getComputedStyle(el).fontSize` for a font floor (never rem arithmetic - root is 14px), and `querySelectorAll('[id]')` total vs unique count for id collisions.
- 2026-07-27 - `display: flex` on a paragraph makes every text run and inline `<code>` its own flex item, so a sentence wraps into a row of disconnected boxes. Never flex a container holding PROSE - float the leading icon instead. Same block: `word-break: break-all` on inline `<code>` split `cloud/wrangler.byo.jsonc` into "wrangler.byo. jsonc", which reads as a typo. Use `overflow-wrap: break-word`.

- 2026-07-27 - Settings row prose (`__hint`, `__row-error`, `__row-note`) is a SIBLING of `.phorma-settings__row`, so it needs the label column added by hand to line up with the control. - 2026-07-27 - A 1px red border alone does not read as "invalid" on a dark theme; `.phorma-settings__input--invalid` also needs a `box-shadow` ring.
- 2026-07-27 - PrimeNG v20 `p-contextmenu` renders NOTHING without an explicit `[target]` - its document-level contextmenu listener is only bound via the target path (a target-less menu never opens, no error). If the target element lives inside `@if`, bind it through a `viewChild` signal + computed (`[target]="targetSignal()"`), not a template ref variable (ref vars are undefined at binding time). Also add `appendTo="body"` or the menu is clipped/mispositioned inside overflow-hidden sidebars.

## Agent Context / Kiro Steering

- 2026-07-31 - Kiro now loads `.kiro/steering/`. Always-on: `product` (inlines `agent.md` via `#[[file:agent.md]]`), `tech`, `structure`, `conventions`, `workflow`, `skills`. Auto-inclusion (loaded when the request matches the front-matter `description`): `agent-memory` (inlines THIS file), `testing` (inlines `docs/e2e-testing.md`), `release`. fileMatch: `frontend-ui`, `engine`, `desktop-rust`, `cloud-worker`. Front matter must be the very first content in the file; `fileMatchPattern` accepts an array; `#[[file:...]]` paths are WORKSPACE-ROOT relative and inline the live file, which is why product/memory/testing never drift.
- 2026-07-31 - Durable RULES belong in the matching `.kiro/steering/` file (always loaded); war stories and dated findings belong here. `.github/copilot-instructions.md` is now a thin pointer to the steering set plus Copilot-only tool notes - do not re-duplicate conventions into it, or the two copies diverge.
- 2026-07-31 - Kiro auto-loads a root `AGENTS.md`, but this repo's product doc is `agent.md` (lowercase, referenced by README + copilot-instructions), so it is pulled in through the `product` steering wrapper instead of being renamed.
- 2026-07-31 - Skill packs in `.agents/skills/` and `.github/skills/` are NOT auto-loaded by Kiro. `.kiro/steering/skills.md` is the index that tells an agent which pack to read for a task; add new packs there or they stay invisible.
- 2026-08-10 - Playwright is NOT installed in this repo despite `docs/e2e-testing.md` being written against its API. `scripts/cdp.mjs` is a zero-dependency Chrome DevTools Protocol driver for browser checks (Node 24 global `WebSocket`, system Chrome at `C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe`): `node scripts/cdp.mjs http://localhost:7322 <snippets.mjs>`, snippet file default-exports `async (evaluate) => any` steps. Two gotchas found writing it: ESM has no `require`, and Chrome can still hold the temp profile directory when you `rmSync` it, so wrap the cleanup or an EPERM masks the actual result.
- 2026-08-10 - Duplicate-id baseline for browser checks: PrimeNG 20's menubar renders NINE `p-menubar-submenu` `<ul>` elements with a literal `id="null"`. Third-party markup, present on a bare page load, NOT a regression in our panels. `document.querySelectorAll('[id]')` total-vs-unique will therefore never be equal - filter to ids you own.

It is now gated on keychain OR a configured deploy target, with the local save button disabled and titled "This host has no local secret store". Verified in a real browser: a bearer connection typed with `apiKey` in the auth field alone renders exactly one declared `apiKey` secret row, and the cloud upload button enables the moment a value is typed.

## AWS Deployment Target (cloud-aws, in flight)

- 2026-08-14 - A CDK Aspect that is exported but never registered is dead code, and nothing in a
  normal test run notices. All six guardrails in `cloud-aws/src/infra/aspects.ts` sat unwired while
  `template.spec.ts` carried six `it.todo` stubs admitting it. Wiring them into
  `PhormaAwsHostStack` immediately surfaced a real bug: `MonitorApi`'s integration role was created
  without the permissions boundary, which an organisation that mandates the boundary would have
  rejected at deploy time. Register Aspects in the stack constructor, after every construct and
  after `Tags.of`.
- 2026-08-14 - `it.todo` is a silent backlog. `vitest --run` reports "6 todo" alongside a green
  summary, so a checkpoint task reads as passing. Treat any `todo` in a spec as an unfinished task,
  not a passing one.
- 2026-08-14 - vitest does not type-check, so a spec file can compile-fail while its tests pass.
  `cloud-aws` had 6 `error TS` in two spec files (invented `RunSource` `'api'`, `PortRole`
  `'tool-in'`/`'tool-out'`, and `WorkflowConnection.sourceNodeId`) while `npm test` was green. The
  real shapes: `RunSource` is manual/schedule/webhook/resume/eval/portal, a tool port role is
  `'tools'`, and a connection is `{id, outputId, inputId, kind}` where the connector id is the port
  base id plus `-in`/`-out`. Import the engine type instead of hand-copying a union.
- 2026-08-14 - `as any` in a `.e2e.mts` scenario script hides shape drift until runtime.
  `purge.e2e.mts` built a flat run record and crashed in `RunTableAdapter.upsert`, which reads
  `record.summary.startedAt`. `RunRecord` is `{summary, graph, events}`. Type the fixture as
  `RunRecord` rather than casting at the call site.

  `tool-mcp`, the `WorkflowNodeKind` is `mcp-tool`. `addNodeFromCatalog('mcp-tool')` returns null
  and every downstream assertion fails on a null node.
- 2026-08-14 - A shared assertion helper that only loops over findings asserts nothing when the
  graph is clean. Karma reports it as "has no expectations" - worth grepping for, it marks a
  vacuous test. Add the emptiness correspondence explicitly.
- 2026-08-15 - `cloud-aws` now pins every dependency and devDependency exactly, enforced by
  `scripts/check-versions.mjs` (local `file:`/`link:`/`workspace:` specs are exempt - they carry no
  registry version). Adding a dependency with `^` or `~` fails `npm run check`. `tsx` is a runtime
  dependency, not a devDependency: the CLI launcher spawns it. Pinning the AWS SDK at `3.1110.0`
  emits one `npm warn ERESOLVE` - `@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb@3.1110.0` pulls

  It is a warning only; npm nests the resolution and install succeeds. Bumping all twelve

- 2026-08-15 - `cloud-aws/src/aws/table-ops-compile.ts` is the only place a `core/table-ops.ts`
  write shape becomes an SDK command input. Two non-obvious rules keep it sound against the pure
  evaluator: a `path` names ONE top-level attribute and is never split on `.` or `[n]` (the pure
  evaluator reads `item[path]`, so splitting would disagree for an attribute literally named
  `a.b`), and an empty `and`/`or` child list has to compile to an existence identity
  (`attribute_exists(#p) OR attribute_not_exists(#p)` / the `AND` form) because DynamoDB has no
  empty-conjunction syntax while `every`/`some` over nothing are true/false. DynamoDB `ADD` takes a
  value operand only, so the compiler throws on a non-literal `AddAction` instead of mistranslating
  it.

  `tsc --noEmit`. Do not add `@types/node` for one stream: read it through
  `(globalThis as { process?: { stdout?: Sink } }).process?.stdout` inside the factory and declare
  the one member you use locally (`stdout-log-writer.ts` does this). Same rule keeps the lookup out
  of module load, which the credential-free Check_Pipeline requires of every `src/aws/` module.

- 2026-08-16 - Two things about the Sentinel_Envelope that a gap-detection test has to encode. (1) The
  wire format has NO terminator line, so the expected set is `0..max(seq)` and deleting the HIGHEST
  sequence lowers `max` instead of punching a hole: it decodes ok with a truncated payload, and only
  deleting the sole sentinel line produces the no-envelope error (which carries no `missingSeq`).
  Asserting "one line removed always fails" is wrong at every size. (2) A single-hole mutation cannot
  distinguish a lowest-first gap scan from a highest-first one - both name the same sequence. To catch
  that bug the enumeration needs a TWO-hole case: re-tagging sequence k as `max+2` leaves holes at k
  and at the old `max`, and only a lowest-first scan answers k. `frontend/src/app/core/deploy/sentinel-envelope.spec.ts`
  covers 1332 such cases by exhaustive enumeration (size x arrival order x noise x content, then every
  single mutation); `fast-check` is an `engine` dependency only and must not be added to `frontend`.

  (`fetch-bearer` for both Cloudflare targets, `aws-cli` for `aws`). Adding a host is a route table;
  adding a credential model is a transport. Rules the conversion had to hold, all easy to break:
  a transport THROWS on a transport failure and on an unparseable body, because that is what `fetch`
  and `Response.json()` did at the eleven call sites and every existing `catch` depends on it; an
  HTTP status is never a failure kind (`AwsRequestService` reports a 409 as `ok: true`); a declared
  `body` reshaper is also the marker for "this endpoint sends a body", so the read routes send none;
  and an absent operation returns `{ ok: 'unsupported' }`, which the caller resolves to that
  operation's documented absent value (`deployedStatus` stays `null` = unknown, `connectionSecretNames()`
  returns `[]`) - never to a fabricated route.

  `arn:aws:scheduler:::aws-sdk:{service}:{operation}`, and an `execute-api` ARN is a valid target for
  an EventBridge RULE, a different service. `CreateSchedule` is therefore rejected at SPEC-PUSH time
  (`SchedulerAdapter.sync` runs from `handleSpecPush`), so any workflow with a `schedule-trigger` node
  carrying a non-blank cron cannot be deployed to the AWS host at all. Operator-visible symptom:
  `POST /workflows/{id}/spec` answers 500 `{"error":"Internal error"}` and the Studio toasts
  `Push failed` / `Internal error`; the real cause is only in the handler-error log line. The spec is
  written BEFORE the sync, so the spec persists while the schedule set does not. Two more holes from
  the same root: the schedule `Input` carries `{workflowId,nodeId,source}` with no `runId` and the
  trigger route 400s without one, and `SchedulerAdapter.handleScheduleFire` has no live caller so the
  skipped-scheduled-run metric can never be published.
  **FIXED 2026-08-17 - this entry is kept for the diagnosis only, and its "workaround today" and
  "deferred to a follow-up spec" are obsolete.** The target is now the Schedule_Shim Lambda, the shim
  mints the `runId`, and the trigger route calls `handleScheduleFire`. There were also two further
  defects this entry did not catch: the cron dialect translation was inverted against AWS, and
  schedule names were unscoped so a push wiped other workflows. See the 2026-08-17 entries at the end
  of this section.
- 2026-08-16 - `check-docs.mjs` extracts several guide sections with regexes whose terminator is
  `(?=\n##\s*\d)`, which does NOT match a `### N.M` subheading (`\s*` matches zero chars and `#` is
  not `\d`), so numbered subsections can be added inside sections 7, 9 and 3 without truncating the
  extracted body. The Verify extraction is `##\s*\d*\.?\s*Verify` with no `^` anchor and takes the
  FIRST match, so a `### Verify ...` subheading placed before `## 7. Verify` would hijack it - name
  subheadings anything else. Renumbering top-level sections 1-3 is what breaks the guard, because
  every `PREREQUISITE_DOCS_ITEMS` citation and `DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE` points at 3.4/3.5/3.6/3.8.
- 2026-08-16 - `AwsCliService.runCommand` reported NOTHING on a non-zero exit, so requirement 5.7's
  `aws sso login` message was unreachable: `doctor` reaches the CLI only through `runCommand`, and
  only `planAndDeploy` called `reportExitFailure`. Found while writing task 15.2's examples and fixed
  there (report when `!success && exitCode !== null` - a `null` exit code means the invocation itself
  failed and `executeStreamedCommand` has already toasted, so reporting again double-toasts one
  failure). The summary names the verb off `command.args[1]`, giving "Doctor failed" / "Plan failed".
  Lesson for the class: a private helper whose docstring names a verb no caller passes it is a
  wiring gap, not a style detail.
- 2026-08-16 - The negative half of a "written BEFORE the CLI ran" ordering assertion cannot be a
  fixed number of task turns. `CloudDialog.runAwsPlanAndDeploy` reaches `planAndDeploy` through two
  MACROTASKS (the `@tauri-apps/api/core` dynamic import in the cdk-entry probe, and the IndexedDB
  read in the egress derivation), so a mutation that starts the config write without awaiting it
  hides behind them and passes three microtask turns. Gate the write on a promise the spec releases
  by hand and give the deploy path a real-time budget (`happensWithin(pred, 750)`) instead: a correct
  implementation can never reach `planAndDeploy` while the write is pending however long you wait, so
  the budget only bounds how much of a wrong implementation's head start is observed - there is no
  flake in either direction. Same fix needed for "a disabled control reached nothing".

- 2026-08-17 - **EventBridge Scheduler has NO API Gateway target**, templated or universal. Its
  templated list is closed (CodeBuild, CodePipeline, ECS `RunTask`, EventBridge `PutEvents`,
  Inspector, Kinesis, Firehose, Lambda `Invoke`, SageMaker, SNS, SQS, Step Functions) and the
  universal target invokes AWS SDK operations of the shape
  `arn:aws:scheduler:::aws-sdk:{service}:{operation}`. An `execute-api` ARN with `*` path
  placeholders IS a valid target for an EventBridge **rule**, which is a different service - that
  ARN shape is Rules semantics wired into Scheduler, and it is why `CreateSchedule` failed and took
  every cron-carrying spec push down with it. Fixed by a Lambda hop: `src/shim/schedule-shim.ts`,
  `{prefix}-schedule-shim`, invoked by Scheduler and making the signed
  `POST /workflows/{id}/trigger` itself. Do not "fix" this by pointing a target at a route again; a
  `template.spec.ts` assertion now fails if `PHORMA_SCHEDULE_TARGET_ARN` ever contains
  `execute-api`.
- 2026-08-17 - The Lambda shim was chosen over draining an SQS queue in the Fargate task, and the
  reason is not cost. A queue drain would have been a SECOND ingress into a run, so the lease
  acquire, the 409 contention answer and the unfenced skip record would each have had a second
  implementation site inside `server/` - the most invariant-dense layer here. The shim reuses the
  existing trigger route, so a scheduled run is byte-identical to a manual one and `server/` needed
  no new code path. It is also cheaper: the shim runs OUTSIDE the VPC against the public
  IAM-guarded `execute-api` endpoint, where a queue would have needed an eleventh interface endpoint
  (~15 USD/month across two AZs) purely so the task could poll. The closed "no Lambda" decision in
  the spec was about the WebSocket routes, a hot bidirectional path; it does not transfer to a cold
  fire-and-forget trigger, and Lambda's 15-minute ceiling is irrelevant because the run happens on
  Fargate.
- 2026-08-17 - **AWS cron is not Unix cron, and the old code had it backwards in both directions.**
  Three differences: six fields with a trailing year, day-of-week `1-7` from Sunday (Unix is `0-6`
  with `7` also Sunday, so AWS is `(unix % 7) + 1`), and `*` may not appear in BOTH day fields -
  exactly one of day-of-month and day-of-week must carry `?`. So the old
  "append a year wildcard" turned the single most common expression a user can type, `0 12 * * *`,
  into `cron(0 12 * * * *)`, which AWS rejects. Meanwhile the old validator ran `parseInt('?')`, got
  `NaN` and returned false, so an operator who worked out the AWS dialect themselves was refused
  locally; and it allowed day-of-week `0`, which AWS refuses. The accepted set and the deployable set
  were nearly disjoint. `core/cron.ts translateCron` now owns validation AND translation as ONE pass
  (they are the same question), and `scheduler-backend.ts scheduleExpression` only adds the
  `cron(...)` wrapper. `L`, `W` and `#` day-of-week fields pass through unremapped, since none is
  Unix syntax and remapping `6L` would silently move the schedule by a day.
- 2026-08-17 - A latent data-loss bug found while fixing cron, unrelated to it: the IaC creates ONE
  schedule group per DEPLOYMENT (`{prefix}-schedules`), but `scheduleName` was a single opaque
  58-hex-char digest with no recoverable workflow id, so `deleteAllForWorkflow` listed the WHOLE
  group and deleted every entry. A spec push for workflow B therefore deleted workflow A's
  schedules, unrecoverably - the rollback path only undoes creates from the failing push. The
  in-code comment hand-waved it ("the schedule group is scoped to one workflow in this adapter"),
  which the IaC contradicts. Fixed by making names two-segment
  (`sched-{16 hex of workflow}-{40 hex of node}`, 63 chars inside the 64 limit) with a
  `schedulePrefix(workflowId)` export, and making `namePrefix` a REQUIRED parameter of
  `SchedulerBackend.listSchedules` so an unscoped list is unrepresentable. `FakeSchedulerBackend`
  honours the prefix deliberately: a fake that ignored it would accept the bug again.
- 2026-08-17 - This bug class survived a green suite because the FAKE was more permissive than AWS.
  `generators.ts` labelled plain five-field Unix expressions as "valid cron", and Property 17 checked
  them against a 40-line COPY of the old Unix validator pasted into the spec, so the test and the
  code agreed on a classification AWS rejects. The engine steering already warns never to mirror a
  production table into a spec as an oracle; the same applies to a validator. Property 17 now calls
  `translateCron` directly and asserts the STORED expression equals the translated form, not the
  operator input.
- 2026-08-17 - The orphan-schedule path (`ScheduleStore.handleScheduleFire`) had no caller at all, so
  the `FailedScheduledRun`/`skipped-scheduled-run` alarm could never fire. It is now called from the
  trigger route, but AFTER the lease acquire, never before: Property 6
  (`runner-lease-ordering.spec.ts`) requires the lease conditional write to be the FIRST Run_Table
  operation of every trigger "with no preceding read", and a spec-presence check is a read. So the
  route takes the lease, checks, and on an absent spec deletes the schedule, publishes the metric,
  releases the lease and answers 404. The release is best-effort inside a `try` - a lease left held
  expires within `LEASE_TTL_MS` anyway, which beats failing the response and having Scheduler retry a
  workflow that cannot run.
- 2026-08-17 - The shim must NOT throw on 409 or 404. Throwing is the retry signal to Scheduler and
  the thing that raises the Lambda invocation-error metric, so throwing on 409 ("another Runner holds
  the lease") would page someone every time the concurrency guard did its job correctly, and throwing
  on 404 would retry a workflow whose schedule has already been deleted. Only 5xx, 4xx other than
  those two, and transport failures throw.
- 2026-08-17 - The Lambda asset is pre-built and consumed with `lambda.Code.fromAsset` on a plain
  directory, NOT with `NodejsFunction`. `NodejsFunction` bundles at synth time and falls back to
  **Docker** when local esbuild resolution fails, which would make the pipeline's no-Docker guarantee
  depend on what happens to be installed. The build runs BEFORE both `cdk synth` calls in `check` and
  the ordering is load bearing - with `dist/` removed, synth dies with
  `Â«CannotFindAssetÂ» Cannot find asset at ...\dist\schedule-shim`. `dist/` is gitignored and is in
  `IMAGE_CONTEXT_EXCLUDES`, `.dockerignore` and `check-deploy-bundle.mjs`'s `NOT_BUNDLED`, or the shim
  bundle would churn the container image fingerprint on every deploy. The bundle is ~957 kB because
  the AWS SDK and Smithy packages are bundled in rather than taken from the Lambda runtime - every
  other module here is pinned exactly, and signing with whatever version AWS happens to deploy would
  break that.
- 2026-08-17 - The shim builder had to move OUT of `scripts/` and into `src/shim/build.ts`, and
  `check-deploy-bundle.mjs` is what caught it. A BYO deploy runs from a workspace the installer
  unpacked, and `cloud-aws/scripts/` is in that guard's `NOT_BUNDLED` list ("check-pipeline guards,
  not part of a deploy") while `src/` ships - so a builder under `scripts/` could never run on a real
  operator machine and every cron deploy would have died at synth. `cli/plan.ts` and `cli/deploy.ts`
  now call `bundleShimForCdk` (`cli/shim-bundle.ts`) before any `cdk` step, which also means the
  bundle is rebuilt from the shipped source on every plan and deploy rather than being a stale
  artefact carried in the installer. Consequence: `esbuild` moved to `dependencies`, since
  devDependencies cannot be assumed in the workspace. `package.json` runs it as
  `"bundle:shim": "tsx src/shim/build.ts"` - `tsx` is already a runtime dependency and `cdk.json`
  already runs the CDK app through it, so this needed no new tooling. General lesson: before putting
  anything on the deploy path under `scripts/`, check `NOT_BUNDLED` - "it works in the repo" is not
  the same as "it works for an operator".

- 2026-08-17 - A `*/` sequence inside a block comment ENDS the comment. Writing `` `*/5 * * * *` ``
  in a JSDoc block in `generators.ts` produced a `[PARSE_ERROR] Unexpected token` from oxc pointing
  at the comment line, which reads like a syntax error in the code below it. Cron expressions with

- 2026-08-17 - vitest's `expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(predicate)` does NOT accept a predicate
  function - it throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'constructor')`, which looks
  like a bug in the code under test rather than in the assertion. To assert on a property of a
  rejection (message length, a field), capture it: `await p.then(() => undefined, e => e as Error)`
  and assert on the result.
